summary: Part II of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions, starting where that roadmap stops: the parent (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #1180) states symmetric power functoriality for modular and Hilbert modular forms and the theorems of Newton–Thorne and Clozel–Thorne on the way as endpoints and import contracts, and this roadmap plans their proofs. SP.0–SP.3 move automorphy of symmetric powers along eigenvarieties (Newton–Thorne I Part I: rigid pseudocharacter spaces, analytic continuation of functoriality between definite unitary eigenvarieties, Theorem 2.33 on the eigencurve, Buzzard–Kilford's boundary annuli and ping-pong for Theorem D). SP.4–SP.7 raise the level on definite unitary groups (Newton–Thorne I Part II and Clozel–Thorne III: endoscopic character identities, depth-zero and Iwahori-spherical types, trace-formula level raising to types, level raising to Steinberg by residually reducible deformation theory, Thorne's p-adic level raising, the CM seed σ_0 and Theorem E, Clozel–Thorne's Sym^{l+1}). SP.8 kills ramification with n-regular refinements. SP.9–SP.10 are Newton–Thorne II: automorphy lifting for Sym^{n−1} through the map P → R and the regularity of the pseudodeformation ring, and the induction on supercuspidal primes through seasoned representations. SP.11–SP.13 are Newton–Thorne 2026 with Thorne 2024 §7: the untwisted tensor r_π ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_σ by comparing deformation problems with congruent special fibres, functoriality lifting for tensor products, residual witnesses for the coefficient-Frobenius twisted tensor, and the Bertrand induction proving SP_n for all n. This is a completed target-level planning pass, with all stages planned rather than closed. G2 remains a conditional intermediate CM seed route; G1,G3–G5 and G7 record missing owners or supplier extensions. G6 is resolved by a perfect-group cyclotomic restriction argument and an explicit finite avoidance set. No endpoint is claimed implemented.

nodes.title: Analytic continuation along irreducible components of rigid spaces
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite extension of ℚ_p, α : 𝒳 → 𝒢 a closed immersion and β : 𝒴 → 𝒢 a morphism of rigid analytic spaces over E, and y ∈ 𝒴 with β(y) ∈ 𝒳. If β^{−1}(𝒳) contains an affinoid open neighbourhood of y, then β(𝒞) ⊂ 𝒳 for every irreducible component 𝒞 of 𝒴 containing y. Moreover, every irreducible component of 𝒴_{ℂ_p} lies in the base change of an irreducible component of 𝒴, and if 𝒴 is quasi-separated and has finitely many irreducible components, there is a finite extension E′/E such that the irreducible components of 𝒴_{E′} are geometrically irreducible (Conrad, Theorem 3.4.2).
hypotheses: 𝒴 and 𝒢 are rigid analytic spaces over a finite extension E of ℚ_p; 𝒳 → 𝒢 is a closed immersion.
The neighbourhood must be an affinoid open of 𝒴 containing y, not just a sequence of points accumulating at y.

For the base-change assertions use quasi-separated rigid spaces; finite extension making all components geometrically irreducible is asserted for a finite set of components, in particular an affinoid. For a selected component first restrict to that component as in NTI.
proofSteps: β^{−1}(𝒳) is a Zariski closed analytic subspace of 𝒴 (pullback of a closed immersion).

Let 𝒞 be an irreducible component through y and 𝒞̃ → 𝒞 its normalization, which is connected (irreducible components are images of connected components of the normalization, AdicSpacesPartIIPartII RZ.1).

The preimage of β^{−1}(𝒳) ∩ 𝒞 in 𝒞̃ is Zariski closed and contains a non-empty admissible open (the preimage of the affinoid neighbourhood meets 𝒞̃ in a set of full dimension at a point over y); by the irreducibility criterion of RZ.1 a proper Zariski closed subset of an irreducible space is nowhere dense, so it is all of 𝒞̃.

Conrad's Theorem 3.4.2 on irreducible components under base change of the ground field gives the second sentence; it is used to pass between components over E, over finite extensions and over ℂ_p in SP.1 and SP.2.
acceptance: Take 𝒴 = 𝒢 the closed unit disc and 𝒳 = {0}: β = id does not send an affinoid neighbourhood of 0 into 𝒳, and the conclusion fails, so the neighbourhood hypothesis is necessary.

Take 𝒢 = 𝒴 = two closed discs meeting at one point (the union of the axes in the bidisc) and 𝒳 one axis: the hypothesis holds at a point of that axis away from the crossing, and only that component is forced into 𝒳.

sources.match: States and proves the analytic continuation lemma for a closed immersion and a morphism of E-rigid spaces, using Conrad's irreducible components.

sources.locator: proof of Theorem 2.24, p. 41; Corollary 2.28 and footnote, pp. 43–44; proof of Theorem 2.33, pp. 50–51
sources.match: Applies Conrad's Theorem 3.4.2 to pass from components over E to components over ℂ_p.
Quasi-separated spaces have the stated component behavior under base extension; the simultaneous finite extension assertion requires finitely many components.

nodes.title: Rigid spaces of conjugate self-dual pseudocharacters and their absolutely irreducible loci
nodes.statement: Fix a CM field F with maximal totally real subfield F⁺, a finite set S of places of F⁺ containing the p-adic places, a residual conjugate self-dual pseudocharacter τ̄ of G_{F,S} of dimension n over a finite field k, and for each v ∈ S_p a place ṽ of F above v. Let R_ps (resp. R_{ps,v}) be the universal deformation ring of τ̄ as a conjugate self-dual pseudocharacter of G_{F,S} (resp. unrestricted pseudodeformations of τ̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}), a complete Noetherian local W(k)-algebra. Define 𝒳_ps and 𝒳_{ps,v} as their rigid generic fibres, with the restriction morphism 𝒳_ps → 𝒳_{ps,p} = ∏_{v∈S_p} 𝒳_{ps,v}. The locus 𝒳_{ps,v}^{v-irr} where the universal pseudocharacter is absolutely irreducible is Zariski open and carries an Azumaya algebra 𝒜 of rank n² with a continuous ρ^u_v : G_{F_ṽ} → 𝒜^× whose reduced trace is the universal pseudocharacter (Chenevier §4.2); 𝒳_ps^{p-irr} is the preimage of ∏_v 𝒳_{ps,v}^{v-irr}. Local splitting (Lemma 2.13): if ρ_v : G_{F_ṽ} → GL_n(E) is absolutely irreducible over E and z = tr ρ_v, then 𝒜 is isomorphic to M_n(𝒪_𝒰) on some affinoid neighbourhood 𝒰 of z.
hypotheses: Pseudocharacters are Chenevier determinants (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0); when n! is invertible in k they are determined by traces.
Lemma 2.13 needs ρ_v defined over E; an E-point of the irreducible locus alone does not split the fibre of 𝒜.
proofSteps: Pro-representability of conjugate self-dual determinant deformations of τ̄ (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1, determinant deformation functor), with the conjugate self-duality condition closed.
Pass to rigid generic fibres by Berthelot's construction (AdicSpacesPartII R2).
Chenevier §4.2: over the absolutely irreducible locus the Cayley–Hamilton quotient of 𝒪[G] is an Azumaya algebra of rank n², and the reduced trace recovers the universal determinant.
Lemma 2.13: the stalk of 𝒜 at z is an Azumaya algebra over a Henselian local ring whose fibre is split by ρ_v, hence split; spread the splitting to an affinoid neighbourhood.
acceptance: For n = 1, 𝒳_{ps,v} is the rigid space of continuous characters of G_{F_ṽ} lifting a given residual character: a finite union of open polydiscs of dimension [F_ṽ : ℚ_p] + 1.
At a point given by an absolutely irreducible ρ_v over E, Lemma 2.13 gives a universal matrix representation G_{F_ṽ} → GL_n(𝒪(𝒰)) lifting ρ_v.

sources.locator: §2.11.1, definitions of 𝒳_ps, 𝒳_{ps,v} and Lemma 2.13, pp. 30–31
sources.match: Defines the rigid generic fibres of the global and local pseudodeformation rings, the absolutely irreducible loci with the Azumaya algebra and universal representation (after Chenevier), and proves local splitting at a point given by an absolutely irreducible representation over E.

uses.where: Newton–Thorne I, Theorem 2.24 and its proof, pp. 40–42
uses.how: the closed realization ℰ_n(τ̄_n) → 𝒳_{ps,n} × 𝒯_n and the trianguline locus 𝒵 are built over 𝒳_ps^{p-irr}
σ_{n,g} : 𝒳_{ps,2} → 𝒳_{ps,n} takes symmetric powers of pseudocharacters
reducibility of the universal pseudocharacter defines a Zariski closed locus of ℰ_0

api.name: PseudocharSpace
api.statement: The rigid generic fibre 𝒳_ps of the conjugate self-dual pseudodeformation ring of τ̄, with its universal pseudocharacter.

api.name: PseudocharSpace.local
api.statement: The unrestricted local pseudodeformation space 𝒳_{ps,v} for a p-adic place v and the restriction morphism 𝒳_ps → ∏_v 𝒳_{ps,v}.

api.name: PseudocharSpace.absIrrLocus
api.statement: The Zariski open absolutely irreducible locus, with its Azumaya algebra 𝒜 and universal representation ρ^u into 𝒜^×.

api.name: PseudocharSpace.trace_universalRep
api.statement: The reduced trace of ρ^u is the universal pseudocharacter on the irreducible locus.

api.name: PseudocharSpace.split_near
api.statement: Lemma 2.13: at a point given by an absolutely irreducible representation over E the Azumaya algebra is a matrix algebra on an affinoid neighbourhood.

api.name: PseudocharSpace.points
api.statement: E-points of 𝒳_ps correspond to conjugate self-dual E-valued pseudocharacters (Chenevier determinants) of G_{F,S} reducing to τ̄.

api.name: PseudocharSpace.restriction_trace
api.statement: At every E-point, the local universal determinant is the restriction of the global determinant to the chosen local decomposition group. The local functor is unrestricted even though the global determinant is polarized.

tests.name: PseudocharSpace.dim_one
tests.statement: For n = 1 and G_{F_ṽ} with F_ṽ = ℚ_p, p odd, the local space has dimension 2 (the characters of ℤ_p^× × ℤ_p lifting a fixed residual character form a two-dimensional open polydisc after fixing the torsion part).

tests.name: PseudocharSpace.absIrr_residual
tests.statement: If the fixed local residual pseudocharacter is absolutely irreducible, its entire characteristic-zero deformation space is absolutely irreducible. Openness therefore does not imply that this locus is nonclosed; an ordinary upper triangular representation is reducible, even when the extension is nonsplit.

tests.name: PseudocharSpace.split_needs_E_point
tests.statement: If the fibre of 𝒜 at an E-point is a non-split quaternion algebra over E (the pseudocharacter is the reduced trace of a representation into a division algebra), Lemma 2.13 does not apply; splitting needs ρ_v over E.

tests.name: PseudocharSpace.trace_eq_classical
tests.statement: At a point given by ρ : G_{F,S} → GL_n(E), the universal pseudocharacter specialises to the Chenevier determinant of ρ (IHG.0, determinant of a matrix representation).

nodes.title: Polarized lifts correspond to conjugate self-dual traces
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G_{F,S} → GL_n(E) be absolutely irreducible with ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−n}, extended to ρ_1 : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(E) with multiplier ν ∘ ρ_1 = ε^{1−n}δ_{F/F⁺}^a, where a ∈ {0, 1} is determined by ρ. For every complete Noetherian local E-algebra A with residue field E (in particular every Artinian one), conjugacy classes of lifts ρ′ : G_{F,S} → GL_n(A) of ρ whose trace satisfies tr ρ′ ∘ c = tr(ρ′^∨) · ε^{1−n} correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes (by 1 + M_n(𝔪_A)) of lifts ρ′_1 : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(A) of ρ_1 with ν ∘ ρ′_1 = ε^{1−n}δ^a, the map being restriction to G_{F,S}.
hypotheses: ρ absolutely irreducible over E; the multiplier character is fixed.
The category is the complete Noetherian local E-algebras with residue field E, as used on p. 43 of the source (correction E11 of the extraction).
proofSteps: Surjectivity: the trace condition and absolute irreducibility give an isomorphism ρ′^c ≅ ρ′^∨ε^{1−n} over A (Carayol–Serre for absolutely irreducible residual representation of the E-algebra), whose matrix J′ extends ρ′ to 𝒢_n (Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemmas 2.1.1, 2.1.4).

Two extensions of the same restriction with the prescribed multiplier differ at complex conjugation by a scalar λ in 1+𝔪_A. Since 2 is invertible in E, Hensel gives α in 1+𝔪_A with α²=λ^{-1}; conjugation by (α,1) identifies the extensions. This proves uniqueness up to strict conjugacy, rather than equality of the chosen matrices.

Fix ν=ε^{1−n}δ^a as part of the deformation problem. Its value on the odd coset and hence a are not recovered from the trace on G_F alone. The chosen extension of the residual representation fixes the polarization sign.
acceptance: For n = 1 the lemma says a character χ of G_F with χχ^c = ε^0 · 1 lifted with χ′χ′^c = 1 extends uniquely up to conjugacy to 𝒢_1 = (GL_1 × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j}.
With A = E[ε]/(ε²) the bijection identifies the tangent space of the polarized deformation functor with H¹(G_{F⁺,S}, ad ρ_1), as used in SP.0/pseudocharacter-tangent-spaces.

sources.match: States the bijection between conjugacy classes of polarized lifts and lifts with conjugate self-dual trace, for absolutely irreducible ρ, citing Clozel–Harris–Taylor and Chenevier.

nodes.title: Tangent spaces of pseudocharacter spaces at absolutely irreducible points
nodes.statement: (1) At an E-point z of 𝒳_{ps,p}^{p-irr} given by absolutely irreducible ρ_v : G_{F_ṽ} → GL_n(E) (v ∈ S_p), the tangent space is ⊕_{v∈S_p} H¹(F_ṽ, ad ρ_v). (2) At an E-point z of 𝒳_ps^{p-irr} given by ρ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(E) with each ρ|_{G_{F_ṽ}} absolutely irreducible, the tangent space is H¹(G_{F⁺,S}, ad ρ), and the differential of 𝒳_ps → 𝒳_{ps,p} is the restriction map to ⊕_v H¹(F_ṽ, ad ρ_v).
hypotheses: Points with absolutely irreducible local restrictions; ad ρ carries the conjugation action of 𝒢_n through the polarization.
proofSteps: On the absolutely irreducible locus pseudodeformations are deformations of representations (Chenevier §4.1; SP.0/pseudocharacter-rigid-spaces).
Deformations of an absolutely irreducible representation over E[ε] are classified by H¹ of the adjoint (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1, tangent spaces).
For (2), SP.0/polarized-lifts-and-traces identifies conjugate self-dual pseudodeformations with polarized deformations, whose tangent space is H¹(G_{F⁺,S}, ad ρ) (GlobalGaloisDeformations G7).
acceptance: For n = 1 and F_ṽ = ℚ_p, dim H¹(ℚ_p, E) = 2, matching the dimension of 𝒳_{ps,v} for characters.
For n = 2 and ρ_v absolutely irreducible with H²(ℚ_p, ad ρ_v) = 0, the local Euler characteristic gives dim H¹ = 4 + 1 = 5, the dimension of the local pseudocharacter space at that point.

sources.match: Computes the tangent spaces of the local and global pseudocharacter spaces at absolutely irreducible points as H¹ of the adjoint, compatibly with restriction.

nodes.title: Analytic continuation of symmetric power functoriality: the non-critical case
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 3 and τ̄_2 a residual conjugate self-dual pseudocharacter of dimension 2 with τ̄_n = Sym^{n−1}τ̄_2. Let (π_2, χ_2) be a refined automorphic representation of the definite unitary group G_2 with tr r̄_{π_2,ι} = τ̄_2 and point z_2 = γ_2(π_2, χ_2) of ℰ_2(τ̄_2). Suppose (1) χ_2 is numerically non-critical and n-regular; (2) there is a refined automorphic (π_n, χ_n) of G_n with (σ_n ∘ i_2)(z_2) = i_n(z_n); (3) for every v ∈ S_p the Zariski closure of r_{π_2,ι}(G_{F_ṽ}) contains SL_2. Then every irreducible component 𝒞 of ℰ_2(τ̄_2)_{ℂ_p} through z_2 satisfies (σ_n ∘ i_2)(𝒞) ⊂ i_n(ℰ_n(τ̄_n)_{ℂ_p}).
hypotheses: n ≥ 3 (standing assumption of §2.18.1); ℰ_m(τ̄_m) the eigenvariety of the definite unitary group G_m with closed realization i_m : ℰ_m → 𝒳_{ps,m} × 𝒯_m (parent §4.3).
Numerically non-critical: the slopes of the refinement are small relative to the gaps between Hodge–Tate weights, so the attached triangulation is non-critical.
proofSteps: r_{π_n,ι}|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is trianguline with parameter σ_{n,p}(δ_2), which is regular and non-critical by (1) and (3) (Remark 2.25: (3) keeps all symmetric powers locally irreducible).

Choose an affinoid U around z_n in the absolutely irreducible, regular parameter locus. Define 𝒵 to be the Zariski closure in U of the points whose local representations are trianguline with the prescribed parameters. Family triangulation on the dense classical locus puts the eigenvariety in this closure near z_n; it does not assert a triangulation over every point of an arbitrary neighbourhood.

The trianguline tangent bound (parent §4.3, NTI Proposition 2.11), generic local Weil–Deligne parameters and adjoint Selmer vanishing give dim T_{z_n}𝒵≤dim 𝒲_n. The eigenvariety is equidimensional of this dimension, so its closed realization equals 𝒵 near z_n and is smooth there.

Apply family triangulation to the rank-two eigenvariety at its accumulating classical points and take symmetric powers. Their image lies in the pointwise trianguline locus, hence in 𝒵. Zariski density and closedness give the required containment of an affinoid neighbourhood; SP.0/analytic-continuation-lemma then treats every component through z_2.
acceptance: For n = 3 and a refinement with α/β not a root of unity of order 1 or 2, condition (1) is the non-critical slope condition plus α ≠ ±β.
If H¹_f(F⁺, ad r_{π_n,ι}) ≠ 0 the dimension bound fails and the proof gives nothing (the hypothesis enters through PL.8).

sources.locator: Theorem 2.24 and proof, §2.18.1, pp. 40–42; Remark 2.25, p. 42
sources.match: States and proves that under non-criticality, n-regularity and large local image the symmetric power map sends every component of ℰ_2 through a symmetric-power point into ℰ_n, by the tangent-space bound on the trianguline locus.

nodes.title: Analytic continuation of symmetric power functoriality: the ordinary case
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 3 and (π_2, χ_2), z_2 be as in SP.1/continuation-noncritical. Suppose (1) χ_2 is ordinary; (2) there is a refined automorphic (π_n, χ_n) of G_n with (σ_n ∘ i_2)(z_2) = i_n(z_n); (3) the Zariski closure of r_{π_2,ι}(G_F) contains SL_2. Then every irreducible component 𝒞 of ℰ_2(τ̄_2)_{ℂ_p} through z_2 satisfies (σ_n ∘ i_2)(𝒞) ⊂ i_n(ℰ_n(τ̄_n)_{ℂ_p}).
hypotheses: Ordinary refinement: the U_p-eigenvalues are p-adic units after the normalization of the parent's §4.3.
In the proof the affinoid neighbourhood U must be chosen inside 𝒳^{irr}_{ps,n} × (𝒯^{reg}_n ∩ 𝒯^{HT-reg}_n), which is Zariski open and contains δ_n (correction E12 of the extraction).
proofSteps: Replace the trianguline locus by the closed subspace 𝒵^{ord} of the flag variety of G_{F_ṽ}-stable flags in the universal representation over U whose graded pieces are the characters δ_{z,v,i}.

The map 𝒵^{ord} → U is a closed immersion once U is shrunk as in the hypothesis (correction E12); tangent vectors of 𝒵^{ord} at z_n with fixed weight lie in H¹_g (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.8, ordinary tangent vectors, after Geraghty Lemma 3.9).
H¹_f(F⁺, ad r_{π_n,ι}) = 0 (PL.8) gives dim T_{z_n}𝒵^{ord} ≤ dim 𝒲_n; conclude as in the non-critical case with SP.0/analytic-continuation-lemma.
acceptance: A CM form fails (3): its image has Zariski closure a torus normaliser, not containing SL_2.
For an ordinary point the theorem needs no slope condition, in contrast to SP.1/continuation-noncritical.

sources.match: States and proves the ordinary analogue: the symmetric power map sends every component of ℰ_2 through an ordinary symmetric-power point into ℰ_n, using the closed space of ordinary flags.

nodes.title: Non-criticality passes to symmetric powers
nodes.statement: Let ρ_v : G_{F_ṽ} → GL_2(Q̄_p) be continuous, regular and de Rham, such that WD(ρ_v) has distinct Jordan–Hölder characters χ_1, χ_2 with (χ_1/χ_2)^i ≠ 1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, and suppose every triangulation of ρ_v is non-critical. Then every triangulation of Sym^{n−1}ρ_v is non-critical.
hypotheses: ρ_v regular de Rham (distinct Hodge–Tate weights at every embedding).
The ratio condition is n-regularity of the Weil–Deligne parameter.
proofSteps: Work with the filtered (φ, N, Gal(L/K))-module of ρ_v (PadicHodgeTheory R06.3). If N ≠ 0 the triangulation is unique and non-criticality is read off directly.

If N = 0 the refinements of Sym^{n−1} are orderings of the monomials χ_1^aχ_2^b, which are distinct by n-regularity; the Hodge filtration of Sym^{n−1} at each embedding τ is spanned by powers of the line l_τ = ⟨e_1 + a_τe_2⟩.

Non-criticality of every triangulation of ρ_v means a_τ ≠ 0, ∞ for all τ; a Vandermonde determinant in the powers of a_τ shows every flag of φ-stable lines in Sym^{n−1} is in general position with the Hodge filtration (Chenevier 2011, Example 3.26).
acceptance: For n = 2 the statement is the hypothesis itself.
If χ_1/χ_2 has order 2 and n = 3, the monomials χ_1², χ_1χ_2, χ_2² have χ_1² = χ_2², two refinements of Sym² coincide in parameter and the argument breaks down; n-regularity is necessary.

sources.match: States that non-criticality of all triangulations of a regular de Rham ρ_v with n-regular Weil–Deligne parameter passes to Sym^{n−1}, proved with a Vandermonde determinant.

nodes.title: Symmetric power automorphy along an irreducible component of ℰ_2
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 3 and (π_2, χ_2), (π′_2, χ′_2) refined automorphic representations of G_2 with points z_2, z′_2 ∈ ℰ_2(Q̄_p). Suppose either (non-critical case) χ_2 is numerically non-critical and n-regular; every triangulation of r_{π′_2,ι}|_{G_{F_ṽ}} (v ∈ S_p) is non-critical and χ′_2 is n-regular; the Zariski closures of r_{π_2,ι}(G_{F_ṽ}) and r_{π′_2,ι}(G_{F_ṽ}) contain SL_2; Sym^{n−1}r_{π_2,ι} ≅ r_{π_n,ι} for an automorphic π_n of G_n; and z_2, z′_2 lie on a common irreducible component of ℰ_{2,ℂ_p}; or (ordinary case) χ_2 is ordinary, the Zariski closure of r_{π_2,ι}(G_F) contains SL_2, Sym^{n−1}r_{π_2,ι} ≅ r_{π_n,ι}, and z_2, z′_2 lie on a common component. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_2,ι} ≅ r_{π′_n,ι} for an automorphic representation π′_n of G_n(𝔸_{F⁺}).
hypotheses: n ≥ 3; refinements accessible in the sense of the parent's §1.1.
proofSteps: The refinement χ_n = (χ_{2,v,1}^{n−1} ⊗ χ_{2,v,1}^{n−2}χ_{2,v,2} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ χ_{2,v,2}^{n−1}) of π_n is accessible (Zelevinsky Theorem 9.7, Rodier §4.4), so z_n exists and (σ_n ∘ i_2)(z_2) = i_n(z_n).

SP.1/continuation-noncritical or SP.1/continuation-ordinary puts σ_n ∘ i_2 of the common component into i_n(ℰ_n); Conrad's base change of components (SP.0/analytic-continuation-lemma) handles the passage to ℂ_p.

The image point z′_n of z′_2 is classical: in the ordinary case by Hida classicality (PL.2), in the non-critical case because Sym^{n−1} of every triangulation of r_{π′_2,ι} is non-critical (SP.1/noncritical-symmetric-powers) and non-critical points with n-regular refinement are classical (parent §4.3, Newton–Thorne I Lemma 2.30).
A classical point of ℰ_n is attached to an automorphic π′_n of G_n with r_{π′_n,ι} ≅ Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_2,ι}.
acceptance: Taking z′_2 = z_2 recovers the hypothesis.
The ordinary case applies to two Hida families on one component; the non-critical case needs both refinements n-regular.

sources.locator: Corollary 2.28 and proof with its footnote, §2.18.1, pp. 43–44
sources.match: Deduces from Theorems 2.24 and 2.27 that automorphy of Sym^{n−1} propagates along an irreducible component of ℰ_2, with classicality from Lemmas 2.26, 2.29 and 2.30.

nodes.title: The twin involution on the eigencurve
nodes.statement: Let ℰ_0 be the Coleman–Mazur–Buzzard eigencurve of tame level N at p, and Z_0^{pc} ⊂ ℰ_0 the set of classical points z attached to (π_0, χ_{0,1} ⊗ χ_{0,2}) with π_{0,p} not a twist of Steinberg. Let ψ be the finite-order Hecke character of ℚ unramified outside p whose p-component restricts on ℤ_p^× to χ_{0,2}^{−1}|_{ℤ_p^×}. The twin of z is τ(z) ∈ Z_0^{pc}, the point attached to π_0 ⊗ ιψ with refinement χ_{0,2}ψ_p ⊗ χ_{0,1}ψ_p, where ψ_p = ψ|_{ℚ_p^×} is the p-component of ψ (correction E9 of the extraction). Then τ² = 1; for π_{0,p} unramified the twin is the companion point of the other refinement. Lemma 2.32: the slopes satisfy s(z) + s(τ(z)) = k − 1, and v_p(κ(z)(1 + q) − 1) = v_p(κ(τ(z))(1 + q) − 1), with q = p for p odd and q = 4 for p = 2.
hypotheses: π_{0,p} not a twist of Steinberg (so both refinements are accessible).
k is the weight of π_0; κ is the weight map to the weight space 𝒲_0.
proofSteps: Both χ_{0,2}ψ_p ⊗ χ_{0,1}ψ_p and the original refinement are accessible refinements of the twisted representation (π_{0,p} is a principal series).

The product of the two normalized U_p eigenvalues has valuation k−1, which gives the slope sum. Write the weight character on 1+q as (1+q)^{k−2}η, with η of p-power order. The twin replaces η by η^{-1}. If η=1 the valuations coincide. If η≠1, v_p(η(1+q)−1)=v_p(η−1) is strictly below v_p((1+q)^{k−2}−1) (when the latter is nonzero), and the same holds for η^{-1}; the two weight valuations therefore coincide. A finite-order twist is not in general invisible to valuation.
acceptance: For π_{0,p} unramified with U_p-roots α, β, the twin exchanges α and β (ψ trivial), and s(α) + s(β) = k − 1.
Twins of points of the boundary annuli are located by SP.3/twin-on-boundary-annulus.

sources.locator: §2.31, definition of the twin and Lemma 2.32, p. 49
sources.match: Defines the twin of a point of Z_0^{pc} by twisting with ψ and exchanging the refinement, and proves the slope sum and weight valuation identities.

uses.how: locates the twin of a point of X_i on X_{i′} with i + i′ = (k − 1)/v_p(w)
the ping-pong move passes from a point to its twin on another annulus

tests.name: Eigencurve.twin_unramified

tests.name: Eigencurve.twin_Qp_component

nodes.title: Trivialising a family of characters over a CM field
nodes.statement: Let F be a CM field in which every p-adic place of F⁺ splits, S̃_p a set of p-adic places of F with S̃_p ⊔ S̃_p^c the set of all p-adic places, W a connected rigid space over E and χ : G_ℚ → 𝒪(W)^× a continuous character unramified almost everywhere. Then there are a finite étale morphism η : W̃ → W and a continuous character ψ : G_F → 𝒪(W̃)^×, unramified almost everywhere and at every ṽ ∈ S̃_p, with ψψ^c = η^*(χ)|_{G_F}. Chevalley's theorem is used: every finite-index subgroup of 𝒪_F^× contains the units congruent to 1 modulo some non-zero ideal.
hypotheses: F CM with all p-adic places of F⁺ split; W connected.
proofSteps: On the p-adic units prescribe a character L equal to χ^{-1} on the conjugates of the chosen places and trivial on the chosen places. Its restriction to global units is trivial on a finite-index subgroup, by the CM norm-one-unit calculation.

Chevalley supplies a compact open subgroup U^p of the units away from p such that L is trivial on Γ(U^p)=𝒪_F^×∩(U^p×∏_{w|p}𝒪_{F_w}^×). In the idele-class quotient by U^p, the image of the p-adic units has finite index, by class-group finiteness. This is not a finite-index assertion for the closure of all global units in all p-adic units.

Restriction between rigid character spaces for that finite-index inclusion is finite étale. Pull back to extend L and obtain λ; χλλ^c is finite order because it is unramified at p and outside finitely many places. After a constant coefficient extension write it as φφ^c using the finite-order auxiliary-character theorem and put ψ=φλ^{-1}.
acceptance: For W a point the lemma is the existence of a continuous character ψ with ψψ^c = χ|_{G_F} unramified at S̃_p (PL.0, auxiliary characters).
If some p-adic place of F⁺ is inert in F, S̃_p cannot be chosen and the lemma is not claimed.

sources.match: Constructs, after a finite étale cover of the parameter space, a family of characters of G_F whose product with its conjugate is a given family of characters of G_ℚ, using Chevalley's theorem on units.

nodes.title: The base-change morphism from the eigencurve to a unitary eigenvariety
nodes.statement: Let F′ be an abelian CM field in which the primes dividing Np split, with [F′⁺ : ℚ] even and F′/F′⁺ everywhere unramified, F ⊃ F′ a soluble Galois CM extension of ℚ in which every prime dividing Np splits and F/F⁺ is everywhere unramified, ψ the family of characters of SP.2/trivialising-character-families over W̃ → 𝒲_0, and 𝒯̃ = 𝒯_0 ×_{𝒲_0} W̃. With b_p : 𝒯̃ → 𝒯_2 the twist of the refinement parameter by ψ^{−1} at the places of S̃_p, define b : 𝒳_{0,ps} × 𝒯̃ → 𝒳_{2,ps} × 𝒯_2, (τ, μ) ↦ (τ|_{G_F} ⊗ ψ^{−1}, b_p(μ)). Then b maps the classical points of the lift of ℰ_0 into i_2(ℰ_2), by Labesse's descent of the base change to the definite unitary group G_2.
hypotheses: F, F′ as above; G_2 the definite unitary group of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2 over F⁺.

Choose F so that ψ|_{G_F} is unramified away from p. All primes dividing Np split in F, so no imaginary quadratic inducing field of a classical tame-level-N point lies in F: that field ramifies at some prime dividing Np.
proofSteps: At a classical point (π_0, χ_0) the base change π_{0,F} ⊗ ψ^{−1} to GL_2(𝔸_F) is conjugate self-dual (ψψ^c = det twist), cuspidal: failure would make π_0 induced from an imaginary quadratic subfield of F ramified at a prime dividing Np, contrary to complete splitting there.

Labesse's Théorème 5.4 (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a, unitary descent) descends it to an automorphic representation of G_2 with the twisted refinement b_p(χ_0), so b sends the point into i_2(ℰ_2).
b is a morphism of rigid spaces because restriction of pseudocharacters and twisting by the family ψ are.
acceptance: At a classical point of weight k the image has parallel Hodge–Tate weights {0, k − 1} at every embedding of F (before the ψ-twist).

Base change of a form induced from an imaginary quadratic field K is not cuspidal when K⊂F. The splitting condition on F rules out this case; a CM form whose inducing field is not contained in F is not excluded merely for being CM.

sources.match: Builds the field F, the family ψ and the morphism b from the eigencurve to the unitary eigenvariety, and checks it on classical points with Labesse's descent.

uses.where: Newton–Thorne I, proof of Theorem 2.33, pp. 50–51
uses.how: transports a component of ℰ_0 into ℰ_2, where Corollary 2.28 applies

tests.name: Eigencurve.baseChange_CM_excluded
tests.statement: If the splitting condition is dropped and F contains the imaginary quadratic inducing field, the base change decomposes as two characters and cannot give the claimed cuspidal point.

nodes.title: Automorphy of symmetric powers is constant on components of the eigencurve
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and (π_0, χ_0), (π′_0, χ′_0) refined cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) whose points z_0, z′_0 of the eigencurve ℰ_0 (tame level N) lie on a common irreducible component of ℰ_{0,ℂ_p}. Suppose either (1) χ_0 is numerically non-critical and n-regular, (2) χ′_0 is n-regular, (3) the Zariski closures of r_{π_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) and r_{π′_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) contain SL_2, and (4) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic; or (1ord) χ_0 is ordinary, (2ord) π_0 and π′_0 are not CM, and (3ord) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_0,ι} is automorphic. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.5 (node ML.3/eigenvariety-propagation).
hypotheses: Automorphy of Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} in the sense of the parent's §0.2 (node ML.0/nt26-automorphy-predicate).
For n = 2 the statement is trivial; the work is for n ≥ 3.
proofSteps: Choose F′, F, ψ and b as in SP.2/eigencurve-base-change-morphism.

After a finite coefficient extension the selected component is geometrically irreducible. Its pullback along W̃→W is finite étale, and each irreducible component of that pullback maps onto it. Thus lifts of both points can be chosen on one geometrically irreducible component. The accumulating classical locus and closedness put the image of this component inside the unitary eigenvariety.

Large local image at p (3) gives non-criticality of all triangulations (Newton–Thorne I Example 2.10), so the hypotheses of SP.1/automorphy-along-components hold for the base-changed points; in the ordinary case (2ord) gives large global image.

b maps the common component into a component of ℰ_2 through b(z_0) and b(z′_0) (SP.0/analytic-continuation-lemma); Sym^{n−1} of the base change of π_0 is automorphic on G_n by (4) and Labesse descent.

SP.1/automorphy-along-components gives automorphy of Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_0,ι}|_{G_F} on G_n, hence on GL_n(𝔸_F) by base change; soluble descent for GL_n (parent ML.5, cyclic base change and descent) returns to ℚ.
acceptance: n = 2: the conclusion holds for every z′_0 (Sym^1 is r itself, automorphic by modularity).
Two points on a common Hida family with non-CM forms satisfy the ordinary hypotheses.

sources.match: States and proves that automorphy of Sym^{n−1} propagates along irreducible components of the eigencurve, through base change to a definite unitary eigenvariety and Corollary 2.28.

nodes.title: The locus where the hypotheses of Theorem 2.33 fail is Zariski closed
nodes.statement: Fix n ≥ 1. The set Z ⊂ ℰ_0 of points x whose pseudocharacter t_x is absolutely reducible, or is the trace of an absolutely irreducible ρ_x whose image has Zariski closure not containing SL_2, or satisfies t_x|_{G_{ℚ_l}} = χ_1 + χ_2 with (χ_1/χ_2)^i = 1 for some prime l | N and some 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, is Zariski closed in ℰ_0.
hypotheses: ℰ_0 of tame level N; t_x the specialised universal pseudocharacter.
proofSteps: Absolute reducibility is a Zariski closed condition on the pseudocharacter space (Chenevier §4.2; SP.0/pseudocharacter-rigid-spaces).

For absolutely irreducible ρ_x, the Zariski closure of the image contains SL_2 iff Sym^6ρ_x is absolutely irreducible (finite subgroups of PGL_2 and normalisers of tori have no irreducible Sym^6); this is again a reducibility condition on the pseudocharacter Sym^6 t_x.

At l|N choose finitely many local Galois elements whose character values detect the ratio conditions. The discriminants of the characteristic polynomials of Sym^{n−1} at these elements are analytic functions. Their common vanishing cuts out the specified finite-order-ratio locus, as in NTI pp. 52–53, without depending on the later SP.8 argument.
acceptance: The CM points of a CM family form part of Z (their images have Zariski closure a torus normaliser).
For n = 1 the ratio condition is empty and Z is the reducible-or-small-image locus.

sources.match: Proves that reducibility, small Zariski closure of the image, and non-regularity at primes dividing the level define a Zariski closed subset of the eigencurve.

nodes.title: Buzzard–Kilford: the 2-adic eigencurve of tame level one over the boundary annulus
nodes.statement: Take p = 2 and N = 1. Then ℰ_0 lies over the component 𝒲_0⁺ of weight space where χ(−1) = 1, and w = χ(5) − 1 identifies 𝒲_0⁺ with the open unit disc {|w| < 1}. Over the annulus 𝒲_0(b) = {|8| < |w| < 1}, the preimage ℰ_0(b) = κ^{−1}(𝒲_0(b)) is a disjoint union ⊔_{i≥1} X_i of admissible opens, each κ|_{X_i} : X_i → 𝒲_0(b) is an isomorphism, and on X_i the slope is i·v_2(w). Buzzard–Kilford also deduce that there are no newforms of level 4 and odd slope (used in the proof of Newton–Thorne I Theorem 7.6, p. 90). This proves the statement the parent records in §4.6 (node ML.3/buzzard-kilford-eigencurve).
hypotheses: The cuspidal eigencurve: over the boundary annulus the ordinary part of the full eigencurve is the Eisenstein family, removed here (Pilloni §6; Buzzard–Calegari Lemma 7.4).
proofSteps: Buzzard–Kilford compute the U_2 operator on overconvergent forms of weight χ with |8| < |w(χ)| < 1 in the basis of powers of the 2-adic Hauptmodul and show its Newton polygon has slopes v_2(w), 2v_2(w), 3v_2(w), … each with multiplicity one (Buzzard–Kilford, Theorem B).
Hence the spectral curve over 𝒲_0(b) splits into components of degree one over weight space, the X_i.
Remove the Eisenstein component to pass to the cuspidal eigencurve (Pilloni; Buzzard–Calegari).
acceptance: At w with v_2(w) = 1/2 (a weight with m = 2 in SP.3/boundary-annulus-weights) the slopes are 1/2, 1, 3/2, …
No classical point of odd slope and level 4 exists over the annulus.

sources.match: Records Buzzard–Kilford's theorem in the form used: the boundary annulus, the decomposition into annuli X_i mapping isomorphically to weight space, and slope i·v_2(w) on X_i.
Uses the consequence of Buzzard–Kilford that there are no newforms of level 4 and odd slope.
Computes the slopes of U_2 on overconvergent 2-adic forms of tame level one near the boundary of weight space.

nodes.title: Classical weights in the 2-adic boundary annulus
nodes.statement: Let z be a classical point of weight k whose weight character satisfies κ(z)(5) = 5^{k−2}ζ with ζ a primitive 2^m-th root of unity (m ≥ 0). Then κ(z) ∈ 𝒲_0(b) iff k is odd or m ≥ 1; v_2(w(z)) = 2^{1−m} for m ≥ 1, and v_2(w(z)) = 2 for m = 0 with k odd; and in all these cases (k − 1)/v_2(w(z)) is an integer.
proofSteps: For j=k−2>0, lifting the exponent gives v₂(5^j−1)=2+v₂(j). If m=0 and k is odd this is 2; if k is even and k>2 it is at least 3. For k=2,m=0 one has w=0, outside the boundary annulus; do not apply the nonzero-j formula there.
For m = 0, k odd: (k − 1)/2 is an integer; for m ≥ 1: (k − 1)·2^{m−1} is an integer.
acceptance: k = 4, m = 0: w = 24, v_2(w) = 3, not in the annulus.

sources.match: Describes the classical weights lying over the boundary annulus and the valuation of w at them, and notes the integrality used in Lemma 3.3.

nodes.title: The twin of a point on a boundary annulus
nodes.statement: Let z ∈ Z_0^{pc} ∩ ℰ_0(b) be of weight k with z ∈ X_i, and z′ = τ(z) its twin. Then z′ ∈ X_{i′}, where i + i′ = (k − 1)/v_2(w(z)). (The source prints z ∈ X_{i′}; correction E1 of the extraction.)
hypotheses: p = 2, N = 1; z classical with π_{0,2} not a twist of Steinberg.
proofSteps: By SP.2/twin-map, v_2(w(z′)) = v_2(w(z)), so z′ also lies over 𝒲_0(b), on some X_{i′}.
By SP.3/buzzard-kilford-boundary the slopes are s(z) = i·v_2(w(z)) and s(z′) = i′·v_2(w(z)).
Lemma 2.32 gives s(z) + s(z′) = k − 1; divide by v_2(w(z)), an integer quotient by SP.3/boundary-annulus-weights.
acceptance: Weight 3 at m = 0: v_2(w) = 2, so i + i′ = 1, impossible for i, i′ ≥ 1; hence no classical non-Steinberg point of weight 3 and trivial character lies over the annulus with both refinements there, consistent with Buzzard–Kilford.
Weight 2, m = 1: i + i′ = 1 likewise forbids such points.

sources.match: Locates the twin of a point on X_i on the annulus X_{i′} with i + i′ = (k − 1)/v_p(w(z)).

nodes.title: Refinements of level-one forms at 2 are non-critical and regular
nodes.statement: Let π be an everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2. Every accessible refinement of π at 2 is numerically non-critical and n-regular for every n ≥ 2. Ingredients: no level-one cusp form is 2-ordinary; and for l ∈ {5, 7} the semisimplified mod-l representation of a level-one eigenform is a twist of that of E_4 or E_6 (l = 5) or of E_4, E_6 or E_8 (l = 7), so ι_5^{−1}(α/β) ≡ 2³ or 2⁵ and ι_7^{−1}(α/β) ≡ 2³, 2⁵ or 2⁷ modulo the maximal ideal, where α, β are the roots of the T_2-polynomial.
hypotheses: π of level one; refinements at p = 2 given by the roots α, β of X² − a_2X + 2^{k−1}.
proofSteps: No cusp form of level one is ordinary at 2, so both slopes are positive; since they add up to k − 1, both are less than k − 1, which gives numerical non-criticality.

If α/β were a root of unity ζ, the mod 5 congruence with E_4 or E_6 gives ι_5^{−1}(ζ) ≡ 2³ or 2⁵, so ζ is a 5-power root of unity times ±i (2 has order 4 in 𝔽_5^×); the mod 7 congruence with E_4, E_6 or E_8 makes ζ a 7-power root of unity times a cube root of unity; these are incompatible (argument of F. Diamond, avoiding Hatada's congruence).
acceptance: For Δ (k = 12), a_2 = −24, so v_2(a_2) = 3 and the slopes are 3 and 8, both in (0, 11).
The argument would fail at level Γ_0(2), where forms can be 2-ordinary.

sources.match: Proves that refinements at 2 of level-one forms are numerically non-critical and n-regular for all n, by non-ordinarity at 2 and congruences modulo 5 and 7 with Eisenstein series.

nodes.title: Local reducibility and local image criteria for modular forms
nodes.statement: Let π be cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 and p a prime. (1) r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is reducible iff π is ι-ordinary. (2) If either r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is irreducible and π_p admits a 3-regular refinement, or k > 2 and r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is not potentially crystalline, then the Zariski closure of r_{π,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) in GL_2 contains SL_2. (3) If p = 2 and π is everywhere unramified, the Zariski closure of r_{π,ι}(G_{ℚ_2}) contains SL_2. Sen's theorem is used: a Hodge–Tate representation of G_{ℚ_p} with distinct weights has a regular maximal torus in the Zariski closure of its image.
hypotheses: π cuspidal of weight k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: (1): Thorne 2015, Theorem 2.4 and Lemma 2.3 (ordinary forms have reducible local representation and conversely, via the weight filtration).

(2): by Sen the Zariski closure H of the image contains a regular torus; if H does not contain SL_2, its identity component is a torus, so r is potentially abelian, induced or a sum of characters; the 3-regularity or non-potentially-crystalline hypothesis excludes both.
(3): an induced local representation at 2 would force the T_2-eigenvalue to vanish, which is excluded as in SP.3/level-one-refinements-at-two; reducibility is excluded by non-ordinarity.
acceptance: A CM form at a prime inert in the CM field has induced local representation; its Zariski closure is a torus normaliser, and π_p has refinement ratio −1, failing 3-regularity, consistent with (2).
A weight-2 form with good supersingular reduction is potentially crystalline; (2) then needs the 3-regular hypothesis.

sources.match: Proves the three local criteria: reducibility iff ordinarity, large Zariski closure under 3-regularity or non-potential crystallinity, and large Zariski closure at 2 in level one, using Sen's theorem.

nodes.title: Moving within one annulus
nodes.statement: Let z, z′ be classical points of X_i (for some i ≥ 1) attached to (π, χ), (π′, χ′) with χ and χ′ n-regular. If Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic, then so is Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι}.
hypotheses: p = 2, N = 1; X_i a Buzzard–Kilford annulus.
proofSteps: For n=2 automorphy is already given by the forms themselves. Assume n≥3. The annulus X_i is geometrically irreducible, so the two points lie on a common component.

There are no ordinary cuspidal points over this boundary annulus. The original refinement and, in the potentially crystalline case, its twin therefore have positive slopes. Since the slope sum is k−1, both are numerically noncritical. In the Steinberg case the same conclusion follows from the Steinberg slope (k−2)/2.
Nonordinarity gives local irreducibility. An n-regular refinement with n≥3 is 3-regular, so SP.3/local-image-criteria gives large local image. Apply SP.2/eigencurve-propagation.
acceptance: Two classical points of X_1 of different weights with n-regular refinements are linked.

sources.match: Shows automorphy of Sym^{n−1} propagates between n-regular classical points of one annulus X_i, by Theorem 2.33.

nodes.title: The ping-pong move
nodes.statement: Let π be everywhere unramified of weight k ≥ 2 with an accessible refinement χ at 2. There is m_π ≥ 1 such that for every m ≥ m_π there is a cuspidal π′ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ), unramified outside 2, with two accessible refinements of distinct slopes, and a refinement χ′ of π′ such that (π, χ) and (π′, χ′) lie on one irreducible component of ℰ_{0,ℂ_p}, the point z′ of (π′, χ′) lies over 𝒲_0(b), its twin z″ = τ(z′), attached to the twisted representation denoted π″, lies on X_{2^m−1}, and automorphy of any one of Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι}, Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι}, Sym^{n−1}r_{π″,ι} implies all three.
proofSteps: The component of (π, χ) meets ℰ_0(b) in some X_i (every component meets the boundary annulus, parent §4.6).

Let m_π be the least integer m ≥ 1 with (2i + 2^{m+1} − 3)/2 > 2i. For m ≥ m_π put k′ = 2i + 2^{m+1} − 1 (odd) and let z′ ∈ X_i be the point with κ(z′)(5) = 5^{k′−2}; then v_2(w(z′)) = 2, s(z′) = 2i < (k′ − 2)/2, so z′ is classical by Coleman's small-slope criterion (PadicFamilies L2) and not 2-Steinberg (a Steinberg point would have slope (k′ − 2)/2); its two refinements have the distinct slopes 2i and k′ − 1 − 2i.
SP.3/twin-on-boundary-annulus places the twin z″ on X_{i′} with i′ = (k′ − 1)/2 − i = 2^m − 1 (SP.3/boundary-annulus-weights).

The two refinements of π′ have unequal slopes, so their ratio is not a root of unity and they are n-regular for every n. They are nonordinary, so local-image-criteria gives large local image. The original level-one point uses level-one-refinements-at-two. Apply eigencurve-propagation between z and z′; twisting by the finite-order character defining the twin preserves symmetric-power automorphy and gives the equivalence with z″.
acceptance: The index 2^m − 1 depends only on m, so two level-one forms can be connected through a common annulus by choosing the same m (this is the 'ping-pong').

sources.match: Constructs from a level-one form a form of 2-power level on the same component whose twin lies on the annulus X_{2^m−1}, with automorphy of symmetric powers equivalent for all three.

nodes.title: Theorem D: symmetric powers for one level-one form give them for all
nodes.statement: Fix n ≥ 2. If π_0 is an everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 with Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} automorphic for some (equivalently any) prime p and ι, then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every everywhere unramified cuspidal π of weight ≥ 2. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.7 (node ML.3/level-one-ping-pong).
hypotheses: Automorphy in the sense of ML.0/nt26-automorphy-predicate; independence of p and ι by the parent's one-prime criterion (§4.15).
proofSteps: Work at p = 2. For π_0 and π choose refinements; by SP.3/ping-pong-move with a common m ≥ max(m_{π_0}, m_π) both are linked to points z″_0, z″ on X_{2^m−1}.

The new points z″_0 and z″ have unequal refinement slopes by the construction of ping-pong-move, hence n-regular refinements. Apply annulus-propagation on X_{2^m−1}. The level-one regularity lemma is used only for the original forms.
Chain the equivalences; pass between primes with the one-prime criterion (ML.3/one-prime-criterion).
acceptance: n = 2 is trivial; for n = 3, 4, 5 the conclusion is also given by the known low-rank lifts (parent ML.3/low-rank-symmetric-powers), a consistency check.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.1 and proof, §3, pp. 53, 57; Introduction, Theorem D, p. 3
sources.match: States Theorem D and proves it by ping-pong on the Buzzard–Kilford annuli using Theorem 2.33.

nodes.title: Quasi-split unitary groups and the pure inner twist of the definite group
nodes.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F of local or global fields with conjugation c, let Φ_n be the antidiagonal matrix with entries 1, −1, …, (−1)^{n−1} and θ_n(g) = Φ_n c(g)^{−t} Φ_n^{−1}. The quasi-split unitary group U_n is the fixed subgroup of θ_n in Res_{E/F} GL_n, with its θ-stable standard pinning and L-group ^LU_n = GL_n(ℂ) ⋊ W_F (w_c acting by g ↦ Φ_n g^{−t}Φ_n^{−1}); for 2(n_1 + ⋯ + n_{k−1}) + n_k = n its standard Levi subgroups are Res GL_{n_1} × ⋯ × Res GL_{n_{k−1}} × U_{n_k}. Under the standard assumptions (F/F⁺ CM and everywhere unramified, [F⁺ : ℚ] even, S ⊇ S_p split), the definite unitary group G_n over F⁺ (compact at infinity, quasi-split at finite places) is an inner form of U_n via ξ(g_1, g_2) = (g_1, Φ_n^{−1}g_2Φ_n), lifted to a pure inner twist (ξ, u) with u_c = (Φ_n, Φ_n) for n odd; a character μ of F^×\𝔸_F^× restricting to the quadratic character of F/F⁺ fixes the L-embeddings. This gives isomorphisms ι_v : G_n(F⁺_v) ≅ U_n(F⁺_v) at finite places and the canonical ι_w : G_n(F⁺_v) ≅ GL_n(F_w) at split v = ww^c, compatible with base change to totally real L⁺/F⁺.
hypotheses: Standard assumptions of Newton–Thorne I §1; for n even the twist uses (ζΦ_n, ζ^{−1}Φ_n) with tr ζ = 0.
proofSteps: Define U_n and its pinning; the Levi description is the block-diagonal computation.
The class of u is trivial in H¹(F⁺_v, U_n) at finite places (Hilbert 90 and Rogawski §1.9), so ι_v exists; at infinity the twist realises the compact form.
The definite group itself and its algebraic modular forms are PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2; this node adds the pure inner twist data used to normalise transfer factors (Kaletha).
acceptance: For n = 1, U_1 is the norm-one torus E^{N=1} and G_1 = U_1.
For n = 3 the Levi subgroups are U_3 and Res GL_1 × U_1.

sources.locator: Notation, pp. 8–9; §1, standard assumptions and the pure inner twist, pp. 9–10

nodes.title: Archimedean, unramified and split endoscopic character identities
nodes.statement: Let n be odd and E = (H, s, η) an extended endoscopic triple for the definite group G = G_n. (Archimedean) For v | ∞ and a Langlands parameter φ_H with η ∘ φ_H the parameter of an irreducible σ_v of G(F⁺_v), with π the tempered θ-invariant representation of H(F_ṽ) of parameter φ_H|_{W_{F_v}} and f_v a coefficient of σ_v, there is a sign ϵ(v, E, φ_H) ∈ {±1} with π̃(f̃_v^H) = ϵ(v, E, φ_H)σ_v(f_v) = ϵ(v, E, φ_H) for the Whittaker-normalised twisted trace, compatible with totally real base change. (Unramified inert) For f_v unramified and an unramified parameter φ_H, π̃(f̃_v^H) = σ_{v,H}(f_v^H) = σ_v(f_v), with the twisted trace normalised to fix the spherical vector. (Split) The same identities hold at split v for bounded parameters with the Whittaker normalisation.
hypotheses: n odd; transfer factors normalised by the pure inner twist of SP.4/unitary-groups-and-inner-twist.
proofSteps: Archimedean: Clozel 1982 and Kaletha 2016 Proposition 5.10; the sign depends on the pure inner twist.
Unramified: the fundamental lemmas for stable base change (Clozel 1990) and standard endoscopy (Laumon–Ngô) with Hales's normalisation (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.3).
Split: constant terms reduce to GL_n (Rogawski Lemma 4.13.1, Proposition 4.13.2; Shin §§3.3–3.4).
acceptance: Under a totally real base extension the archimedean sign at a lifted real place equals the sign at the original place (NTI Proposition 1.6). The unramified identity uses spherical normalization; the split identity uses Whittaker normalization.

sources.match: States the archimedean identity with a sign, and the unramified and split identities on the nose, for odd n with the normalisations of §1.

nodes.title: Stable base change and L-packets of U_n at an inert place
nodes.statement: Let v be a place of F⁺ inert in F. Identify irreducible admissible representations of GL_n(F_ṽ) with parameters W_{F_ṽ} × SL_2(ℂ) → GL_n(ℂ); let A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺ be the tempered conjugate self-dual ones whose parameter extends to W_{F⁺_v} × SL_2(ℂ) → ^LU_n (unique up to conjugacy, Gan–Gross–Prasad Theorem 8.1). Writing φ = ⊕ρ_i^{l_i} ⊕ σ_j^{m_j} ⊕ (τ_k ⊕ τ_k^{w_c,∨})^{n_k} with ρ_i conjugate self-dual of sign (−1)^{n−1} and σ_j of sign (−1)^n, the extension exists iff every m_j is even. Mœglin's extended cuspidal support esc(τ) of a tempered τ of U_n(F⁺_v) equals sc(π_τ) for a unique π_τ ∈ A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺ (Proposition 1.9); BC : τ ↦ π_τ is surjective with finite fibres, and the L-packets Π(π) = BC^{−1}(π) partition the tempered dual (Proposition 1.10); and for an extension π̃ to GL_n ⋊ θ there are constants c_τ ≠ 0 with π̃(f) = Σ_{τ∈Π(π)} c_τ τ(f^{U_n}) (Proposition 1.11).
hypotheses: v inert in F; tempered representations; Whittaker-normalised intertwining operator for π̃.
proofSteps: Mœglin 2007, Lemme 5.4 and Théorème 5.7 for θ-discrete π (all l_i = 1, J and K empty), extended to all tempered π by Waldspurger's Proposition III.4.1 and parabolic induction.
The twisted character identity: Mœglin 2007 Proposition 5.5 for θ-discrete π, constant terms (Morel Lemma 6.3.4) and disjointness of Jordan–Hölder factors otherwise.
These are the local statements of Mok's classification at inert places (parent ML.4), with Mœglin's explicit cuspidal-support description.
acceptance: The trivial representation of U_1 has base change the trivial character of F_ṽ^×; for n = 1 every packet is a singleton.
St_2(χ) ⊞ 1 with χ the nontrivial unramified quadratic character lies in A^θ_t(GL_3(F_ṽ))⁺ (SP.4/depth-zero-cuspidals).

nodes.title: Depth-zero cuspidal representations of U_3 and GL_3 and their base change
nodes.statement: Let v be inert with odd residue characteristic, k(v) its residue field and k(ṽ) the quadratic extension. τ(v) is the unique cuspidal unipotent representation of U_3(k(v)) (Lusztig). For k_3/k(v) cubic let C = ker(N : Res_{k_3k(ṽ)/k(v)}𝔾_m → Res_{k_3/k(v)}𝔾_m), an anisotropic torus embedded in U_3 uniquely up to conjugacy; for a prime p with q_v a primitive 6th root of unity mod p and θ : C(k(v)) → ℂ^× of order p, λ(v, θ) = −R_C^{U_3}θ is irreducible cuspidal. With C̃ = Res_{k_3k(ṽ)/k(ṽ)}𝔾_m and θ̃(z) = θ(z/z^c), λ̃(ṽ, θ̃) = R_{C̃}^{GL_3}θ̃ is irreducible cuspidal. Their compact inductions τ_v = c-Ind_{U_3(𝒪)}^{U_3(F⁺_v)} τ(v), λ_v(θ) and λ̃_ṽ(θ̃) = c-Ind_{F_ṽ^×GL_3(𝒪)}^{GL_3(F_ṽ)} λ̃(ṽ, θ̃), where the finite type is extended by trivial action of F_ṽ^× are irreducible supercuspidal, with BC(τ_v) = St_2(χ) ⊞ 1 (χ the nontrivial unramified quadratic character) and BC(λ_v(θ)) = λ̃_ṽ(θ̃) (Proposition 1.12). For n = 2k + 1 and π = St_2(χ) ⊞ 1 ⊞ (⊞_{i=1}^{2k−2}χ_i) with χ_i|_{𝒪^×} of order 2, after relabelling χ_i = χ_{2k−1−i}^{w_c,∨}, the packet Π(π) contains every irreducible subquotient of χ_1 × ⋯ × χ_{k−1} × τ_v (Corollary 1.13).
hypotheses: Odd residue characteristic; q_v a primitive 6th root of unity mod p for λ(v, θ).
Deligne–Lusztig induction R_C is used only for the anisotropic tori C ⊂ U_3 and C̃ ⊂ GL_3 (no atlas roadmap owns general Deligne–Lusztig theory; gap recorded).

For Corollary 1.13 require π∈A_t^θ(GL_n)⁺, including the correct conjugate-self-duality sign and multiplicities, before relabelling its characters. Arbitrary quadratic-on-units characters need not satisfy this.
proofSteps: Deligne–Lusztig: −R_C^{U_3}θ is irreducible cuspidal for θ in general position (θ of order p is in general position because q_v has order 6 mod p), since C lies in no proper rational parabolic.
Supercuspidality of depth-zero compact inductions: Moy–Prasad Proposition 6.6.
BC(τ_v): the reducibility points of depth-zero supercuspidals (Lust–Stevens §8, odd residue characteristic) give two possibilities; the sign condition BC(τ_v) ∈ A^θ_t⁺ selects St_2(χ) ⊞ 1.
BC(λ_v(θ)) = λ̃_ṽ(θ̃) by the same reducibility computation; Corollary 1.13 by Jacquet modules and SP.4/stable-base-change-packets.
acceptance: For q_v = 3 (so k(v) = 𝔽_3), dim τ(v) = q(q − 1) = 6, the cuspidal unipotent degree of U_3(𝔽_q).
dim λ(v, θ) = |U_3(𝔽_q)|_{ℓ′}, where ℓ=char 𝔽_q,/|C(𝔽_q)| = (q + 1)(q² − 1) (C is the anisotropic torus of order q³ + 1).

nodes.title: The types τ(v, n) and λ(v, θ, n) and their congruence
nodes.statement: Let v be inert, of odd residue characteristic, n = 2k + 1, p_v ⊂ U_n(F⁺_v) the parahoric with Levi quotient M_{(1,…,1,3)}(k(v)) = (Res GL_1)^{k−1} × U_3, and ω(ṽ) the nontrivial quadratic character of k(ṽ)^×. τ(v, n) (resp. λ(v, θ, n)) is the representation of p_v inflated from ω(ṽ) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ ω(ṽ) ⊗ τ(v) (resp. ⊗ λ(v, θ)). The test function φ(v, θ, n) is supported on p_v and inflated from the character of λ(v, θ, n)^∨, so π(φ) is a positive multiple of dim Hom_{p_v}(λ(v, θ, n), π|_{p_v}). When q_v mod p is a primitive 6th root of unity: (1) the reduction τ̄(v, n) is irreducible (Dudas–Malle, modular irreducibility of cuspidal unipotent characters); (2) the semisimplified reduction of λ(v, θ, n) contains τ̄(v, n) with multiplicity one (a Brauer-character computation for U_3(k(v)), Geck 1990 Theorem 4.2).
hypotheses: char k(v) odd; q_v of order 6 modulo p; θ of order p.
proofSteps: Inflate from the Levi quotient through the pro-unipotent radical of p_v.
Modular irreducibility: Dudas–Malle 2018.

Congruence: θ ≡ 1 mod p so R_C θ ≡ R_C 1 on p-regular classes; decompose R_C 1 into unipotent characters and use Geck's decomposition numbers for U_3 in non-defining characteristic with q of order 6 (the source notes a typo in Geck's proof).
acceptance: For k = 1 (n = 3), p_v = U_3(𝒪) and τ(v, 3) = τ(v).

nodes.title: Endoscopic transfer of the test function φ(v, θ, n)
nodes.statement: Assume char k(v) > n. Let φ = φ(v, θ, n), E = (H, s, η) with H = U_p × U_q, and π_p ∈ A^θ_t(GL_p(F_ṽ))⁺, π_q ∈ A^θ_t(GL_q(F_ṽ))⁺ with (π_p ⊗ π_q)~(φ̃^H) ≠ 0. Then sc(π_p) + sc(π_q) = λ̃_ṽ(θ̃) + χ_1 + ⋯ + χ_{2k−2} with each χ_i|_{𝒪^×} = ω(ṽ). The input is Kazhdan–Varshavsky's theorem: for char k(v) > n the transfer φ^H can be taken to be a weighted sum of inflations to H(𝒪) of the Deligne–Lusztig characters R_{C_i}^{H_{k(v)}}(θ^{−1} ⊗ ω(ṽ)^{⊗(k−1)}), one for each conjugacy class of embeddings C_i of C × (Res 𝔾_m)^{k−1} into H_{k(v)}.
hypotheses: char k(v) > n (needed for Kazhdan–Varshavsky).
proofSteps: Kazhdan–Varshavsky 2012 Theorem 2.2.6 computes φ^H as above.

Transitivity of Deligne–Lusztig induction and the cuspidality of λ̃(ṽ, θ̃) identify the depth-zero supercuspidal support of representations on which φ^H has nonzero twisted trace (Newton–Thorne I Proposition 1.14).
Combine with the twisted character identity of SP.4/stable-base-change-packets.
acceptance: In the stable case H=U_n the supercuspidal support contains λ̃_ṽ(θ̃), while the untwisted unipotent construction has the St₂(χ)⊞1 support. This distinguishes the supports used in level raising; it does not by itself prove that an arbitrary representation cannot contain both compact types.

sources.match: Determines the cuspidal supports of endoscopic representations detected by the transfer of φ(v, θ, n), using Kazhdan–Varshavsky's transfer of Deligne–Lusztig functions.

nodes.title: Splitting of lifts and Frobenius on fixed-type lifting rings
nodes.statement: Let ṽ be a place of F split over F⁺ with char k(ṽ) odd, 1 ≤ n_1 ≤ n, n_2 = n − n_1, q_ṽ mod p a primitive n_1-th root of unity and Θ a character of k_{n_1}^× of order p. Let ρ̄_ṽ = σ̄_{ṽ,1} ⊕ σ̄_{ṽ,2} with σ̄_{ṽ,1} ≅ Ind_{G_{F_{ṽ,n_1}}}^{G_{F_ṽ}} ψ̄_ṽ (ψ̄_ṽ unramified) and σ̄_{ṽ,2} ⊗ ω(ṽ)∘Art^{−1} unramified on inertia. (Lemma 1.21) Every lift of ρ̄_ṽ to a complete Noetherian local 𝒪-algebra R is (1 + M_n(𝔪_R))-conjugate to σ_{ṽ,1} ⊕ σ_{ṽ,2} with σ_{ṽ,i} lifting σ̄_{ṽ,i}, each unique up to conjugacy. On the fixed-type lifting ring R(ṽ, Θ, ρ̄_ṽ) (lifts of inertial type τ_ṽ, with the Artin map of F_{ṽ,n_1} on the first summands, correction E6): (3) with α_ṽ the reduction of (−1)^{n_1+1} det σ_{ṽ,1}(φ_ṽ), one has det(X − σ_{ṽ,1}(φ_ṽ^{n_1})) ≡ (X − α_ṽ)^{n_1} modulo ϖ, and α_ṽ in R(ṽ, Θ, ρ̄_ṽ)/(ϖ) is independent of the Frobenius lift φ_ṽ (correction E7: the printed Hensel argument is replaced); (4) for L_ṽ/F_ṽ finite with τ_ṽ|_{I_{L_ṽ}} trivial, the map from the framed ring of L_ṽ factors through its unramified quotient.
hypotheses: The hypotheses make H⁰ and H¹ of Hom(σ̄_1, σ̄_2) and Hom(σ̄_2, σ̄_1) vanish (Shotton Lemma 2.3); they fail for p = char k(ṽ) or p = 2.
The case n_1 = 1 (q_ṽ ≡ 1 mod p, λ̃ = Θ) is included (correction E19).
The coefficient prime p is odd and different from the residue characteristic of F_ṽ.
proofSteps: Vanishing of the cross cohomology gives the splitting and uniqueness by deformation theory of extensions.

For a fixed Frobenius lift, check at characteristic-zero points that the induced first block has scalar n₁-th Frobenius power and characteristic polynomial (X−(−1)^{n₁+1}det σ₁(φ))^{n₁}. Reducedness and p-torsion-freeness spread this polynomial identity. Reduce modulo ϖ. The determinant on inertia is then trivial because Θ has p-power order, so the reduced α is independent of the Frobenius lift. No Hensel root of α is needed, and no integral independence is claimed for n₁=1.
(4): on restriction to G_{L_ṽ} the type becomes trivial, so lifts are unramified.
acceptance: For n_1 = n the second summand is zero and Lemma 1.21 is vacuous; (3) says the n-th Frobenius power is scalar on the induced summand.

sources.match: Proves the splitting of lifts of σ̄_1 ⊕ σ̄_2 and the Frobenius and restriction properties of the fixed-type lifting ring.

nodes.title: The Iwahori–Hecke algebra of ramified U_{2k+1} is that of Sp_{2k}
nodes.statement: Let E/F be ramified quadratic of odd residue characteristic, U_{2k+1} the ramified quasi-split unitary group, B an Iwahori subgroup with Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_B, and B′ an Iwahori subgroup of split Sp_{2k}(F) with Λ′ ≅ ℤ^k spanned by ε′_i = diag(1, …, ϖ², …, ϖ^{−2}, …, 1). The identifications Λ ≅ Λ′ and W_0 ≅ W′_0 extend to an isomorphism of affine Weyl groups W ≅ W′ carrying the simple affine reflections s_0, …, s_k to those of Sp_{2k}, and induce an isomorphism H_B ≅ H_{B′} with [Bε_iB] ↦ [B′ε′_iB′].
hypotheses: E/F ramified, residue characteristic odd; both Hecke algebras with the same parameter q at every simple reflection.
proofSteps: Compute the affine root system of ramified U_{2k+1} (Tits) and check it matches that of Sp_{2k} with equal parameters at all simple reflections.

Use the Iwahori–Matsumoto multiplication rule T_s²=(q−1)T_s+q, equivalently (T_s−q)(T_s+1)=0, and braid relations on both sides. Over ℤ use the positive braid monoid presentation; a braid group presentation requires q invertible. This avoids the reversed quadratic relation and integral group-algebra presentation printed on CTIII p. 7.
acceptance: For k = 1 both algebras are the affine Hecke algebra of type Ã_1 with equal parameters q.
The generic-parameter Iwahori–Hecke algebras of SR.1.5 specialise to H_B and H_{B′} at the same q.

sources.match: Identifies the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of the ramified unitary group in 2k + 1 variables with that of split Sp_{2k}.

nodes.title: The Kazhdan–Lusztig modules X, Y, Z in the packet of St_{n−4} ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1
nodes.statement: For n = 2k + 1 ≥ 7, let Π_E = St_{n−4,E} ⊞ St_{3,E} ⊞ St_{1,E}, a tempered representation of GL_n(E) with conjugate orthogonal parameter φ_E extending uniquely to a parameter φ of U_n, and Π_φ its L-packet. Exponents [m_1, …, m_k] denote characters |·|^{m_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ |·|^{m_k} ⊗ 1 of the torus (E^×)^k × (E^×)^{N=1}. Through SP.4/iwahori-hecke-sp2k and the Kazhdan–Lusztig classification for PSp_{2k} (the partition (n − 4) + 3 + 1 of the dual SO_{2k+1}(ℂ), with component group {±1} for n = 7 and {±1}² otherwise, and the fixed-point variety B_u^s smooth and projective by De Concini–Lusztig–Procesi, hence paved by affine spaces by Białynicki-Birula's theorem), there are irreducible tempered Iwahori-spherical modules X, Y (n = 7) and X, Y, Z (n ≥ 9) with: for n = 7, dim X^P = dim X^B = 1, dim Y^B = 7, X^{norm}_{N_0} = [1, 0, −1], (Y^{norm}_{N_0})^{ss} = [1, 0, −1] + 2[1, 0, 1] + 4[1, 1, 0]; for n=9, dim X^B=1, dim Y^B=11, dim Z^B=2, jX=[2,1,0,−1], jY=[2,1,0,−1]+2[2,1,0,1]+4[2,1,1,0]+[1,0,2,1]+[1,2,0,1]+2[1,2,1,0], and jZ=[1,0,2,1]+[1,2,0,1], where j denotes the semisimplified normalized Jacquet module. For k≥5 let L_k be the multiset obtained by inserting 0 in positions 2 through k−1 of [1,k−2,k−3,…,1]. Then jX_k=[k−2,k−3,…,0,−1], jY_k=L_k+2[1,k−2,k−3,…,0]+prepend(k−2,jY_{k−1}), and jZ_k=L_k+prepend(k−2,jZ_{k−1}); the dimensions satisfy dim Y_k^B=dim Y_{k−1}^B+k and dim Z_k^B=dim Z_{k−1}^B+k−2. The packet Π_φ has exactly these members for n = 7 and one further non-Iwahori-spherical member W for n ≥ 9.
hypotheses: E/F ramified, odd residue characteristic; P the maximal parahoric containing B with [P : B] = q + 1.
Normalised Jacquet modules for the upper-triangular Borel.
proofSteps: Kazhdan–Lusztig: irreducible Iwahori-spherical tempered modules of PSp_{2k} ↔ pairs (u, ρ) with ρ a representation of the component group occurring in H_*(B_u^s); the Białynicki-Birula paving of the smooth projective variety B_u^s (De Concini–Lusztig–Procesi; Reeder for n ≥ 9) gives the dimensions and exponents (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroupsPartII SRU.7).
For n = 7: B_u^s = X_1 ⊔ X_2 ⊔ X_3 with X_1 two points (exponent [1, 0, −1]), X_2 ≅ ℙ¹ ([1, 0, 1]) and X_3 ≅ ℙ¹ × ℙ¹ ([1, 1, 0]); homology of dimension 8 = 1 + 7.
Membership in Π_φ: the stable base change of X, Y is semistable with θ-stable exponent forcing the parameter ⊕ sp(n_i) ⊗ χ_i to have trivial χ_i and {n_i} = {n − 4, 3, 1} (Clozel–Thorne III §3.5).
acceptance: n = 7: dim X^B + dim Y^B = 8 = dim H_*(B_u^s).
n = 9: dim X^B + dim Y^B + dim Z^B = 14.

sources.locator: §2.2 and Theorem 2.3, pp. 8–9; Theorem 2.5 and proof, pp. 10–11
sources.match: Defines the parameter φ_E and the packet Π_φ, states the Iwahori dimensions and Jacquet exponents of its members, and constructs X, Y, Z by Kazhdan–Lusztig through the Sp_{2k} Hecke algebra.
Shows the Kazhdan–Lusztig modules lie in the packet, and computes the Jacquet module of the U(4) packet.

uses.how: integral lattices in X^B, Y^B, Z^B with disjoint reductions

uses.where: Clozel–Thorne III, Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.2, pp. 35–37
uses.how: M ⊗ ℂ ≅ (X^B)^a ⊕ (Y^B)^b ⊕ (Z^B)^c at the level-raising place, and the count of exponents ≡ [2, 1, 0, −1]

nodes.title: Integral structures, localisations and duality for the Kazhdan–Lusztig modules
nodes.statement: Let l = n − 2 be prime (n ∈ {7, 9}), K/ℚ_l finite containing √q over which X, Y (and Z) are defined, with integers 𝒪 and residue field k. (Proposition 2.6) If q is a primitive root mod l there are H_{B,𝒪}-lattices X^B_𝒪, Y^B_𝒪 (and Z^B_𝒪) whose reductions have pairwise no common Jordan–Hölder factor; Y^B_𝒪 ⊗ k is absolutely irreducible. (Corollary 2.8) If q is a primitive root mod l, a finite flat H_{B,𝒪}-module M with M ⊗ K ≅ (X^B)^a ⊕ (Y^B)^b (⊕ (Z^B)^c) is the direct sum of its intersections with the isotypic parts. Let ȷ be the anti-involution [BgB] ↦ [Bg^{−1}B], 𝒪[Λ] the Bernstein subalgebra, and M(χ̄), M(χ̄ȷ) localisations at residual characters. (Proposition 2.9) If q ≡ −1 mod l, with χ̄ the reduction of the character of 𝒪[Λ] on X^B: X^B_K = X^B_K(χ̄) = X^B_K(χ̄ȷ), dim Y^P_K ∩ Y^B_K(χ̄) = dim Y^P_K ∩ Y^B_K(χ̄ȷ) = 1, and Z^B_K(χ̄) = 0 for n = 9. (Duality) Self-duality of Y_K gives a perfect K-valued pairing on Y^B_K with ⟨tx, y⟩ = ⟨x, ȷ(t)y⟩, under which Y^B_K(χ̄ȷ) annihilates the other localisations and (1 − e_P)Y^B_K annihilates Y^P_K; no integral perfect pairing is claimed.
hypotheses: Proposition 2.6 needs q a primitive root mod l; Proposition 2.9 needs q ≡ −1 mod l: these are different places (v_i and v_0 in SP.5).
e_P = [P]/(q + 1) exists over K but is not integral when q ≡ −1 mod l.
proofSteps: Proposition 2.6: write Y^B by explicit matrices for T_{s_i} and the Bernstein generators (Reeder's matrices); the n = 9 matrix T_{s_2} has a misprinted (10, 10) entry, which must be −1/(1 + q) (E7 of the extraction: the 2×2 block has trace q−1 and determinant −q after this correction, hence satisfies the Hecke quadratic relation; the remaining presentation relations are part of the explicit-matrix proof target); reduce and check irreducibility and disjointness.
Corollary 2.8: Brauer–Nesbitt for H_{B,𝒪}-lattices and disjointness of the reductions.
Proposition 2.9: compute the Bernstein-character exponents modulo l with q ≡ −1; duality from Theorem 3.3 (self-duality of Y_K).
acceptance: For n = 7, Y^B has rank 7 and its reduction is absolutely irreducible of dimension 7.
With q ≡ −1 mod l the X-isotypic part lies in both localisations; this asymmetry with Y (one-dimensional P-fixed parts) drives the count in SP.5/ct-level-raising.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.6, p. 12; Remark 2.7 and Corollary 2.8, p. 17; §2.3 and Proposition 2.9, pp. 17–18
sources.match: Constructs lattices with disjoint reductions under the primitive-root hypothesis, splits lattices into isotypic parts, defines the anti-involution and localisations, and computes the localisations when q ≡ −1 mod l.

nodes.title: Identification of the packet members and their endoscopic signs
nodes.statement: Suppose E/F ramified of odd residue characteristic and n = m + 4 with m ≥ 3 odd. The members X, Y (m = 3) or X, Y, Z (m ≥ 5) of Π_φ are semistable with the Jacquet exponents of SP.4/kazhdan-lusztig-modules (for m = 3, X has exponent [1, 0, −1], correcting the printed [1, 0, 1], E3 of the extraction), and W is not semistable. For m≥5, with the characters ε_1, ε_2 of the component group S_φ and ε = ε_1ε_2: ε(Y) = ε(Z) = 1, ε(X) = ε(W) = −1, ε_1(X) = ε_1(Y) = 1, ε_1(Z) = ε_1(W) = −1. For m=3 the component group has one nontrivial character ε, with ε(Y)=1 and ε(X)=−1; Z and W are absent.
hypotheses: Transfer factors on the maximally split torus normalised as in Lemma 3.6: Δ(t_H, t) = μ(z_1)μ(z_2)Δ_IV(t_H, t) for t_H = (t_0, z_1, z_2) ∈ U(m) × U(4).
proofSteps: Compute transfer factors on the maximally split torus (Δ_I = Δ_{III,1} = 1, Δ_II = 1 for trivial χ-data, Δ_IV the discriminant ratio) (Lemma 3.6).

Express traces through Jacquet modules on the regular part of the split torus ((3.8)) and compare the stable identity with the endoscopic identity Σ ε(π)⟨tr π, f⟩ = ⟨tr π_H, f^H⟩ for H = U(m) × U(4) ((3.7)): the right side is 2Σ_w w([k − 2, …, 1, 1, 0]) over shuffles, equal to jY − jX + jZ for m = 5; the U(4) packet of St_3 ⊞ St_1 has Jacquet module 2μ^{−1}(z_1z_2) ⊗ [1, 0].

The ε₁ computation uses Mœglin’s hereditary Jacquet formula. The printed uniqueness claim used to identify Z is false: the same exponent also gives Y in the relevant induced socle. A complete socle-multiplicity argument, followed by packet counting, is still needed; this is recorded in gap G4 rather than called an immediate repair.
acceptance: For m = 5 (n = 9, k = 4), Σ_π ε(π) j(π) = jY − jX + jZ, and the shuffle sum 2Σ_w w([2, 1, 1, 0]) matches it (the extraction's review checked k = 3, …, 8).

sources.locator: Theorem 3.3 and sign table, p. 21; §3.4, Lemma 3.6, pp. 23–24; §3.5, (3.7)–(3.8) and proof, pp. 24–27; Proposition 3.7, p. 27
sources.match: Identifies the Kazhdan–Lusztig modules with the Mœglin–Mok packet members, fixes their semistability and Jacquet exponents and computes the endoscopic signs through transfer factors on the split torus.

nodes.title: The data of Newton–Thorne I §4 for level raising to types
nodes.statement: Fix n = 2k + 1 ≥ 3 odd, the standard assumptions, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, and cuspidal conjugate self-dual π_2 on GL_2(𝔸_F) and π_{n−2} on GL_{n−2}(𝔸_F) with: (1) π = π_2 ⊞ π_{n−2} regular algebraic, with ρ̄ = r̄_{π,ι} = ρ̄_2 ⊕ ρ̄_{n−2}, ρ̄_2 = r̄_{π_2|·|^{(2−n)/2},ι}, ρ̄_{n−2} = r̄_{π_{n−2}|·|^{−1},ι}; (2) π ι-ordinary; (3) pairwise disjoint non-empty sets T_1, T_2, T_3 of places of F⁺ outside S of odd residue cardinality, π unramified outside S ∪ T: at v ∈ T_1, v inert, q_v of order 6 mod p, char k(v) > n, π_{2,ṽ} ≅ St_2(χ_ṽ), π_{n−2,ṽ} ≅ ⊞_{i=0}^{2k−2}χ_{ṽ,i} with χ_ṽ, χ_{ṽ,0} unramified and χ_{ṽ,i}|_{𝒪^×} = ω(ṽ) for i ≥ 1; at v ∈ T_2, v split, q_v ≡ −1 mod p, π_{2,ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ) and π_{n−2,ṽ} ⊇ ω(ṽ)∘det; at v ∈ T_3, v split, q_v of order n − 2 mod p, π_{n−2,ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ) and π_{2,ṽ} ⊇ ω(ṽ)∘det; and characters θ_v of C(k(v)) of order p for v ∈ T_1. The level is U = ∏U_v with U_v = ι_v^{−1}p_v (v ∈ T_1), ι_ṽ^{−1}𝔮_ṽ (v ∈ T_2 ∪ T_3), the ordinary Iwahori level at S_p and hyperspecial elsewhere outside S; the global types are τ_g = ⊗_{T_1}τ(v, n) ⊗ ⊗_{T_2∪T_3}λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) and λ_g = ⊗_{T_1}λ(v, θ_v, n) ⊗ ⊗_{T_2∪T_3}λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n), with 𝒪-lattices.
hypotheses: Standard assumptions of SP.4/unitary-groups-and-inner-twist; π tempered at every place (π_2, π_{n−2} are).

Choose the p-adic level sufficiently small that the finite double-coset stabilizers have order prime to p. This is the exactness hypothesis for changing integral coefficient types in the ordinary forms functor.
proofSteps: The data are assembled from SP.4/level-raising-types at T_1 and the split-place types λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) of GL_n (inflations of Deligne–Lusztig cuspidals of GL_{n_1}(k(ṽ)) for n_1 = 2, n − 2, with ω(ṽ)∘det on the complement).
acceptance: For n = 3, π_{n−2} = π_1 is a character and T_3 imposes an order-p character at a place with q_v ≡ 1 mod p (correction E19).

sources.locator: §4, data and assumptions before Theorem 4.1, pp. 59–60; the level U and types τ_g, λ_g, p. 62
sources.match: Fixes the isobaric sum π_2 ⊞ π_{n−2}, the auxiliary place sets T_1, T_2, T_3 with their local conditions, the level U and the global types τ_g and λ_g.

uses.where: Newton–Thorne I, Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.6, pp. 60–65

nodes.title: Local components at inert places and box sums with the same residual representation
nodes.statement: (Lemma 4.3) In the setting of SP.5/nt-level-raising-data, if v is inert in F then π_ṽ ∈ A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺ (π_ṽ is tempered because π_{2,ṽ} and π_{n−2,ṽ} are); consequently, for v ∈ T_1, χ_ṽ is the nontrivial unramified quadratic character and χ_{ṽ,0} is trivial. (Lemma 4.5) In the setting of SP.5/nt-level-raising-data, let π′ = π′_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ π′_r be regular algebraic with π′_i cuspidal conjugate self-dual, r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, and π′_ṽ|_{𝔮_ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) for v ∈ T_2 ∪ T_3. Then either π′ is cuspidal, or r = 2 and after reordering π′ has blocks of sizes n − 2 and 2 with the T_2, T_3 types distributed as for π and the same residual blocks ρ̄_{n−2}, ρ̄_2.
hypotheses: Bellaïche–Chenevier's sign of r_{π,ι} extends the local parameter to ^LU_n.
proofSteps: Lemma 4.3: the Galois representation of a conjugate self-dual π has the polarization sign that makes its parameter extend to ^LU_n at inert places (Bellaïche–Chenevier 2011); combine with SP.4/stable-base-change-packets and the sign condition for St_2(χ) ⊞ 1.

At T₃ the regular induced local type forces an entire (n−2)-dimensional local block into one isobaric constituent. Compare semisimplified residual inertia: the two residual blocks have respectively the quadratic and trivial inertial characters there, so this constituent contains the prescribed residual (n−2)-block, whether or not that block is globally irreducible. At T₂ the analogous comparison forces the residual two-dimensional block into a constituent of rank at least two. Thus only a single cuspidal constituent or the ranks (n−2,2) can occur. The proof does not assume global irreducibility of either residual block.
acceptance: A box sum with three blocks cannot carry both the T_2 and T_3 types and the residual representation ρ̄_2 ⊕ ρ̄_{n−2}.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.3 and Remark 4.4, p. 61; Lemma 4.5 and proof, p. 61
sources.match: Places local components at inert places in the conjugate self-dual tempered set extending to the L-group, and shows that box sums congruent to π with the T_2, T_3 types are cuspidal or of shape (n − 2, 2).

nodes.title: A form of the definite group with prescribed types, via the trace formula
nodes.statement: In the setting of SP.5/nt-level-raising-data, for every S ∪ T-split totally real quadratic L⁺/F⁺ (L = L⁺F), either there is an automorphic σ of G(𝔸_{F⁺}) with base change π, σ_v^{U_v} ≠ 0 for v ∉ T and σ_T|_{U_T} ⊇ τ_g, or there is such a σ of G(𝔸_{L⁺}) with base change π_L, σ_v^{U_{L,v}} ≠ 0 for v ∉ T_L and σ_{T_L}|_{U_{L,T_L}} ⊇ τ_{g,L}.
hypotheses: Setting of SP.5/nt-level-raising-data.
proofSteps: The stabilised trace formula for G gives Σ m(σ_i)σ_i(f) = ½(π̃(f̃) + (π_{n−2} ⊗ (π_2 ⊗ μ^{−1}∘det))~(f̃^{U_{n−2}×U_2})) for test functions f matching π (Shin Proposition 4.8, Mœglin–Waldspurger, Jacquet–Shalika, Hiraga Proposition 4.6; EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4).
With f built from τ_g at T and SP.4/endoscopic-character-identities elsewhere, the multiplicity is m(σ) = ½(∏ϵ ∏c_{τ_v} + ∏ϵ ∏d_{v,1}).
If it vanishes over F⁺, quadratic base change to L⁺ squares the local constants and gives m(σ) = ∏c_{τ_v}² ≠ 0.
acceptance: The multiplicity over F⁺ is the half-sum ½(∏ϵ ∏c_{τ_v} + ∏ϵ ∏d_{v,1}), which can vanish whatever the signs; then ∏c_{τ_v}² = ∏d_{v,1}², and over L⁺ the multiplicity is ∏c_{τ_v}² ≠ 0.

sources.match: Finds, by the stabilised trace formula and a quadratic base change if necessary, an automorphic representation of the definite group with base change π containing the type τ_g.

nodes.title: Level raising to a type on a definite unitary group (Newton–Thorne I Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: In the setting of SP.5/nt-level-raising-data, for every S ∪ T-split totally real quadratic L⁺/F⁺ with L = L⁺F there is a RACSDC automorphic representation Π of GL_n(𝔸_L) with (1) Π ι-ordinary, of the weight of π, and unramified outside S ∪ T; (2) r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}|_{G_L}; (3) for v ∈ T_{1,L}, Π_ṽ restricted to r_ṽ contains λ̃(ṽ, θ̃_{v|_{F⁺}}, n)|_{r_ṽ}; (4) for v ∈ T_{2,L} ∪ T_{3,L}, Π_ṽ|_{𝔮_ṽ} contains λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ|_F, n), with n_1 = 2 on T_{2,L} and n_1 = n − 2 on T_{3,L} (correction E14: the source prints n_2). This proves the odd-rank level-raising statement the parent records in §4.4.
hypotheses: The weight of Π is that of π (correction E23 makes this explicit).
proofSteps: SP.5/nt-prescribed-types gives σ (over F⁺ or L⁺) containing τ_g in σ_T.

The congruence of types (SP.4/level-raising-types) and exactness of the ordinary forms functor S^{ord}_λ(U, −) at l-torsion-free level (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2) give Σ with the same Hecke eigensystem mod p containing λ_g.

Its base change is cuspidal: SP.5/nt-local-components-and-box-sums allows only shape (n − 2, 2), which SP.4/type-transfer excludes at T_1 (identities (4.6.4)–(4.6.5)); T_2 ∪ T_3 serve to force cuspidality (Remark 4.2).
Ordinarity from the ordinary level at S_p; local–global compatibility gives (3)–(4).
acceptance: For n = 3 the conclusion produces a cuspidal RACSDC representation of GL_3 congruent to a GL_2 × GL_1 isobaric sum.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1, p. 60; Remark 4.2, p. 60; proof, pp. 64–65
sources.match: States and proves level raising from π_2 ⊞ π_{n−2} to a cuspidal RACSDC representation over a quadratic extension with the prescribed types at T_1, T_2, T_3.
