nodes.title: A conjugate-symplectic Hecke character with prescribed archimedean components
nodes.statement: For a CM extension E/F of a totally real field there is a continuous character μ : E^×\𝔸_E^× → ℂ^× with μ|_{𝔸_F^×} = ε_{E/F} (the quadratic character) and μ(z) = (z/z̄)^{1/2} for z ∈ E_w ≅ ℂ at every archimedean place w.
hypotheses: E/F CM.
proofSteps: On E^×𝔸_F^×E_∞^× prescribe the quadratic character on 𝔸_F^× and z/|z| at each complex place. The restrictions agree on intersections; the CM unit calculation lets one choose a compact open finite-idelic subgroup on which the prescription is trivial. The resulting character on a subgroup of the discrete quotient extends to the whole quotient because ℂ^× is divisible. Pullback gives a continuous Hecke character with exactly the required restriction and infinity type (CTIII proof of Lemma 3.4, pp. 21–22).
acceptance: For F = ℚ and E imaginary quadratic, μ is a Hecke character of ∞-type (1/2, −1/2) restricting to the quadratic character of E/ℚ.

sources.match: Constructs a conjugate-symplectic Hecke character of E with archimedean components (z/z̄)^{1/2} restricting to the quadratic character of E/F.

nodes.title: Counting automorphic representations of the definite unitary group with given base change
nodes.statement: Let G be the unitary group in n = l + 2 variables over F (l > 5 prime for Theorem 3.8; l = 5 is Theorem 3.10), split by the CM field E, compact at infinity and quasi-split at finite places, [F : ℚ] even. (Theorem 3.8(1)) For σ_1, σ_2 conjugate self-dual cuspidal on GL_4(𝔸_E), GL_m(𝔸_E) (m = l − 2) with σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 regular algebraic of infinity type ((l + 1)/2, …, (−1 − l)/2) and ∏_{v|∞}det(w_v) = 1, places v_0, …, v_s ramified in E of odd residue characteristic with σ_{1,w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_1 and σ_{2,w_i} ≅ St_m, and all other ramification split: there are exactly 4^{s+1}/2 automorphic representations of G(𝔸_F) with stable base change σ_1 ⊞ σ_2, each of multiplicity one, in bijection with tuples (σ_{v_i}) ∈ ∏Π_{φ_{v_i}} with ∏ε_{v_i}(σ_{v_i}) = 1. (Theorem 3.8(2)) For a RACSDC π with π_{w_i} ≅ St_m ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1 there are exactly 4^{s+1}, in bijection with ∏Π_{φ_{v_i}}. (Theorem 3.10) For l = 5 the counts are 2^s and 2^{s+1}. Stable base change holds for representations with trivial σ_∞.
hypotheses: The archimedean sign condition holds when every place above l splits in E with [F_v : ℚ_l] even and the representation is ι-ordinary (Remark 3.9).
proofSteps: Stabilise the trace formula for G with test functions that are pseudo-coefficients at infinity and Iwahori-level at the v_i (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.4).
Insert the stable and endoscopic local identities of SP.4/ct-packet-signs with the character μ of SP.5/ct-conjugate-symplectic-character in the L-embedding.
Mok's multiplicity formula (parent ML.4) gives multiplicity one and the sign condition.
acceptance: For s=0 and l>5 the endoscopic and cuspidal counts are respectively 2 and 4. For l=5 the corresponding two-member-packet counts are 1 and 2.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.8, pp. 28–29; Remark 3.9 and the remark after the proof, pp. 29–31; Theorem 3.10, pp. 31–32
sources.match: Counts automorphic representations of the definite unitary group with endoscopic or cuspidal stable base change, with multiplicity one and the sign condition, and records strong base change.

nodes.title: The set-up of Clozel–Thorne III §4: places, levels and algebraic modular forms
nodes.statement: Let l ≥ 5 be prime, ι : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ, E a CM field with totally real F such that every place v | l of F splits in E with [F_v : ℚ_l] even, and places v_0, …, v_s (s ≥ 1) of F ramified in E of odd residue characteristic with q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l and each q_{v_i} (i ≥ 1) a primitive root mod l, all other places unramified in E. Let n = l + 2, m = l − 2, G as in SP.5/ct-definite-unitary-count, and π_1, π_2 cuspidal conjugate self-dual on GL_m(𝔸_E), GL_4(𝔸_E) with π_{1,w_i} ≅ St_m, π_{2,w_i} ≅ St_3 ⊞ St_1, π = π_1 ⊞ π_2 regular algebraic, ι-ordinary of infinity type ((n − 1)/2, …, (1 − n)/2), r̄_ι(π) = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible and the tame inertia generator acting at w_i as a regular unipotent on ρ̄_1 and with Jordan type 3 + 1 on ρ̄_2. Levels: U_0 with P_{v_0} at v_0 and B_{v_i} at v_i (i ≥ 1), and U_1 = U_0 except B_{v_0} at v_0, so [U_0 : U_1] = q_{v_0} + 1. S(U, A) is the module of A-valued functions on G(F)\G(𝔸_F^∞)/U, with Hecke algebra T(U, 𝒪) generated by the spherical operators at split places and the U_v^j at v | l; 𝔪 and 𝔪^∨ are the maximal ideals of σ and σ^∨.
hypotheses: Weight zero; ordinary parts at the places above l as in PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2.

Choose U away from v₀ sufficiently small for p-integral exactness and the unweighted double-coset pairing. Fix an ordinary automorphic σ with base change π₁⊞π₂, supplied by ct-definite-unitary-count, to define 𝔪; impose the prescribed local invariants at the other places.
proofSteps: Assemble from PL.2 (algebraic modular forms and Hecke algebras on definite unitary groups) with Iwahori level at the ramified places.

sources.match: Fixes the fields, the ramified places v_0, …, v_s with their congruence conditions, the isobaric sum π_1 ⊞ π_2, the levels U_0 ⊃ U_1 and the algebraic modular forms with their Hecke algebras and maximal ideals.

nodes.title: Local types of representations contributing to S(U_1, 𝒪)_𝔪
nodes.statement: In the set-up SP.5/ct-level-raising-setup, if Σ contributes to S(U_1, 𝒪)_𝔪 and Π is its stable base change to GL_n(𝔸_E), then Π is ι-ordinary and its components at the places above v_0, …, v_s are semistable; moreover either (1) Π_{w_i} ≅ St_m ⊞ St_3 ⊞ St_1 for every i, or (2) for some i the monodromy of r_ι(Π) at w_i has Jordan type (n − 2) + 1 + 1 or n, and Π is cuspidal.
hypotheses: Set-up of SP.5/ct-level-raising-setup.
proofSteps: Semistability: from Σ c(σ)⟨tr σ, f_v⟩ = ⟨tr π_w × I_c, f_{E_w}⟩ with c(σ) > 0 and the twisted Jacquet trace (correcting the proof of Clozel–Thorne II Lemma 4.3).

Residual monodromy has Jordan types m and 3 + 1; the closure order on nilpotent classes (dim ker N^j ≤ dim ker N̄^j), Mok's parity condition and quadratic characters ≡ 1 mod λ leave only the listed possibilities.
acceptance: The original π = π_1 ⊞ π_2 itself falls in case (1).

sources.match: Shows the base change of a contributing representation is ordinary and semistable at the v_i, and either has the original local types everywhere or is cuspidal with a larger Jordan block at some w_i.

nodes.title: The pairing on S(U_1) and the module structure at the level-raising place
nodes.statement: The pairing ⟨f, g⟩ = Σ_{x∈G(F)\G(𝔸_F^∞)/U_1} f(x)g(x) on S(U_1, 𝒪) satisfies ⟨af, g⟩ = ⟨f, ȷ(a)g⟩ for a ∈ H_{B_{v_0},𝒪} and induces (1) perfect pairings S(U_1, 𝒪)_𝔪 × S(U_1, 𝒪)_{𝔪^∨} → 𝒪 and mod l; (2) a pairing vanishing on S(U_0, k)_𝔪 × S(U_0, k)_{𝔪^∨}, because q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod l; (3) a perfect pairing M × N → 𝒪 whose reduction vanishes on M^{U_0} ⊗ k × N^{U_0} ⊗ k, for M the intersection of the R_i^{B_{v_i}}-isotypic parts of S(U_1, 𝒪)_𝔪 and N the intersection of the (R_i^∨)^{B_{v_i}}-isotypic parts of S(U_1, 𝒪)_{𝔪^∨} (N is not defined in the source, E14). (Lemma 4.4) If no contributing representation falls in case (2) of SP.5/ct-contributing-local-types, then M ⊗ ℂ ≅ (X^B)^a ⊕ (Y^B)^b ⊕ (Z^B)^c ≅ N ⊗ ℂ as H_{B_{v_0}}-modules with a > b = c ≥ 0. For l=5 omit Z and c; the conclusion is a>b≥0 for the X,Y multiplicities.
hypotheses: l ∤ #U_1-stabilisers (U_1 sufficiently small).
proofSteps: Perfectness from the finite double-coset sum and smallness of U_1 (as in Clozel–Thorne II Proposition 4.5).
Vanishing on U_0-invariants: the P_{v_0}-averaging multiplies the pairing by [U_0 : U_1] = q_{v_0} + 1 ≡ 0 mod l.
Lemma 4.4: endoscopic base changes contribute only X at v_0 (SP.5/ct-definite-unitary-count), cuspidal ones X, Y, Z; the endoscopic set is non-empty because of π_1 ⊞ π_2.
acceptance: If U_1 = U_0 (no level raising at v_0), the pairing would not vanish mod l: the vanishing uses q_{v_0} + 1 ≡ 0 mod l.

sources.match: Proves perfectness of the pairing on the localised forms of level U_1 and its vanishing modulo l on U_0-invariants, and describes M ⊗ ℂ as an Iwahori–Hecke module.

nodes.title: Level raising for l = 5 and l = 7 (Clozel–Thorne III Theorem 4.2)
nodes.statement: In the set-up SP.5/ct-level-raising-setup with l = 5 or l = 7, there is an automorphic representation Σ of G(𝔸_F) contributing to S(U_1, 𝒪)_𝔪 whose stable base change is cuspidal with monodromy of Jordan type (n − 2) + 1 + 1 or n at some w_i (case (2) of SP.5/ct-contributing-local-types).
hypotheses: l ∈ {5, 7}; the count fails for l > 7 since Z(χ̄) ≠ 0 (Remark 4.5).
proofSteps: Suppose every contributing base change has the original monodromy. Choose local packet members at v_i (i≥1) with product of signs −1. For l=7 the endoscopic contributors supply X at v₀ and cuspidal contributors supply X⊕Y⊕Z, yielding multiplicities a>b=c. For l=5 the packet has X,Y only and gives a>b.

Let M,N be the dual-type lattices of ct-pairing. The perfect pairing restricts to M(χ̄)×N(χ̄ȷ). Proposition 2.9 gives rank a+3b for each, and their P-fixed sublattices have rank a+b. For l=7 use the exponent [2,1,0,−1]; for l=5 use [1,0,−1]. Z contributes nothing to these localizations in the l=7 case.

Modulo l the two P-fixed subspaces annihilate one another by ct-pairing. In a perfect pairing between spaces of dimension a+3b, this forces 2(a+b)≤a+3b, hence a≤b, a contradiction. No self-pairing or self-isotropic identification of M and N is used.
acceptance: For l = 5 the count compares ranks a + b and a + 3b of modules over H_{B_{v_0}} for n = 7.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.2, p. 35; proof, pp. 35–37; Remark 4.5, p. 37
sources.match: Proves level raising at v_0 for l = 5, 7 by an isotropy count in the localised Iwahori–Hecke module.

nodes.title: Schur and primitive residual representations after split extensions; cuspidal soluble base change
nodes.statement: In the setting of Newton–Thorne I §6 (r̄ = r̄_{π,ι} a sum of characters χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n as in SP.6/nt-steinberg-level-raising), choose Y_a so that Y_a-split finite CM extensions L/F are linearly disjoint from the field cut out by r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}}. Then for such L: (1) the polarized extension r̄^{pol}:G_{F⁺}→𝒢_n(k), restricted to G_{L⁺(ζ_p)}, is Schur; (2) r̄|_{G_L} is primitive; (3) if L/F is soluble the base change of π to L is cuspidal; (4) more generally, for L/F_0/F with L/F_0 soluble and Π RACSDC on GL_n(𝔸_{F_0}) with r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ r̄|_{G_{F_0}}, the base change of Π to L is cuspidal. (Lemma 6.3) There are infinitely many places ṽ_a of F prime to S, not split in F(ζ_p), with r̄(Frob_{ṽ_a}) scalar.
hypotheses: Hypotheses (1)–(5) of SP.6/nt-steinberg-level-raising.
proofSteps: (1)–(2): the ratios χ_i/χ_j have large order on G_{F(ζ_p)} and stay distinct after disjoint extensions (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.6, Schur and primitive representations, sums of characters with large ratios).
(3)–(4): a non-cuspidal cyclic base change would make the Galois representation induced (Arthur–Clozel Theorems 4.2, 5.1, Proposition 4.4; Clozel's purity lemma), contradicting primitivity.
Lemma 6.3: Chebotarev with τ = τ_0τ_0^c where ε(τ_0)² ≠ 1.
acceptance: If two characters χ_i, χ_j agree on G_{L(ζ_p)}, r̄|_{G_L} fails to be Schur; the order hypothesis on χ_i/χ_j prevents this.

sources.match: Proves Schur and primitivity properties after split extensions, cuspidality of soluble base changes, and the existence of auxiliary places with scalar residual Frobenius.

nodes.title: Deformation data with Steinberg and fixed-type local conditions
nodes.statement: A deformation datum D = (L, {R_v}_{v∈X}) consists of a soluble CM extension L/F, split at the auxiliary sets (Y_a ∪ S̃_a in Newton–Thorne I §6; the set V_0 ∪ S_a of a good extension in Clozel–Thorne III §5), a set X of places of L⁺ away from p, and for each v ∈ X a local lifting ring R_v: the fixed-type ring R(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, r̄|_{G_{L_ṽ}}) of SP.4/fixed-type-lifting-rings, the unipotent ring R^1_v, the Steinberg ring R^{St}_v (q_v ≡ 1 mod p and r̄ trivial at v), a ring R^{χ_v}_v of fixed characters, or the partition ring R^m_v cut out by det(X−ρ(φ_v))∈Pol_n(m,q_v): its Frobenius polynomial is a product of q_v-strings of lengths given by m. This is a Frobenius-polynomial condition, not an upper bound on the Jordan type of monodromy; at pure points the monodromy partition is m. Attached are the global polarized deformation problem 𝒮_D with ordinary conditions R^Δ_v at p over the Iwasawa algebra Λ_L, its universal ring R_D, the pseudodeformation subring P_D ⊂ R_D (R_D finite over P_D), the localised ordinary Hecke algebra 𝕋_D, the surjection P_D → 𝕋_D with kernel J_D (and J_D R_D) when every R_v is a fixed-type ring, R^1_v or R^{χ_v}_v (in Newton–Thorne I: when no R_v is R^{St}_v; Clozel–Thorne III: when every R_v is R^{χ_v}_v), and the reducible quotient R_D^{red}. When every R_v is a fixed-type, R^{χ_v}_v, unipotent or Steinberg ring (not a partition ring R^m_v), every irreducible component of R_D has dimension at least 1 + n[L⁺ : ℚ] = dim Λ_L (Newton–Thorne I Lemma 6.4; Clozel–Thorne III §5.1); for partition rings only the bound on R_D^{red} of SP.6/ct-reducible-locus is used.
hypotheses: Newton–Thorne I: n ≥ 3 odd and p > 2n; Clozel–Thorne III: n ≥ 2, l > 3 with l ∤ n_1n_2n; X is a set of places of L⁺ (correction E26).
proofSteps: The objects Λ_L, 𝒮_D, R_D, P_D, 𝕋_D, J_D, R_D^{red} are those of Thorne 2015, planned in PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2 (ordinary deformation datum), PL.6 (pseudodeformation subring, reducibility ideal) and PL.7; this node packages the local conditions used for level raising.
Dimension bound: Thorne 2015 Proposition 3.9 with Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 2.1.7 and the dimensions of the local rings (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7, partition rings).
acceptance: For X empty, R_D is the ordinary deformation ring of r̄|_{G_{L⁺}} with no additional partition or type places in X; the global finite ramification set and its auxiliary unrestricted local conditions remain part of the datum.

sources.match: Defines deformation data with fixed-type, unipotent and Steinberg local rings, the attached global problem and ring, and bounds the dimension of its components.

sources.locator: §5.1, deformation data, preliminary reductions and the objects of Thorne 2015, pp. 38–40
sources.match: Defines deformation data with characters, unipotent, Steinberg and partition rings over good soluble extensions, after preliminary reductions.

nodes.title: The Hecke comparison and a generic prime unramified outside p
nodes.statement: (Lemma 6.6) With 𝕋_D = 𝕋^{ord}(D)_{𝔪_D} and P_D ⊂ R_D as in SP.6/steinberg-deformation-data, if R_v ≠ R^{St}_v for all v ∈ X there is a natural surjection P_D → 𝕋_D of Λ_L-algebras. (Lemma 6.7) There are a deformation datum D_1 = (L_1, ∅) with 𝕋_{D_1} ≠ 0 and a generic prime 𝔭_1 ⊂ R_{D_1} of dimension 1 and characteristic p with J_{D_1} ⊂ 𝔭_1 and r_{𝔭_1}|_{G_{L_1,v_{St}}} trivial. The auxiliary field is L_0 = M_d·F with M_d/F⁺ cyclic totally real of odd degree d > n + n², split at R, Y_a and S_a and totally inert at S_p.
hypotheses: Setting of SP.6/nt-steinberg-level-raising.
proofSteps: Lemma 6.6: Galois representations r_σ over the rings A_c (Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemmas 2.1.5, 2.1.7), as in Thorne 2015 Proposition 4.12.

Lemma 6.7: choose L_0 so that the anti-cyclotomic unit rank at each R_i exceeds n + n² (Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 7.1, Maire Proposition 19; the source's multiplicity-one claim must be applied to one place of R_i, correction E22); then Newton–Thorne I Theorem 1.4 and the generic-prime theorem PL.7 (Theorem 5.7) at L_0, then pass to L_1 where the types become unramified (SP.4/fixed-type-lifting-rings (4)) and Thorne 2015 Proposition 4.18.
acceptance: The chosen prime is in the characteristic-p special fibre by the generic-prime construction. Finiteness of the Hecke algebra over Λ alone would not force an arbitrary prime to have characteristic p.

sources.locator: Lemma 6.6, p. 79; Lemma 6.7 and proof, pp. 80–82
sources.match: Constructs the surjection from the pseudodeformation ring to the ordinary Hecke algebra and finds a dimension-one generic prime of characteristic p, trivial at the Steinberg place.

nodes.title: Level raising to Steinberg by Galois deformation theory (Newton–Thorne I Theorem 6.1)
nodes.statement: Under the standard assumptions, let n ≥ 3 be odd, p > 2n, and π RACSDC on GL_n(𝔸_F) with (1) π ι-ordinary; (2) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1; (3) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n with χ_i^c = χ_i^∨ε^{1−n} and χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} of order > 2n; (4) r̄_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_ṽ}} trivial and [F_ṽ : ℚ_p] > n(n − 1)/2 + 1 for v ∈ S_p; (5) R = R_1 ⊔ R_2 ⊂ S − S_p with R_1 and R_2 both non-empty and of odd residue characteristic, π_ṽ|_{𝔮_ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) (n_1 = 3, q_v of order 3 mod p, on R_1; n_1 = n − 2, q_v of order n − 2, on R_2), each Θ_ṽ of order p, and (5)(d): for each non-trivial decomposition r̄_{π,ι} = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 there is i ∈ {1, 2} such that at every v ∈ R_i both ρ̄_1|_{G_{F_ṽ}} and ρ̄_2|_{G_{F_ṽ}} have a non-trivial unramified subquotient. For a place v_{St} above S − (S_p ∪ R) with q_{v_{St}} ≡ 1 mod p and r̄ trivial there, there is a RACSDC ι-ordinary π′ on GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, HT_τ(r_{π′,ι}) = HT_τ(r_{π,ι}) for all τ, and π′_{v_{St}} an unramified twist of Steinberg.
hypotheses: Standing assumptions of Newton–Thorne I §1 and §6; in applications R_1, R_2 are the sets T_1, T_3 of SP.5/nt-level-raising-data.

In the residually reducible inputs, primitive means weakly primitive in the source sense, tested over the algebraic closure of the residual field. Choose a common finite splitting field for every subgroup of the residual image before fixing integral coefficient rings. The PL.6 normalization coefficient condition then holds; no implication from arbitrary finite-field primitivity to geometric primitivity is assumed.
proofSteps: SP.6/nt-generic-prime gives a generic prime 𝔭_1 of R_{D_1} containing J_{D_1}, trivial at v_{St}.

The source labels D_{1,a} Steinberg at v_{St} and D_{1,b} unipotent there. Work first in the unipotent ambient problem, to which the generic Hecke-kernel theorem applies at the prime trivial at v_{St}. The Steinberg quotient meets this prime, and the local dimension bound produces a component of the expected dimension in that quotient. Character-sum finiteness and generic propagation then produce an automorphic characteristic-zero point on the Steinberg component.

Geraghty Lemma 2.25 and Theorem 1.2 (ordinary R = T) give an automorphic π″ on that component, Steinberg at v_{St}; SP.6/nt-schur-primitive-base-change and the prescribed-type lifts of PL.7 (Proposition 5.8) descend to F.
acceptance: For n = 3 the theorem raises the level of a residually reducible RACSDC representation of GL_3 to Steinberg at a place with q ≡ 1 mod p.

nodes.title: The reducible locus with Steinberg-type conditions
nodes.statement: Under the standing hypotheses of Clozel–Thorne III §5.1, fix a partition m with m_1 > n_1 = dim ρ̄_1 and a deformation datum D = (L, {R_v}_{v∈R_0} ∪ {R^m_v}_{v∈R_1}) with R_v ∈ {R^1_v, R^{St}_v, R^m_v} at every v ∈ R_0 (v ∤ l, q_v ≡ 1 mod l; this restriction to unipotent conditions is E21 of the extraction, and the only application has R_0 = ∅). Let Δ (resp. Δ′) be the Galois group of the maximal abelian l-extension of L unramified outside l (resp. also split at R̃_1 ∪ R̃_1^c) and d = dim_{ℚ_l} ker(Δ ⊗ ℚ_l → Δ′ ⊗ ℚ_l)^{c=−1}. (Lemma 5.3) dim R_D^{red} ≤ 1 + n[L⁺ : ℚ] − d, and R_D^{red} is finite over Λ_L. (Lemma 5.4) For D with R^m_v at the places above v_0 (m the Jordan type of N in rec^T(Π_{w_0})) and D′ with R^1_v there, dim R_D/J_{D′}R_D = dim Λ_L.
hypotheses: Standing hypotheses of §5.1, including potential ordinary automorphy of ρ̄_1, ρ̄_2 (hypothesis (4) of SP.6/ct-steinberg-level-raising).
proofSteps: For every distribution of ordinary characters between the two residual blocks, the fixed-determinant ordinary block deformation rings are finite over their weight algebras. Let A be their completed tensor product and adjoin universal determinant-twist characters Ψ₁,Ψ₂ to parametrize reducible deformations. One cannot identify arbitrary block deformations with the residual blocks tensored by characters.

After quotienting by the maximal ideal of A, the blocks become r̄₁⊗Ψ₁ and r̄₂⊗Ψ₂. The partition Frobenius-polynomial condition with m₁>n₁ forces a common eigenvalue of the two blocks, hence Ψ₁(Frob_ṽ)−Ψ₂(Frob_ṽ) is nilpotent at v∈R₁. The anti-invariant class-field rank d then gives the asserted dimension loss and finiteness.

For Lemma 5.4, use the pure automorphic point furnished by Π and the unique-component assertion of Lemma 5.2: its local component is retained by the partition quotient. Combined with the Λ-finite ordinary Hecke algebra and the lower component-dimension bound, this gives dim R_D/J_{D′}R_D=dim Λ_L. Finiteness alone is only an upper bound.
acceptance: If m = (1, …, 1) (unramified condition) the shared-eigenvalue argument gives nothing and the bound is not claimed.

sources.match: Bounds the dimension of the reducible locus of a deformation ring with a partition condition by the rank of anti-cyclotomic units split at the chosen places, and computes the dimension of the quotient by J_{D′}.

nodes.title: Changing characters, and a characteristic-l prime giving a Steinberg lift
nodes.statement: (Lemma 5.5) For D_0^χ = (L_0, {R^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R}) with pairwise distinct χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} at each v ∈ R, and a good L ⊃ L_0 on which every χ_{v,i} is unramified above R, the datum D = (L, ∅) has R_D ← P_D → 𝕋_D compatible with R^{nil}_{D_0^χ} ← P^{nil}_{D_0^χ} → 𝕋_{D_0^χ}. (Lemma 5.6) Suppose D = (L, ∅) and a dimension-one prime 𝔭 ⊂ R_D of characteristic l satisfy: (1) r_𝔭 : G_L → GL_n(Frac A) absolutely irreducible (A the normalisation of R_D/𝔭); (2) the characters ψ_1^v, …, ψ_n^v of I_{L_ṽ} (v ∈ S_{l,L}) pairwise distinct; (3) for some v ∈ S_{l,L} some σ ∈ I_{L_ṽ} with r_𝔭(σ) having eigenvalues λ₁,…,λ_n satisfying ∏λ_i^{a_i}=1 only when every a_i=0 (multiplicative ℤ-independence); (4) J_D ⊂ 𝔭; (5) r_𝔭|_{G_{L_ũ}} trivial for some u ∈ T_L − (S_{l,L} ∪ S_{a,L}). Then there is an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π_1 of GL_n(𝔸_L) with r̄_ι(Π_1) ≅ r̄_ι(Π)|_{G_L} and Π_{1,ũ} an unramified twist of Steinberg.
hypotheses: n_1 ≠ n_2 and n_1n_2 even (needed for soluble base change and descent for G, Clozel–Thorne I Proposition 2.9).

In the residually reducible inputs, primitive means weakly primitive in the source sense, tested over the algebraic closure of the residual field. Choose a common finite splitting field for every subgroup of the residual image before fixing integral coefficient rings. The PL.6 normalization coefficient condition then holds; no implication from arbitrary finite-field primitivity to geometric primitivity is assumed.
proofSteps: Lemma 5.5: soluble base change and descent for the definite group (Clozel–Thorne I Proposition 2.9; PL.6, twisting and base change for residually reducible rings).

The independent inertial eigenvalues make 𝔭 a generic prime. Add a Steinberg condition at the place where r_𝔭 is trivial and compare its components with the unipotent ambient problem. The generic Hecke-kernel theorem and the local dimension bound give an automorphic characteristic-zero point on a Steinberg component; independence does not assert uniqueness of that local component.
acceptance: Without (5) the lift need not be Steinberg anywhere; (5) places the Steinberg condition at u.

sources.match: Compares deformation rings and Hecke algebras after removing characters by base change, and derives a Steinberg automorphic lift from a suitable characteristic-l prime containing J_D.

nodes.title: Level raising to Steinberg for residually reducible representations (Clozel–Thorne III Theorem 5.1)
nodes.statement: Let E be imaginary CM, n ≥ 2, and Π RACSDC on GL_n(𝔸_E) with r̄_ι(Π) = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2, ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible, non-isomorphic, ρ̄_i^c ≅ ρ̄_i^∨ε^{1−n}, n_1 > n_2, r̄_ι(Π) primitive, and a place w_0 where Π_{w_0} is Iwahori-spherical and the monodromy N of rec^T(Π_{w_0}) has a Jordan block of length > n_1. Assume (1) Π ι-ordinary; (2) l > 3, l ∤ n_1n_2n, n_1n_2 even; (3) each ρ̄_i|_{G_{E(ζ_l)}} adequate and E(ζ_l) ⊄ the fixed field of ad r̄_ι(Π); (4) a CM E_0/E linearly disjoint from the extension of E(ζ_l) cut out by r̄_ι(Π) and ι-ordinary RAECSDC (π_i, χ_i) of GL_{n_i}(𝔸_{E_0}) with r̄_ι(π_i) ≅ ρ̄_i|_{G_{E_0}}. Then there are a soluble CM E_1/E linearly disjoint from that extension and an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π_1 on GL_n(𝔸_{E_1}) with r̄_ι(Π_1) ≅ r̄_ι(Π)|_{G_{E_1}} and Π_{1,w_1} an unramified twist of Steinberg at a place w_1 | w_0.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (4) and the standing assumptions as corrected in the extraction.

In the residually reducible inputs, primitive means weakly primitive in the source sense, tested over the algebraic closure of the residual field. Choose a common finite splitting field for every subgroup of the residual image before fixing integral coefficient rings. The PL.6 normalization coefficient condition then holds; no implication from arbitrary finite-field primitivity to geometric primitivity is assumed.
proofSteps: Preliminary reductions by soluble base change (SP.6/steinberg-deformation-data).

The reducible-locus bound gives an absolutely irreducible generic representation r_{𝔭₀}. Over a good Galois extension the two residual blocks remain absolutely irreducible. If r_{𝔭₀} became reducible after that restriction, Clifford theory gives a transitive set of conjugate constituents of equal dimension. Their residual semisimplifications distribute the two residual irreducible blocks, and transitivity would force n₁=n₂. This contradicts the hypothesis. Thus the restricted generic representation is absolutely irreducible; no unproved primitivity of r_{𝔭₀} is needed.
SP.6/ct-steinberg-prime then gives the Steinberg lift.
acceptance: The hypothesis n_1 > n_2 with a Jordan block longer than n_1 excludes Π_{w_0} unramified.

sources.match: States and proves level raising to Steinberg for an ordinary RACSDC representation with two residual constituents and a long Jordan block, by the dimension of the reducible locus and a generic prime.

nodes.title: Automorphy lifting from a lift with a long Jordan block (Clozel–Thorne III Theorem 5.7)
nodes.statement: Let E be CM and ρ : G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l) continuous with (1) ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ε^{1−n}; (2) finitely many ramified places; (3) ρ ordinary of weight λ; (4) l > 3 and E(ζ_l) ⊄ the field cut out by ad ρ̄; (5) ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_i|_{G_{E(ζ_l)}} adequate, n_1 ≠ n_2, n_1n_2 even, l ∤ n_1n_2(n_1 + n_2), ρ̄ primitive; (6) a place w_0 ∤ l with ρ|^{ss}_{G_{E_{w_0}}} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n ψε^{n−i}, ψ unramified; (7) an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π with r̄_ι(Π) ≅ ρ̄ whose monodromy at w_0 has a Jordan block of length > max(n_1, n_2); (8) hypothesis (4) of SP.6/ct-steinberg-level-raising. Then ρ ≅ r_ι(π) for a RACSDC π on GL_n(𝔸_E).
hypotheses: As in SP.6/ct-steinberg-level-raising.

The PL.6 normalization coefficient condition then holds; no implication from arbitrary finite-field primitivity to geometric primitivity is assumed.
proofSteps: SP.6/ct-steinberg-level-raising gives Π_1 Steinberg at w_1 | w_0 over a soluble E_1.

Thorne's residually reducible automorphy lifting with a Steinberg place (Thorne 2015 Theorem 7.1; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.7) shows ρ|_{G_{E_1}} automorphic; soluble descent returns to E.
acceptance: The unramified direct sum ⊕_{i=1}^nψε^{n−i} satisfies (6) with N=0. Thus (6) alone does not force Steinberg monodromy; the automorphic long-block witness (7) is essential.

nodes.title: Level raising to an ordinary Steinberg lift by p-adic methods (Thorne 2024 Theorem 6.11)
nodes.statement: Let F = F⁺F_0 be CM with F_0 imaginary quadratic and F/F⁺ everywhere unramified, p and q primes split in F_0, v_0 a q-adic place of F⁺ and ṽ_0 the place of F above v_0 and a fixed q-adic place u_0 of F_0, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. Let n = n_1 + n_2 and π_1, π_2 cuspidal conjugate self-dual on GL_{n_1}(𝔸_F), GL_{n_2}(𝔸_F) with π = π_1 ⊞ π_2 regular algebraic and ι-ordinary, such that (1) π is ramified only at places split over F⁺; (2) writing λ_{i,τ} for the dominant weight of π_i|·|^{(n_i−n)/2}, for each embedding τ₀:F₀→ℂ and each pair of dominant weights (μ₁,μ₂), the number of τ:F→ℂ restricting to τ₀ and satisfying (λ_{1,τ},λ_{2,τ})=(μ₁,μ₂) is even; (3) at some finite place w ∉ S split over F⁺, r̄_ι(π)|^{ss}_{G_{F_w}} ≅ ⊕χ̄_i with unramified residual characters χ̄_i and χ̄_i/χ̄_j ≠ ε̄ for i ≠ j; (4) π_{1,ṽ_0} ≅ St_{n_1}(ψ_1), π_{2,ṽ_0} ≅ St_{n_2}(ψ_2) with ψ_1, ψ_2 unramified and ι^{−1}(ψ_1ψ_2^{−1}|·|^{−n/2}) valued in 1 + 𝔪_{ℤ̄_p}; (5) π is unramified at the q-adic places not above v_0. Then there is an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_ι(Π) ≅ r̄_ι(π) and Π_{ṽ_0} an unramified twist of St_n, unramified at the other q-adic places and ramified only at places split over F⁺.
hypotheses: S is a finite set of places of F⁺ containing S_p, v₀ and the places below ramification of π, with no other q-adic places. Choose the genericity place w outside S.

The missing §§3–5 input is concentration of the Hecke-localized derived tensor RΓ_c(Ω^{n−1},k)⊗^L_{k[GL_n(F_{w₀})^0]}A_𝔪 in degree n−1 under residual genericity, together with Steinberg detection and the automorphic-forms comparison. It is not a concentration assertion for bare RΓ_c(Ω^{n−1},k). Gap G3 names its owner boundary.
proofSteps: Suppose not; Thorne's Proposition 6.5 gives a maximal ideal 𝔪 of the Hecke algebra in the support of the p-adic forms S(K^p, k) with the residual eigensystem of π.

Theorem 5.2 gives concentration of the Hecke-localized derived tensor with the automorphic module, using the residual genericity place. Lifting to O and using Theorem 3.4 shows that a nonzero middle-degree part would detect a Steinberg constituent, contrary to the assumed absence. Hence the whole tensor vanishes, and Corollary 6.3 yields the twisted Hom-space vanishing (6.4) at every weight.

Choose an anticyclotomic ψ≡1 with the Frobenius value in Lemma 6.10 and twist the first block only: (r_{π₁|·|^{(n₁−n)/2}}⊗ψ)⊕r_{π₂|·|^{(n₂−n)/2}}. Propositions 6.7 and 6.9 reduce its local constituents to Steinberg or the specified two-block constituent; either gives nonzero derived Hom in a degree forbidden by (6.4), completing the contradiction.
acceptance: For n_1 = n_2 = 1 condition (4) says ψ_1ψ_2^{−1}|·|^{−1} ≡ 1 modulo 𝔪 at ṽ_0, the classical level-raising congruence for GL_2, in conjugate self-dual form.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.11 and its assumptions, pp. 39–40; proof, pp. 40–41; Lemma 6.10, p. 39
sources.match: States and proves level raising from an ordinary isobaric sum, Steinberg at ṽ_0 on each block, to an ordinary RACSDC representation Steinberg at ṽ_0, by the vanishing of a tensor product with the cohomology of the Drinfeld space.

nodes.title: The CM newform σ_0 of weight 5 and level Γ_1(4)
nodes.statement: σ_0 is the cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) attached to the normalised newform f_0 = q − 4q² + 16q⁴ − 14q⁵ − 64q⁸ + ⋯ of level Γ_1(4) and weight 5, the automorphic induction from K = ℚ(i) of the unramified Hecke character ψ_∞ of ∞-type (4, 0) (on ideals, (α) ↦ α^4 for α ∈ ℤ[i], independent of the generator because units have fourth power 1). For p ≡ 1 mod 4, σ_0 is ι-ordinary, r_{σ_0,ι} ≅ Ind_{G_K}^{G_ℚ}ψ for the p-adic avatar ψ, and det r_{σ_0,ι} = δ_{K/ℚ}ε^{−4}.
hypotheses: K = ℚ(i); p ≡ 1 mod 4 for ordinarity.
proofSteps: a_ℓ(f_0) = α^4 + ᾱ^4 for a prime ℓ = αᾱ ≡ 1 mod 4, a_ℓ = 0 for ℓ ≡ 3 mod 4, a_2 = (1 + i)^4 = −4.

Automorphic induction of a Hecke character of an imaginary quadratic field (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer, parent ML.5 automorphic induction register); ordinarity at split p because ψ_∞ has ∞-type (4, 0).
acceptance: a_5 = (2 + i)^4 + (2 − i)^4 = −14, matching the q-expansion.

nodes.title: Properties of the residual symmetric powers of σ_0
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 3, p ≡ 1 mod 48n!, ω : G_K → Q̄_p^× de Rham with ωω^c = ε³, F/K a finite CM extension linearly disjoint from the extension of K(ζ_p) cut out by r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_{K(ζ_p)}}, and χ_i = ω̄^{n−1}ψ̄^{n−i}(ψ̄^c)^{i−1}, so ρ̄ = ⊕χ_i ≅ ω̄^{n−1} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_K}. Then (1) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1; (2) ψ̄/ψ̄^c|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has order > 2n(n − 1) and χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} order > 2n; (3) χ_iχ_i^c = ε^{1−n}; (4) ζ_p ∉ F^{ker ad ρ̄} and F ⊄ F⁺(ζ_p); (5) ρ̄|_{G_F} is primitive.
hypotheses: p ≡ 1 mod 48n!.
proofSteps: For the coefficient field of ψ̄, the extension cut out by ψ̄/ψ̄^c retains degree at least (p−1)/8 after adjoining ζ_p, as in NTI pp. 83–84. The disjointness hypothesis preserves this bound over F. Since p≡1 mod 48n!, this exceeds 2n(n−1), and division by an exponent i−j gives order greater than 2n for each χ_i/χ_j.

On G_K the determinant identity is ψψ^c=ε^{-4} exactly. Therefore χ_iχ_i^c=(ωω^c)^{n−1}(ψψ^c)^{n−1}=ε^{1−n}. The auxiliary-field avoidance and character-ratio primitivity criterion give the remaining assertions, with primitivity valid over every residue coefficient extension.
acceptance: For n = 3 the congruence asks p ≡ 1 mod 288; p = 577 is the smallest such prime (the parent's check for §4.8).

nodes.title: A weight-5 form with automorphic symmetric powers (Newton–Thorne I Corollary 7.3)
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 3 there is a cuspidal automorphic representation σ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 5, unramified away from 2 and a prime q ≡ 3 mod 4, with σ_2 ≅ i_{B_2}^{GL_2}χ_1 ⊗ χ_2 (χ_1 unramified, χ_2 of conductor 4), σ_q an unramified twist of Steinberg, and Sym^{n−1}r_{σ,ι} automorphic for every p and ι. GL_2 level raising is used: Diamond's criterion raises the level of a form at a prime q satisfying the level-raising congruence to an unramified Steinberg twist at q.
hypotheses: Uses SP.7/residually-cm-steinberg (Theorem 7.1) in rank n, whose odd case rests on SP.7/odd-rank-residually-cm (gap E21).

nodes.title: Theorem 7.1 for odd n (Newton–Thorne I Proposition 7.4), with its gap
nodes.statement: The statement of SP.7/residually-cm-steinberg holds for n = 2k + 1 odd. The printed proof is an induction on odd n: Chebotarev primes q_1 (split in K, > n, of order 6 mod p, with prescribed Frobenius ratios), q_2 ≡ −1 and q_3 (of order n − 2) mod p; real quadratic fields M_1, M_2, M_3; a GL_2 form τ Steinberg at q_1 and supercuspidal at q_2 (Diamond–Taylor); the inductive π on GL_{n−2}; prescribed-type lifts; SP.5/nt-level-raising-to-types; and SP.6/nt-steinberg-level-raising. As printed, the GL_2 block π_2 = τ_0 ⊗ |·|^{(n−2)/2}ιω_1ω_0^{n−1} is not conjugate self-dual (it fails by δ_{K/ℚ}|_{G_{F_0}}), so SP.5/nt-level-raising-to-types does not apply (gap E21 of the extraction). A conjugate self-dual GL_2 block with residual representation ω̄_0^{n−1}ω̄_1 ⊗ Ind ψ̄^{2k} and the required local components must be supplied; until then the odd case is recorded as a gap. The rank-one input is a character. At n=3, E19 repairs the rank-one local type but does not repair the non-conjugate-self-dual GL₂ block; this method is still conditional there.
hypotheses: Induction hypothesis: the statement for n − 2.
Hodge–Tate weights tracked as in E23; G_{F_{−1}} in place of G_E in the inductive hypothesis (E2).
proofSteps: Construct the auxiliary primes and fields by Chebotarev (Tau Ceti Chebotarev).
Build τ by Diamond–Taylor's prescribed-type level raising for GL_2 and the inductive π_{n−2}.
Gap (E21): replace π_2 by a conjugate self-dual block with the same residual representation and local components; the review of the extraction found none.
With such a block: SP.5/nt-level-raising-to-types (types at T_1, T_2, T_3), then SP.6/nt-steinberg-level-raising (Steinberg above q).
acceptance: At n=3 the rank-one constituent and its order-p local character exist. The second constituent still has the δ_{K/ℚ} polarization defect, so this is not an independent proof of the full Theorem 7.1 witness in rank three.

sources.match: Proves the odd case of Theorem 7.1 by induction on n with level raising to types and to Steinberg; the GL_2 block used is not conjugate self-dual as printed.

nodes.title: Residually CM symmetric powers with a Steinberg place (Newton–Thorne I Theorem 7.1)
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 3, p ≡ 1 mod 48n!, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, q ≠ p a prime, X_0 a finite set of places of K = ℚ(i) prime to 2pq, and ω : G_K → Q̄_p^× de Rham with ωω^c = ε³, unramified at X_0. Then there are an X_0-split soluble CM extension F/K and a RACSDC ι-ordinary Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) with (a) r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ ω̄^{n−1}|_{G_F} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_F}; (b) HT_τ(r_{Π,ι}) = HT_τ(ω^{n−1}|_{G_F} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_F}) for all τ; (c) Π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg at some v | q. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.8, unconditionally within this method for n = 2^r, and for other n conditionally on the gap of SP.7/odd-rank-residually-cm.
hypotheses: The odd case uses SP.7/odd-rank-residually-cm (gap E21).
proofSteps: Odd n: SP.7/odd-rank-residually-cm.

n = 2^r m with m odd: induction on r with Anastassiades–Thorne's level raising for GL_{2n} of unitary type (stated in the parent's §4.4), applied to π_0 = π_1 ⊞ π_2 with r̄_{π_0} ≅ ω̄^{2n−1} ⊗ Sym^{2n−1}r̄_{σ_0}; for n a power of 2 Anastassiades–Thorne alone suffices (Remark 7.5).
acceptance: For n = 4 the route is Anastassiades–Thorne twice from n = 1, with no use of the odd case.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.1, p. 83; proof, p. 89; Remark 7.5, p. 90
sources.match: States and proves the existence of an ordinary RACSDC representation residually a twisted symmetric power of σ_0 with a Steinberg place above q, from Proposition 7.4 and Anastassiades–Thorne.
Raises the level of an isobaric sum of two conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations of GL_n with Steinberg components to a cuspidal representation of GL_{2n}.

nodes.title: Theorem E: one level-one form with automorphic symmetric powers
nodes.statement: For each n ≥ 3 there is a cuspidal, everywhere unramified automorphic representation π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 such that Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every ι. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.9, by this seed method for n a power of 2, and independently for n≤5 by the known low-rank lifts, and for other n conditionally on the gap E21.
hypotheses: Uses SP.7/weight-five-symmetric-power.
proofSteps: Start from σ of SP.7/weight-five-symmetric-power: Steinberg at q ≡ 3 mod 4 and of conductor 4 at 2.

The first move is nonordinary on the q-adic eigencurve of tame level 4. The Steinberg local representation at q is irreducible because σ has weight 5, and the local-image criterion gives Zariski closure containing SL₂. Move to a point σ′ unramified at q of weight k≡3 mod 4 and apply the noncritical case of eigencurve-propagation. This step does not use the ordinary case.

At 2 there are no ordinary cuspidal points of tame level one. If the two slopes of σ′ coincided, their common value (k−1)/2 would be odd; the level-4 odd-slope exclusion rules this out. Unequal slopes give n-regularity, and local-image-criteria gives large local image. Apply eigencurve-propagation at 2 to an everywhere unramified point.
acceptance: n = 3, 4, 5: Δ works, since Sym^2, Sym^3, Sym^4 of every non-CM form are automorphic (Gelbart–Jacquet, Kim–Shahidi, Kim).

sources.locator: Theorem 7.6 and proof, pp. 90–91; Introduction, Theorem E, p. 4
sources.match: Deduces from Corollary 7.3 and Theorem 2.33 (twice) the existence of a level-one form with automorphic Sym^{n−1}.

nodes.title: Automorphy of Sym^{l+1} for l ∈ {5, 7} (Clozel–Thorne III Theorem 6.2)
nodes.statement: Let l ∈ {5, 7}, F totally real, ι : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ, and (π, χ) RAESDC on GL_2(𝔸_F) with (1) π ι-ordinary of weight zero; (2) ρ̄ = r̄_ι(π) irreducible with image containing a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{l^a}) for some a > 1, and (φρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄)|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} and Sym^{l−3}ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} adequate; (3) a place u_0 ∤ 2 with π_{u_0} an unramified twist of Steinberg, q_{u_0} a primitive root mod l and ρ̄ ramified at u_0. Then Sym^{l+1}ρ is automorphic.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (3) gives u_0 ∤ l and [F(ζ_l) : F] = l − 1, so the cyclotomic avoidance needed in SP.6/ct-jordan-block-lifting holds with no extra hypothesis (as recorded in the extraction).
proofSteps: The residual congruence (Sym^{l+1}ρ̄)^{ss} ≅ (φρ̄ ⊗ ρ̄) ⊕ χ̄² Sym^{l−3}ρ̄ (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, mod-p Clebsch–Gordan).

Pass to a CM field E_2 = F_2E_1 = F_2E with prescribed places above u_0 (E4 of the extraction); build π′_2 (Clozel–Thorne II Proposition 3.10 with base change for U_2, Steinberg above u_0) and an isobaric Π_1 ⊞ Π_2 of type (4, l − 2) with the Steinberg-type components of SP.5/ct-level-raising-setup.
SP.5/ct-level-raising gives a cuspidal congruent Σ with a long Jordan block; SP.6/ct-jordan-block-lifting shows Sym^{l+1}ρ|_{G_{E_2}} automorphic; soluble descent.
acceptance: For l = 5 the conclusion is automorphy of Sym^6, as used for the parent's §4.31 (Clozel–Thorne Theorem 6.1).

sources.match: Proves automorphy of Sym^{l+1} for l = 5, 7 under ordinarity, large image, adequacy and a Steinberg place, via level raising on a definite unitary group in l + 2 variables and residually reducible automorphy lifting.

planet.name: Sym^6 and Sym^8 by level raising (CT Theorem 6.2)

nodes.title: The non-regular locus of a local lifting ring is a principal divisor
nodes.statement: Let l ≠ p be a prime, R_l the lifting ring of r̄|_{G_{ℚ_l}} (fixed determinant) for a representation π_l with non-trivial Jacquet module, formally smooth of relative dimension 3, and φ_l a Frobenius lift. Let I_l ⊂ R_l be the principal ideal generated by the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of Sym^{n−1}r_l^{univ}(φ_l). A Q̄_p-point f of R_l has eigenvalues α_l, β_l of ρ_f(φ_l) with (α_l/β_l)^i = 1 for some 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1 iff f(I_l) = 0, and dim R_l/I_l < dim R_l.
hypotheses: π_l has non-trivial Jacquet module (so lifts are reducible on the relevant component); n ≥ 2.
proofSteps: The discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of Sym^{n−1} vanishes iff two of the monomials α^aβ^b (a + b = n − 1) coincide, iff (α/β)^i = 1 for some 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1.

The formally smooth fixed-determinant ring is a domain. If π_l is a Steinberg twist, its Frobenius ratio is l^{±1}, so the original point already has nonzero discriminant. In the principal-series case write its characters χ₁,χ₂ and deform them to χ₁ψ_T,χ₂ψ_T^{-1}, where ψ_T is unramified with Frobenius value 1+T. This preserves determinant and varies their ratio nontrivially, so the discriminant is nonzero in the domain. A nonzero principal ideal has quotient of strictly smaller dimension. No general component-classification assertion is required.
acceptance: For n = 2 the ideal is the discriminant (α − β)² of the Frobenius characteristic polynomial.
For n = 3 it vanishes iff α = ±β.

sources.match: Shows the locus of non-n-regular Frobenius eigenvalues in the local lifting ring is cut out by one discriminant and has smaller dimension.

nodes.title: A congruence to a form with n-regular refinements (Newton–Thorne I Proposition 8.3)
nodes.statement: Let π be cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2, non-CM, with π_l of non-trivial Jacquet module at every prime l. There are p, ι and π′ cuspidal of weight k with (1) p > max(2(n + 1), (n − 1)k); (2) r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) ⊇ a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_p); (3) π_p and π′_p unramified; (4) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}; (5) every π′_l has non-trivial Jacquet module, and every accessible refinement of π′_l is n-regular where π′_l is ramified. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.10.
hypotheses: Unobstructedness for almost all p: H⁰(ℚ_l, ad⁰r̄(1)) = 0 at every ramified l (Weston 2004), so the fixed-determinant lifting rings there are formally smooth; and an auxiliary prime q_a > p with π_{q_a} unramified and formally smooth lifting ring (Diamond–Taylor 1994 Lemma 11).
proofSteps: Choose p large (Fontaine–Laffaille range, large image by Ribet–Momose, unobstructedness) and q_a.

Patch (Kisin Proposition 3.2.5; Thorne 2016; Khare–Thorne Corollary 2.7) with g = q_0 + |T| − 1 variables (correction E3): the patched module H_∞ has full support of dimension 4|T| + q_0 over the patched local rings.

If every congruent form failed n-regularity, H_∞ would be supported on the quotient by I = ∏_{l∈T} I_l with T = S − {p, q_a} (correction E25), of smaller dimension by SP.8/nonregular-locus-divisor: contradiction.
q_a needs its own argument: smoothness at q_a forces q_a ≢ 1 mod p and excludes the ratio q_a^{±1}, so π′_{q_a} is unramified; the Jacquet-module condition holds because p ∤ l(l² − 1) (E25).
acceptance: The bound p > (n − 1)k puts every Sym^{n−1} residual lift in the Fontaine–Laffaille range (parent's check for §4.10).

sources.match: Produces, by Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching and a dimension count, a congruent form of the same weight with n-regular refinements at all ramified primes.

nodes.title: Symmetric powers with n-regular refinements at ramified primes (Newton–Thorne I Proposition 8.2)
nodes.statement: Let π be cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2, not CM, with an n-regular accessible refinement at every prime where it is ramified. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every ι.
hypotheses: Uses Theorem A in level one (the parent's §4.12, proved from SP.7/theorem-e and SP.3/level-one-propagation) as the base case.

As a proof via NTI §§7–8 this uses the conditional seed route of G2 outside powers of two and the independent low-rank endpoints. The later SP.13 endpoint is a different proof and does not retroactively repair the CM seed construction.
proofSteps: Induction on the number of primes dividing the conductor; level one is Theorem A.

At a ramified prime p, move along the tame-level-M p-adic eigencurve, avoiding the Zariski closed set of SP.2/bad-locus-closed, to a classical π′ of level prime to p; SP.2/eigencurve-propagation (ordinary or non-ordinary case) transfers automorphy.

π′_l must not be supercuspidal at the remaining ramified primes: the restriction to I_l is locally constant along the component and supercuspidal types differ from those of representations with non-trivial Jacquet module (correction E24).
acceptance: A semistable elliptic curve over ℚ has Steinberg components at bad primes, with accessible refinement ratio q_l^{±1}, which is n-regular; so Proposition 8.2 applies directly.

sources.match: Proves automorphy of Sym^{n−1} for non-CM forms with n-regular refinements at ramified primes by induction on the conductor using Theorem 2.33.

nodes.title: The setting of Newton–Thorne II §2
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p, a totally real field F, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ and n ≥ 1. A pair (π, π′) is in the setting of §2 if π, π′ are regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight 2, non-CM, with r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} and r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} not ordinary (hence potentially Barsotti–Tate) at every v | p, r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}, π_v a twist of Steinberg iff π′_v is for every v ∤ p, and for some a ≥ 1 with p^a > max(5, 2n − 1), PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) ⊂ Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) ⊂ PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) up to conjugacy. After soluble base change one may assume: (6) [F : ℚ] even; (7) det r_{π,ι} = det r_{π′,ι} = ε^{−1}; (8) π, π′ unramified at p; (9) Iwahori-spherical away from p with an even number of ramified places; (10) r̄ trivial on S = S_p ∪ Σ, with q_v ≡ 1 mod p and π_v, π′_v Steinberg on Σ; (11) an everywhere unramified CM quadratic K/F in which S splits. One then works with Π = π_K and the pseudodeformation ring P of Sym^{n−1}r̄|_{G_K}.
hypotheses: The sandwich hypothesis makes Taylor–Wiles primes with Sym^{n−1}r̄(Frob) regular semisimple available (parent §1.7, projective image sandwich).
proofSteps: Soluble base change and descent (parent ML.5; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0) preserve all hypotheses and the conclusion (Newton–Thorne II reductions (6)–(11)).
acceptance: For n=1, Sym⁰r is the trivial rank-one representation and the functoriality conclusion is tautological. The n=2 instance is the rank-two modularity-lifting problem for weight-two Hilbert forms.

sources.locator: §2, setting and statement of Theorem 2.1, p. 5; reductions (6)–(11), pp. 5–6
sources.match: Fixes the weight-two non-ordinary non-CM pair with large projective image and lists the reductions by soluble base change.

nodes.title: Symmetric powers of Barsotti–Tate lifts and the morphism P → R
nodes.statement: In the setting SP.9/nt2-setting, let A be an Artinian object of 𝒞_𝒪, v ∈ S_p, and r̃ : G_{F_v} → GL_2(A) a lift of r̄ of determinant ε^{−1} through R_v, the ring of non-ordinary crystalline lifts with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} (Barsotti–Tate lifts, after reduction (8)). Then A^n with G_{F_v} acting through Sym^{n−1}r̃ is isomorphic to a subquotient of a lattice in a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, n − 1]. Consequently Sym^{n−1} of the universal deformation restricted to G_K defines a morphism P → R from the conjugate self-dual pseudodeformation ring with semistable-in-the-torsion-sense conditions at p to the rank-two deformation ring.
hypotheses: Determinant ε^{−1}; R_v as in Newton–Thorne II §2 (crystalline, Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}, not ordinary), available after the reductions (6)–(11).
proofSteps: The dual of A² is the generic fibre of a finite flat group scheme; Berthelot–Breen–Messing Théorème 3.1.1 gives a crystalline lattice with weights in [0, 1] of which it is a quotient.
Symmetric powers of subquotients of crystalline lattices with weights in [0, 1] are subquotients of lattices in crystalline representations with weights in [0, n − 1] (tensor operations).
The pseudodeformation ring P (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.8) is defined by exactly this torsion-semistable condition, so the universal property gives P → R.
acceptance: For n=1, Sym⁰r̃ is trivial, so P→R is the map classifying the constant trivial rank-one pseudocharacter, not the rank-two determinant map.
For n = 2 the weights of Sym^1 are [0, 1], recovering Barsotti–Tate.

sources.match: Shows symmetric powers of Barsotti–Tate Artinian lifts are subquotients of crystalline lattices with weights in [0, n − 1], so Sym^{n−1} induces a map from the pseudodeformation ring to the deformation ring.

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles data for symmetric powers and the rings P_Q
nodes.statement: A Taylor–Wiles datum of level N is (Q, Q̃, (α_v, β_v)_{v∈Q}) with Q a finite set of places of F split in K and not in S, q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N, a chosen factorisation v = ṽṽ^c, and α_v, β_v the eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_v), such that α_v^{n−1}, α_v^{n−2}β_v, …, β_v^{n−1} are pairwise distinct. With Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q} k(v)^×(p), the deformation ring R_Q is an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra with R_Q ⊗_{𝒪[Δ_Q]} 𝒪 ≅ R. P_Q is the quotient of the pseudodeformation ring of G_{K,S∪Q} parametrising pseudodeformations whose restriction to each G_{K_ṽ} is the determinant of characters χ_{v,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{v,n} lifting the unramified characters with Frobenius α^{n−i}β^{i−1} (unique by Allen–Newton–Thorne Proposition 2.5), with χ_{v,i}|_I = χ_{v,m}^{n+1−2i}|_I for n = 2m, or χ_{v,m}^{(n+1−2i)/2}|_I for n = 2m + 1; this makes P_Q an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra with a map P_Q → R_Q (𝒪[Δ_Q]-linear when n is even).
hypotheses: The distinctness of the n monomials is stronger than the rank-two Taylor–Wiles condition.
Use n≥2 and N≥1 for this construction. The n=1 functoriality theorem is handled before patching; when n=1, m=0 would make the displayed χ_{v,m} undefined.
proofSteps: The decomposition into characters uses uniqueness of the decomposition of residually multiplicity-free pseudocharacters (Allen–Newton–Thorne Proposition 2.5; Bellaïche–Chenevier Proposition 1.5.1).
The inertial relations are those obtained by applying Sym^{n−1} to the rank-two local characters. The resulting P_Q→R_Q is O[Δ_Q]-linear for even n; no such linearity is asserted for odd n.
acceptance: For n = 2 the condition is α_v ≠ β_v and P_Q is the rank-two Taylor–Wiles ring with determinant fixed.

sources.locator: §2, Taylor–Wiles data and the rings P_Q, pp. 8–9
sources.match: Defines Taylor–Wiles data with distinct symmetric-power Frobenius eigenvalues and the quotient P_Q of the pseudodeformation ring with its Δ_Q-structure.

nodes.title: Definite unitary Hecke modules with twisted Taylor–Wiles level
nodes.statement: Let G be the definite unitary group over F split by K (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2) and H_G(V) the 𝒪-valued functions on G(F)\G(𝔸_F^∞)/V. With V_0 Iwahori at Σ, a Taylor–Wiles datum gives V_0(Q) (Iwahori at Q) and V_1(Q; N) ⊂ V_0(Q), cut out at v ∈ Q by requiring ∏_i a_ii^{n+1−2i} (n even) or ∏_i a_ii^{(n+1−2i)/2} (n odd) to map to 1 in k(ṽ)^×(p)/(p^N), so V_0(Q)/V_1(Q; N) ≅ Δ_Q/(p^N). Hecke operators T_w^{(i)} and U_{ϖ_ṽ}^{(i)}, the maximal ideals m_G (Hecke eigenvalues of Sym^{n−1}r̄) and m_{G,Q}, and twisting by characters θ of U_1 through det. (Lemma 2.4) For n even and p = 2, each quadratic χ of F^×\(𝔸_F^∞)^×/det U_1(Q; N) has a unique θ_χ with θ_χ(z/z^c) = χ(zz^c). (Proposition 2.5) For a datum of level N+c_G, where p^{c_G} kills the p-primary parts of the finitely many base-level stabilizers: m_G and m_{G,Q} are in the supports; H_G(V_1(Q; N))_{m_{G,Q}} is free over 𝒪[Δ_Q/(p^N)] with coinvariants H_G(V_0)_{m_G}; and it is a P_Q-module on which the universal characteristic polynomial coefficients at Frob_w act by q_w^{i(i−1)/2}T_w^{(i)}, compatibly with the Δ_Q-actions.
hypotheses: Setting of SP.9/nt2-setting after the reductions.
Assume n≥2, N≥1 and automorphy of Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι}; this extra seed hypothesis supplies the nonzero localized unitary module. It is not part of nt2-setting by itself.
proofSteps: Use a Taylor–Wiles datum at level N+c_G. Its congruence conditions put the p-primary stabilizer images inside V₁(Q;N), so the deck group Δ_Q/(p^N) acts freely on the localized finite double quotient. The ordinary exactness/freeness theorem gives a free O[Δ_Q/(p^N)]-module and trace identifies its coinvariants with H_G(V₀)_{m_G}. The argument does not assume that the original level has trivial stabilizers.
Support of m_G: Labesse's base change descends Π_n = Sym^{n−1} of the automorphic π′_K to G (Labesse Théorème 5.4; EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a).

P_Q-module structure: the Galois pseudocharacter on the Hecke algebra (PL.2) restricted at ṽ ∈ Q decomposes into characters by uniqueness of the decomposition (Allen–Newton–Thorne Proposition 2.5), matching the definition of P_Q.
Lemma 2.4: Hilbert 90 for 0 → 𝔾_m → Res_{K/F}𝔾_m → U_1 → 0.
acceptance: At N=1, tensoring H_G(V₁(Q;1))_{m_{G,Q}} with O along the augmentation of O[Δ_Q/(p)] gives H_G(V₀)_{m_G}, as a module with its Hecke action.

sources.locator: §2, unitary Hecke modules, pp. 9–11; Lemma 2.4, p. 11; Proposition 2.5, p. 11
sources.match: Defines the twisted Taylor–Wiles levels and Hecke maximal ideals on the definite unitary group, the quadratic twisting characters for p = 2, and proves freeness and the P_Q-module structure.

tests.statement: If the congruence level is only N and a p-primary stabilizer has image nontrivial in the deck group, its action on the double quotient has a fixed orbit and group-ring freeness can fail. The offset c_G is what removes this obstruction.

nodes.title: Patching for symmetric powers, p > 2
nodes.statement: In the setting SP.9/nt2-setting with p > 2, let q = dim_k H¹(F_S/F, ad⁰r̄(1)) and g = q + |S ∪ S_∞| − 1. (Lemma 2.7) For every N there is a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N with a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R^□_Q. (Proposition 2.6) There are W_∞ = 𝒪[[Y_1, …, Y_q, Z_1, …, Z_{4|S∪S_∞|−1}]], complete Noetherian local W_∞-algebras P_∞, R_∞ with P_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ P and R_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ R, a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R_∞, a P_∞-module H_{G,∞} and an R_∞-module H_{D,∞}, both finite free over W_∞, specialising to H_G = H_G(V_0)_{m_G} and H_D (quaternionic forms of level U_0 localised at m_D), and a morphism P_∞ → R_∞ compatible with P → R.
hypotheses: For this patching argument assume n≥2 and Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} automorphic, and use the stabilized levels of twisted-unitary-hecke-modules. Handle n=1 separately by Sym⁰=1.
proofSteps: Lemma 2.7: Chebotarev and H¹(PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), ad⁰) = 0 (Cline–Parshall–Scott) give Taylor–Wiles primes with Frob_v regular for Sym^{n−1} ((α/β)^i ≠ 1 for i < n), as in Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorem 2.49 and Kisin.

Patch the modules of SP.9/twisted-unitary-hecke-modules and the quaternionic modules (GL2ModularityLifting R22.2, R22.3) simultaneously over the framed rings, with Newton–Thorne 2020 Lemma 2.16 bounding P_N.
The commutative algebra of patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6).
acceptance: dim W_∞ = 1 + q + 4|S ∪ S_∞| − 1, matching dim R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] when the local rings have the expected dimensions.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.6, p. 13; Lemma 2.7, p. 14; proof of Proposition 2.6, pp. 14–17
sources.match: Constructs the patched rings and modules for p > 2 from enough Taylor–Wiles data for symmetric powers.

nodes.title: Patching for symmetric powers, p = 2
nodes.statement: In the setting SP.9/nt2-setting with p = 2, let q = dim_k H¹(F_S/F, ad r̄) − 2, g = 2q + 1 and γ = 2 − |S ∪ S_∞| + q. (Lemma 2.9) q ≥ |S ∪ S_∞| − 2 and for every N there is a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N with |Q| = q, a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R′^□_Q, and Θ_Q/(2^N) ≅ (ℤ/2^N)^γ for Θ_Q the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-2 extension of F unramified outside Q and (S ∪ S_∞)-split. (Proposition 2.8) There are data as in SP.9/symmetric-patching-odd but with surjections R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R′_∞ → R_∞, a free action of Ĝ_m^γ on Sp R′_∞ with an equivariant δ : Sp R′_∞ → Ĝ_m^γ (acting on itself by the square), δ^{−1}(1) = Sp R_∞, the action of Ĝ_m^γ[2](𝒪) on R_∞ lifting to H_{D,∞}, and an action of Ĝ_m^γ[2] on Sp P_∞ making Sp R_∞ → Sp P_∞ equivariant and lifting to H_{G,∞}.
hypotheses: p = 2; the twisting characters of SP.9/twisted-unitary-hecke-modules (Lemma 2.4).
For this patching argument assume n≥2 and Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} automorphic, and use the stabilized levels of twisted-unitary-hecke-modules. Handle n=1 separately by Sym⁰=1.
proofSteps: Khare–Wintenberger II Lemma 5.10 with the stronger distinctness condition gives Lemma 2.9.
Patch as in Khare–Wintenberger II §2 and Kisin, recording the action of quadratic twists by characters of Θ_Q (Ĝ_m^γ).
acceptance: For γ = 0 there is no twisting action and R′_∞ = R_∞.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.8, p. 17; Lemma 2.9, p. 18; proof, pp. 17–19
sources.match: Constructs the 2-adic patched rings and modules with the action of Ĝ_m^γ from twisting, after Khare–Wintenberger.

nodes.title: Regularity of P at an automorphic point transfers automorphy
nodes.statement: Let p_∞, p′_∞ be the points of Spec P_∞ defined by the pseudocharacters t = Sym^{n−1}r|_{G_K} and t′ = Sym^{n−1}r′|_{G_K}, with t′ automorphic. (p > 2) H_{G,∞} and H_{D,∞} are Cohen–Macaulay with all components of their supports of dimension q + 4|S ∪ S_∞|, so R^{loc}[[X]] → R_∞ is an isomorphism, R_∞ is a domain and H_{D,∞} is faithful; since the localized ring P_{(p′)} is its residue field E (vanishing of the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group of Π′_n), P_∞ is regular of dimension q + 4|S ∪ S_∞| − 1 at p′_∞, so a unique component of Spec P_∞ through p′_∞ lies in Supp H_{G,∞}; Spec R_∞ maps into it, hence p ∈ Supp_P H_G. (p = 2) The dimension argument gives R^{loc}[[X]] ≅ R′_∞ only; Spec R′_∞ and the invariant ring R_∞^{inv} are irreducible and Sp R_∞ → Sp R_∞^{inv} is a Ĝ_m^γ[2]-torsor on the represented complete-local functors whose 𝒪-points act transitively on components. Choose a translate r″_∞ of the automorphic point on a component containing the target point; equivariance and the action on H_{G,∞} put its image p″_∞ in the support, regularity transfers from p′_∞ to p″_∞, and the unique-component argument puts p_∞ in the support. No assertion that R_∞ is a domain is made for p = 2.
hypotheses: Patched data of SP.9/symmetric-patching-odd (p > 2) or SP.9/symmetric-patching-dyadic (p = 2).
For this patching argument assume n≥2 and Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} automorphic, and use the stabilized levels of twisted-unitary-hecke-modules. Handle n=1 separately by Sym⁰=1.
proofSteps: Regularity: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.8 (the localization of the pseudodeformation ring at the characteristic-zero automorphic prime is its residue field E, from vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups), lifted to P_∞ by counting dimensions.
Cohen–Macaulay modules finite free over W_∞ have full-dimensional support components (Stacks 0BUS; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6).
Dyadic case: Khare–Wintenberger II Proposition 2.5 (invariant ring) and transitivity of Ĝ_m^γ[2](𝒪) on components.
acceptance: If P were not regular at p′_∞ (nonzero adjoint Selmer group), several components of Spec P_∞ could pass through p′_∞ and the argument would fail.

sources.locator: proof of Theorem 2.1 for p > 2, pp. 12–13; for p = 2, pp. 17–19
sources.match: Transfers automorphy from t′ to t by the regularity of the patched pseudodeformation ring at the automorphic point, with the torsor and translation argument for p = 2.

nodes.title: Automorphy lifting for symmetric powers (Newton–Thorne II Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: In the setting SP.9/nt2-setting, if Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} is automorphic then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.11 (node ML.3/symmetric-power-automorphy-lifting); it needs no vanishing of the dual Selmer group of the symmetric-power residual representation, allows p = 2 and p ≤ n, and serves as the template for Newton–Thorne 2026 §4.
hypotheses: Setting of SP.9/nt2-setting.
proofSteps: Handle n=1 by Sym⁰=1. For n≥2 assume the stated automorphy of the π′ symmetric power and reduce by soluble base change ((6)–(11)); it supplies the seed in every patching module used below.
SP.9/support-argument puts p = Sym^{n−1}r|_{G_K} in the support of H_G: a RACSDC Π_n on GL_n(𝔸_K) with r_{Π_n,ι} ≅ Sym^{n−1}r|_{G_K} (Labesse Corollaire 5.3).
Descend from K to F (Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Harris–Taylor Lemma 1.5) and then soluble descent.
acceptance: For n=1 the conclusion is the tautological automorphy of the trivial rank-one representation. For n=2 it recovers the rank-two weight-two modularity-lifting instance.

sources.match: States and proves automorphy lifting for symmetric powers of non-ordinary weight-two Hilbert forms with large projective image.
Reuses the Newton–Thorne II template with modified Taylor–Wiles level structure for the tensor version.

nodes.title: The semisimple conductor and the supercuspidal primes of a modular form
nodes.statement: For π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ), sc(π) is the set of primes p with π_p supercuspidal and M_π = ∏_l N((rec_{ℚ_l}π_l)^{ss}) is its semisimple conductor (the Artin conductor of the semisimplified Weil–Deligne representation). Lemma 3.3: if p is odd and r̄_{π,ι} is reducible or dihedral, the prime-to-p part of its conductor divides M_π.
hypotheses: Normalised local Langlands rec_{ℚ_l} (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.3).
proofSteps: Semisimplification forgets the monodromy, so Steinberg components contribute their unramified part only.

For odd p, a reducible residual representation, or a dihedral one, has semisimplified image of order prime to p. Thus its local monodromy vanishes after semisimplification. Reduction of the characteristic-zero semisimplified Weil representation bounds its prime-to-p conductor by M_π (NTII Lemma 3.3); no separate Livné comparison is needed here.
acceptance: For a semistable elliptic curve, sc(π) = ∅ and M_π = 1.

sources.locator: Introduction, p. 2; Definition 3.2 and Lemma 3.3, p. 20
sources.match: Defines the set of supercuspidal primes and the semisimple conductor, and bounds conductors of reducible or dihedral residual representations by it.

uses.how: the lcm M in the definition of seasoned uses the prime-to-q part of M_π

nodes.title: Non-ordinary weight-two congruences with controlled type at p
nodes.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) with Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) containing a conjugate of PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), p^a > 5. (Lemma 3.4) There is π′ with r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, π′ of weight 2 and not ι-ordinary, rec π′_p ≅ ω_1 ⊕ ω_2 with ω_i of conductor dividing p³, and for l ≠ p, π_l Steinberg (resp. supercuspidal) iff π′_l is. (Lemma 3.5) If moreover p ≥ 3, π′ can be chosen with in addition r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} ∼ r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} (strongly connected in the sense of BLGGT) for every l ≠ p; in particular N(π_l) = N(π′_l).
hypotheses: p^a > 5; p ≥ 3 for Lemma 3.5.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.4: Breuil–Mézard types at the supercuspidal primes, a quaternion algebra ramified at the Steinberg primes, a neat level, Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis Corollary 2.12, and a dimension count on the slope-(0, 1) part of cohomology of level U_0(p³) via Hida theory and Mackey's formula; non-ordinarity by Geraghty Lemma 5.2.
Lemma 3.5: Gee's lifts of prescribed type (Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7; PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3) with strong connection (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.1).
acceptance: For π of weight 2 already non-ordinary with the required type at p, π′ = π works.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.4 and proof, pp. 20–22; Lemma 3.5, pp. 22–23
sources.match: Produces non-ordinary weight-two congruent forms with controlled type at p and the same Steinberg and supercuspidal primes, and strengthens this to strong local connection away from p.

nodes.title: Seasoned automorphic representations
nodes.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 2 with 2 ∉ sc(π), and q, t, r primes. π is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) if (1) t | q + 1, t ∉ sc(π), t > max(10, 8n(n − 1)) and (q + 1)/t > 2; (2) rec π_q ≅ Ind_{W_{ℚ_{q²}}}^{W_{ℚ_q}}χ with χ|_{I_{ℚ_q}} of order t (so q ∈ sc(π) and N(π_q) = q²); (3) r is a primitive root mod q and r ≡ 1 mod M, where M is the lcm of the prime-to-q part of M_π and ∏_{p∈sc(π)−{q}} p⁶; (4) π_r is an unramified twist of Steinberg; (5) for each p ∈ sc(π) and each irreducible dihedral ρ : G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽̄_p) of prime-to-p conductor dividing Mq², there is a prime s with π_s an unramified Steinberg twist, ρ(Frob_s) scalar and s ≢ 1 mod p.
hypotheses: n is the fixed symmetric-power rank; seasoning depends on n through t > 8n(n − 1).
Fix n≥3 throughout the seasoning argument; ranks n=1,2 are handled separately before this induction.
proofSteps: A variant of Khare–Wintenberger's good-dihedral condition (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.1) with an extra Steinberg prime r that guarantees large residual image at every supercuspidal prime.

sources.match: Defines representations seasoned with respect to a triple of primes, by a tamely dihedral component at q of order t, a Steinberg prime r and the dihedral-killing primes s.

uses.how: seasoned representations have large residual image at each supercuspidal prime
the induction on |sc(π)|

nodes.title: Seasoned representations have large residual image at supercuspidal primes
nodes.statement: If π is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r), then for each p ∈ sc(π) there is ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ with PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) ⊂ Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) ⊂ PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) after conjugation, for p^a>max(5,2n−1), and with linear image containing SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}).
hypotheses: π seasoned (SP.10/seasoned-representation).
proofSteps: For p = q: irreducibility from the Steinberg prime r and Gee 2011 Theorem 4.6.1 (niveau-two description); non-dihedrality from condition (5) and Lemma 3.3 (SP.10/semisimple-conductor); a choice of ι gives projective elements of order ≥ t/2 > 4n(n − 1).
For p ≠ q: inertia at q has projective image of order t.
The classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(𝔽̄_p) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4) then gives the SL_2 conclusion.
acceptance: Condition p^a > 2n − 1 is the input SP.9/nt2-setting needs for Theorem 2.1 at p.

sources.match: Shows seasoned representations have residual image containing SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with p^a > 2n − 1 at every supercuspidal prime.

nodes.title: Making a representation seasoned
nodes.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 2, non-CM, with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π). There is π′ regular algebraic cuspidal with (1) primes (q, t, r) such that π′ is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) and sc(π′) = sc(π) ∪ {q}; (2) Sym^{n−1}π′ exists iff Sym^{n−1}π does.
hypotheses: π non-CM, weight 2, 2, 3 ∉ sc(π).
Fix n≥3 throughout the seasoning argument; ranks n=1,2 are handled separately before this induction.
proofSteps: Choose t > max(10, 8n(n − 1), N(π)), t ≡ 1 mod 4, with large t-adic image; q ≡ −1 mod t with Frob_q conjugate to complex conjugation; r and the primes s by Chebotarev (with Lemma 3.8, the elementary fibre-product description of Gal(L₁L₂/K) for two finite Galois extensions: pairs of automorphisms with equal restriction to L₁∩L₂).
Gee's prescribed-type lifts (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3) produce π′ congruent to π at t with the new local components.

BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.5) shows Sym^{n−1}π′ automorphic iff Sym^{n−1}π is: both are Fontaine–Laffaille at t, and Sym^{n−1} of SL_2(𝔽_t) is irreducible for t > n − 1 (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7).
acceptance: The new supercuspidal prime is q; sc grows by exactly one.

sources.match: Constructs a seasoned congruent representation adding one supercuspidal prime, preserving the existence of Sym^{n−1}.

nodes.title: Removing one supercuspidal prime
nodes.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 2, seasoned with respect to (q, t, r), and p ∈ sc(π) with p ≥ 5. There is π′ of weight 2, non-CM, with sc(π′) = sc(π) − {p}, still seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) if p ≠ q, such that if Sym^{n−1}π′ exists then Sym^{n−1}π exists.
hypotheses: π seasoned; p ≥ 5.
Fix n≥3 throughout the seasoning argument; ranks n=1,2 are handled separately before this induction.
proofSteps: SP.10/seasoned-large-image chooses ι at p with large residual image.
SP.10/nonordinary-weight-two-congruences (Lemma 3.5) produces π′ non-ordinary at p with principal-series type at p (so p ∉ sc(π′)), strongly connected to π away from p.
SP.9/symmetric-power-automorphy-lifting (Theorem 2.1) transfers automorphy of Sym^{n−1} from π′ to π.
When p≠q impose conductor dividing p⁶ at p. This is essential to preserve seasoning: unchanged components at q and r alone do not control the auxiliary integer M.
acceptance: For p≠q, strong connection preserves the local Weil–Deligne data away from p, while N(π′_p) divides p⁶. Together these preserve the bounds defining M and the dihedral-killing conditions (3) and (5), as well as the types at q and r.

sources.match: Removes a supercuspidal prime p ≥ 5 from a seasoned representation by a non-ordinary congruence and Theorem 2.1.

nodes.title: Symmetric powers in weight two when 2, 3 are not supercuspidal primes
nodes.statement: If π is regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 2, non-CM, with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π), then Sym^{n−1}π exists.
hypotheses: Base case: Newton–Thorne I Theorem B (sc(π) = ∅), the statement the parent records in §4.20.
Fix n≥3 throughout the seasoning argument; ranks n=1,2 are handled separately before this induction.
proofSteps: Let H_k assert the result for all eligible π with |sc(π)|≤k, and H′_k for the seasoned ones with |sc(π)|≤k.
H_k⇒H′_{k+1}: remove any supercuspidal prime by Proposition 3.10, including q if needed. The result has at most k such primes, so H_k applies; no seasoning condition is needed on that result.

H′_k⇒H_k for k≥1: for |sc(π)|=k, add a new good-dihedral prime q by Proposition 3.9. Remove an old prime p∈sc(π), hence p≠q, by Proposition 3.10. The result is still seasoned and has k supercuspidal primes, so H′_k applies. Compose the automorphy implications. H_0 is the separate base case.

The NTI route to H_0 uses SP.8/n-regular-ramified-automorphy and SP.8/n-regular-congruence. Its recorded source gap G2 and the supplier boundaries remain part of this proof plan; the endpoint imported in the parent is not an independent proof of that route.
acceptance: k = 0 is Newton–Thorne I Theorem B.

sources.match: Proves existence of Sym^{n−1}π for non-CM weight-two π with 2, 3 not supercuspidal primes, by induction on the number of supercuspidal primes.

nodes.title: The reductions completing symmetric power functoriality for non-CM modular forms (Newton–Thorne II Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: For every non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) and every n ≥ 1, Sym^{n−1}π exists. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.29 (Newton–Thorne II Theorem A). The proof reduces to SP.10/weight-two-case: for π of weight 2 with 2 ∉ sc(π) and 3 ∈ sc(π), choose t > max(5, 4n(n − 1), N(π)), t ≡ 1 mod 4, with large t-adic projective image, and q ≡ −1 mod t, q ≡ 1 mod 8 and mod every prime l < t, Frob_q conjugate to complex conjugation; a good-dihedral π′ at q with Sym^{n−1}π′ existing iff Sym^{n−1}π does; the 3-adic projective image of r̄_{π′,ι} (not of r̄_{π,ι}, correction E1) is PSL_2 or PGL_2 of 𝔽_{3^a} with 3^a > 2n − 1; Lemma 3.4 gives a weight-2 π″ with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π″), non-ordinary at 3; then SP.10/weight-two-case and SP.9/symmetric-power-automorphy-lifting conclude. If 2 ∈ sc(π), run the same argument with 2 and 3 exchanged and conclude by the case just treated, not by Proposition 3.11, since π″ may have 3 ∈ sc(π″) (correction E3). Weight k > 2 reduces to weight 2 by a t-adic congruence with a potentially crystalline weight-2 form and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1.
hypotheses: π non-CM; CM and weight-one forms are the parent's §4.13.
This NTII proof plan inherits the conditional NTI base case G2 and the source/supplier boundaries recorded below. Its endpoint statement is not asserted to have been formalised or reproved here.
proofSteps: As in the statement; the large-image choice of t uses Ribet–Momose (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.3), the good-dihedral prime Khare–Wintenberger I Lemma 6.3 (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.1), Gee's prescribed-type lifts and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 with potential diagonalisability (Gee–Kisin).
acceptance: For a non-CM elliptic curve over ℚ with additive potentially good reduction at 3, the reduction passes through the 3-adic step.

sources.match: Completes symmetric power functoriality for all non-CM modular forms by reducing to weight two with 2, 3 not supercuspidal primes.

planet.name: Theorem A for non-CM modular forms

nodes.title: The standing hypotheses and auxiliary data of Newton–Thorne 2026 §3
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p ≥ 5, 1 < r < p, n = 2r, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, and π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_F) with (1) det r_{π,ι} = ε^{−1}; (2) weight 0 and π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg at each v | p; (3) a place v_0 with q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod p where π_{v_0} is tamely dihedral of order p; (4) r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) containing a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with a > a_0(p) (the adequacy threshold of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, Newton–Thorne 2026 Lemma 2.3 = Thorne 2024 Lemma 7.3); (5) π_v potentially unramified at every v ∤ p. After conjugation the projective image is PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) or PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with a > 3. Auxiliary data: a place v_a ∤ p where π is unramified and the eigenvalue ratio of r̄(Frob_{v_a}) satisfies (α/β)^i ≢ q_{v_a}^{±1} mod p for i = 0, …, r, so H²(F_{v_a}, ad(r̄ ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄)^{ss}) = 0 (Lemma 3.3); M the extension of F(ζ_p) cut out by r̄; X_0 ∋ v_a a finite set of prime-to-p places such that every Galois subextension M/M′/F of degree > 1 has a non-split place in X_0 (so X_0-split extensions are linearly disjoint from M); K_0 imaginary quadratic with p and the residue characteristics of X_0 ∪ {v_0} split, u_0 | p; and soluble totally real F_2/F_1/F as in Lemma 3.4 (X_0-split, K_1 = K_0F_1 unramified over F_1, [F_1 : F] even, trivial residual representation and [F_{1,v}:ℚ_p]>n(n+1)/2+1 at every v|p, BC(π) unramified away from pv_0 over F_1, v_0 split in F_1/F and, over F_2, the places above v_0 with q≡1 mod p^N for an N with p^N>n and trivial residual representation, p-adic places of F_1 split in F_2, d_{0,F_2} > 1, and characters X, Y of K_1 of type A_0 with xx^c = ε, yy^c = ω, x̄ = ȳ and Hodge–Tate weight 0 at u_0).
hypotheses: r > 1 (Theorem 3.2 is trivial for r = 1).

The last odd abelian extension F_2/F_1 has degree d>1 and is chosen so d_{0,F_2}>1. The characters X,Y are everywhere unramified. The antiunit rank estimate used to arrange this is the explicit inherited boundary of ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3, not an established library fact.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.3 by Chebotarev in the image of r̄ (which contains SL_2(𝔽_{p^a})).

Lemma 3.4 by successive soluble base changes with prescribed local behaviour (Moret–Bailly-type arguments; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0, auxiliary CM extensions and characters) and class field theory for d_{0,F_2} (the source prints 'of K_1' in (2) and an undefined K in (5), corrections E18–E19).
acceptance: For p=5 and this r>1 construction, r∈{2,3,4}; a>a₀(5)≥3 gives a≥4. The r=1 endpoint is treated directly before introducing this data.

nodes.title: A congruent ordinary companion of weights {0, 2}
nodes.statement: Under SP.11/tensor-section-3-hypotheses there is a single RAESDC σ on GL_2(𝔸_F) which is ι-ordinary, has HT_τ(r_{σ,ι}) = {0, 2} for every τ, determinant ε^{−2}ω_p (ω_p the Teichmüller lift of ε mod p), residual representation r̄_{σ,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, an unramified Steinberg twist at v_0, and r_{σ,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} (the BLGGT relation) at every finite v ∤ p, v ≠ v_0. All properties hold for the same σ.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of SP.11/tensor-section-3-hypotheses.
proofSteps: Local lifts at p: put π in a Hida family of Hilbert modular forms (Wiles 1988; OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.2) and specialise to weight {0, 2} with determinant ε^{−2}ω.

Global deformation ring with prescribed components (Bellovin–Gee 2019 §4.2; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.7, global lifts): at v∤pv₀ the component through r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}}⊗χ_v, where χ_v is unramified, χ_v≡1 mod ϖ and χ_v²=ε^{−1}ω_p (a regular point with the required new determinant), at v | p the ordinary potentially crystalline component through the local lift, at v_0 a unipotent component with N generically nonzero, which exists because the tamely dihedral type of order p reduces to an unramified induced representation with Frobenius ratio −1 ≡ q_{v_0} mod p, so r̄|_{G_{F_{v_0}}} is reducible and unipotently ramified; Bellovin–Gee Proposition 4.2.6 gives Krull dimension ≥ 1.

Khare–Wintenberger method: finiteness over 𝒪 (Thorne 2012 Theorem 10.2; PL.4, finiteness) gives a characteristic-zero point ρ, and automorphy lifting after soluble base change (Thorne 2012 Theorem 9.1; PL.4) gives ρ = r_{σ,ι}.
acceptance: Sym^r σ has Hodge–Tate weights {0, 2, …, 2r}, distinct, which makes r_π ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_σ regular (weights {0, 1} + {0, 2, …, 2r − 2}).
