nodes.title: The polarized representation s and its residual decomposition
nodes.statement: With σ from SP.11/ordinary-companion, put π_1 = BC(Sym^r σ) ⊗ XY^{−r}|·|^{(r−1)/2} and π_2 = BC(Sym^{r−2}σ) ⊗ X^{−1}Y^{2−r}|·|^{(r−1)/2} over K_1, and s = (r_{π,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ,ι})|_{G_{K_1}} ⊗ y^{1−r}. Then (Lemma 3.5) s^c ≅ s^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−2r}; π_1, π_2 are cuspidal conjugate self-dual; π_1 ⊞ π_2 is regular algebraic and ι-ordinary; and r̄_{π_1⊞π_2,ι} ≅ s̄. After conjugation s takes values in GL_n(𝒪) and extends to s : G_{F_1} → 𝒢_n(𝒪) with multiplier ε^{1−n}δ^n_{K_1/F_1}. With S_{p,F_1} the p-adic places, T_{F_1} (resp. T′_{F_1}) the places above v_0 (resp. v_a), S_{F_1} = S_{p,F_1} ∪ T_{F_1} and S̃_{F_1} a choice of places of K_1 above them, s is a lift of s̄ of type 𝒮_{F_1}: ordinary at p, of inertial type τ_s at T_{F_1}, unramified outside S_{F_1} (this needs BC(σ) unramified away from pv_0, which follows from SP.11/ordinary-companion since ∼ preserves (r|_I, N); E22 of the extraction).
hypotheses: Lemma 3.4's characters X, Y; residual Clebsch–Gordan for r̄ ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄ ≅ Sym^r r̄ ⊕ (det r̄ ⊗ Sym^{r−2}r̄) when r < p.

Assume SP_{r−1} and SP_{r+1} to define the automorphic π₂ and π₁. These are genuine induction hypotheses already at this construction, not only at the later finiteness step. Here r>1; the tensor for r=1 is simply r_π and uses no SP₀.
proofSteps: Conjugate self-duality from det r_π = ε^{−1}, det r_σ = ε^{−2}ω_p and yy^c = ω.
The residual decomposition is the mod-p Clebsch–Gordan formula (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7) after twisting.
Cuspidality of π_1, π_2 from large image of Sym^r r̄ and Sym^{r−2}r̄; regularity from the weights {0, 2}; ordinarity from that of σ.
The multiplier of tensor products (BLGGT14 §1.1).
acceptance: For r = 2: s̄ ≅ (Sym² r̄ ⊕ det r̄) twisted, of dimensions 3 + 1.

Lemma 3.7: for X_0-split totally real F′ ⊇ F_1, K′ ⊄ F′(ζ_p); s̄|_{G_{K′}} ≅ ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2 with ρ̄_i^c ≅ ρ̄_i^∨ε^{1−n}, of dimensions r + 1 and r − 1, non-isomorphic over K′(ζ_p); s̄|_{G_{K′}} is primitive; and s̄(G_{K′}) has no quotient of order p.
hypotheses: F′ ⊇ F_1 (s̄ is defined on G_{K_1}; correction E19).
proofSteps: Thorne 2015 §3 deformation problems for 𝒢_n with Λ-structure (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2, ordinary deformation datum; GlobalGaloisDeformations G7).
Local rings: Shotton's fixed-type rings and the Steinberg and unipotent rings (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2, L7).
Lemma 3.7 from X_0-splitness (linear disjointness from M), large image and the dimensions r ± 1 being distinct.

nodes.title: Two inertial types with the same reduced special fibre, and the comparison of deformation rings
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.6) For v ∈ T_{F_1}, let R^□_v be the unrestricted lifting ring of s̄|_{G_{K_{1,ṽ}}}, R_v its quotient for the inertial type τ_s of s and R′_v its quotient for the type of the special representation Sp_n. Then R_v and R′_v are nonzero and (R_v/(ϖ))^{red} ≅ (R′_v/(ϖ))^{red} as R^□_v-algebras. (Lemma 3.8) Consequently (R_{𝒮_{F_1}}/(ϖ))_{red} ≅ (R_{𝒮′_{F_1}}/(ϖ))_{red}, and restriction gives a finite morphism R_{𝒮′_{F_2}} → R_{𝒮′_{F_1}}.
hypotheses: v_0 with q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod p and π_{v_0} tamely dihedral of order p; s̄ trivial residual type considerations at T_{F_1}.
proofSteps: Under division-algebra Jacquet–Langlands, the two types in this lemma correspond to characters of order p and order 1. They have the same mod-p reduction. Dotto’s cycle formula therefore gives equal special-fibre cycles for these particular types, not for arbitrary congruent inertial restrictions.

Both local lifting rings are O-flat, reduced and equidimensional of dimension 1+n², with special fibres pure of dimension n². Equal cycles then give the same generic points and hence equal reduced closed special fibres inside the common unrestricted special fibre. Nonemptiness follows from the exhibited characteristic-zero types.

Present the global problems using the same auxiliary global relations over the local rings. Equality after reduction transfers to their reduced special fibres. Finiteness of restriction F₂/F₁ is the separate pseudodeformation-restriction theorem.
acceptance: For these two types, equality of the special-fibre cycles and purity of dimension n² imply equality of reduced special fibres. Equality of mod-p inertial restrictions by itself is insufficient.

sources.match: Shows the fixed-type and special-type lifting rings above v_0 have isomorphic reduced special fibres, and deduces the comparison of global rings and finiteness of restriction.

nodes.title: Finiteness of R_{𝒮′_{F_2}} and a Steinberg automorphic lift
nodes.statement: R_{𝒮′_{F_2}} is finite over Λ_{F_2}, and there is an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π of GL_n(𝔸_{K_2}), unramified outside S_{F_2}, with r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ s̄|_{G_{K_2}} and Π_ṽ an unramified twist of Steinberg for each v ∈ T_{F_2}. The irreducible constituents of s̄|_{G_{K_2}} (twists of Sym^r r̄_{σ,ι} and Sym^{r−2}r̄_{σ,ι}) have ι-ordinary automorphic lifts Steinberg at a suitable ṽ_2: raise the level of σ for GL_2 at v_2 (q_{v_2} ≡ 1 mod p, r̄ trivial there) and take symmetric powers using SP_{r−1} and SP_{r+1}.
hypotheses: SP_{r−1} and SP_{r+1} (the induction hypotheses, parent node ML.3/sp-statement).

In the residually reducible inputs, primitive means weakly primitive in the source sense, tested over the algebraic closure of the residual field. Choose a common finite splitting field for every subgroup of the residual image before fixing integral coefficient rings. The PL.6 normalization coefficient condition then holds; no implication from arbitrary finite-field primitivity to geometric primitivity is assumed.
proofSteps: Choose v₂∉S∪X₀ with q_{v₂}≡1 mod p and trivial residual representation, and ensure all other places of its residue characteristic are unramified in the construction. Raise the GL₂ level at v₂ and apply SP_{r−1},SP_{r+1} to obtain ordinary automorphic lifts of both residual constituents, Steinberg at the chosen place.

First apply the ANT residually reducible finiteness argument with the auxiliary Steinberg condition at v₂. Khare–Wintenberger extraction and Thorne 2024 Theorem 7.5 produce an ordinary automorphic lift Π′ with the prescribed types, including Steinberg at T and v₂. This requires the auxiliary-place variant of NT26 Proposition 3.9, whose local-ring and Hecke comparison boundary is recorded in G7.

Then remove the extra Steinberg condition at v₂. Apply finiteness a second time using Π′ as automorphic input to obtain finiteness of the desired R_{𝒮′_{F₂}} over Λ_{F₂}. Thorne’s level-raising input and the ordinary extraction give Π with the asserted Steinberg types at T. A single unqualified finiteness call does not justify this relaxation.
acceptance: For r = 2 the constituents are twists of Sym² r̄_σ and of a character; SP_1 and SP_3 hold unconditionally.

sources.match: Proves finiteness of the Steinberg deformation ring over Λ and produces an ordinary RACSDC lift Steinberg above v_0, via residual automorphy of the constituents and Thorne's level raising.

nodes.title: Generic primes on every component
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.10) The graph whose vertices are the minimal primes of R_{𝒮′_{F_2}}/(ϖ), with Q, Q′ joined when Q + Q′ lies in a generic prime of dimension 1, is connected. (Proposition 3.11) R_{𝒮_{F_1}} is finite over Λ_{F_1}; each minimal prime has dimension dim Λ_{F_1} and characteristic 0 and lies in a generic prime of dimension 1 and characteristic p. Consequently there is a finite set 𝒫 of generic primes of R_{𝒮′_{F_2}} of dimension 1 and characteristic p witnessing every edge of the graph and such that every minimal prime of R_{𝒮_{F_1}} lies in a generic 𝔭 with 𝔭_{F_2} ∈ 𝒫.
hypotheses: d_{0,F_2} > 1 (SP.11/tensor-section-3-hypotheses) bounds the reducible locus.
proofSteps: Proposition 3.10: connectedness dimension of R_{𝒮′_{F_2}}/(ϖ) (Grothendieck's connectedness and the arithmetic rank; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.6, connectedness dimension) together with the bound on the reducible locus by d_{0,F_2} (PL.6, reducible-locus dimension).
Proposition 3.11: SP.11/reduced-special-fibres transfers finiteness and components from 𝒮′_{F_1} to 𝒮_{F_1}; large quotients contain generic primes (PL.6).
𝒫: Thorne 2015 Proposition 5.3 and the splitting of the p-adic places of F_1 in F_2.
acceptance: If R_{𝒮′_{F_2}}/(ϖ) had two components meeting only in the reducible locus, the graph would be disconnected; d_{0,F_2} > 1 excludes this.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.10, p. 21; Proposition 3.11, p. 22; the set 𝒫, pp. 22–23
sources.match: Proves connectedness of the generic-prime graph, finiteness and generic primes on every component of the fixed-type problem, and chooses the finite set 𝒫.

nodes.title: An extension making generic points scalar, and the generic R = T theorem
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.12) There is a totally real F_3/F_2, soluble and X_0-split over F, in which each p-adic place of F_2 splits, such that for every 𝔭 ∈ 𝒫 and v ∈ T_{F_3}, r_𝔭|_{G_{K_3,ṽ}} is unramified with scalar Frobenius. (Proposition 3.13) If 𝔭 ⊂ R_{𝒮_{F_3}} is a generic prime of dimension 1 and characteristic p with J_{𝒮_{F_3}} ⊂ 𝔭 and r_𝔭|_{G_{K_3,ṽ}} scalar for each v ∈ T_{F_3}, then every prime Q ⊂ 𝔭 contains J_{𝒮_{F_3}}.
hypotheses: 𝒫 as in SP.11/generic-components.

Choose the residual coefficient field initially to split every subgroup of the residual finite image. Verify geometric weak primitivity before this choice; the weak-primitive generic Hecke-kernel theorem then applies over the normalization residue field. An inference from primitivity over an arbitrary finite field is not used.

In the residually reducible inputs, primitive means weakly primitive in the source sense, tested over the algebraic closure of the residual field. Choose a common finite splitting field for every subgroup of the residual image before fixing integral coefficient rings. The PL.6 normalization coefficient condition then holds; no implication from arbitrary finite-field primitivity to geometric primitivity is assumed.
proofSteps: Proposition 3.12: adjoin an X_0-split soluble extension of F sufficiently tamely ramified at v_0 (proof of Thorne 2015 Proposition 6.2).

Proposition 3.13: for trivial restriction this is the generic R = T theorem (Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 4.1; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.6, generic R_𝔭 = T_𝔭); the scalar case reduces to it by the twisting argument of Thorne 2015 Lemma 3.40 (PL.6, twisting and base change).
acceptance: Trivial restriction at T_{F_3} is the special case of scalar restriction with scalar 1.

sources.match: Constructs F_3 making the generic points scalar above v_0, and extends the generic R = T theorem to scalar local restrictions.

nodes.title: Every component of the Steinberg problem is automorphic after restriction
nodes.statement: There are Λ_{F_3}-algebra maps R_{𝒮_{F_3}} → R_{𝒮′_{F_2}} and R_{𝒮_{F_3}} → R_{𝒮_{F_1}} by restriction (τ_s becomes unipotent over F_3 because BC_{F_2/F}(π) is unramified above v_0), compatible maps of the pseudodeformation subrings, and 𝕋_{F_3} → 𝕋_{F_2} by soluble base change, so that J_{𝒮_{F_3}}·P_{𝒮′_{F_2}} ⊂ J_{𝒮′_{F_2}}. (Proposition 3.14) For every prime Q ⊂ R_{𝒮′_{F_2}}/(ϖ), its pullback Q_{F_3} to R_{𝒮_{F_3}} contains J_{𝒮_{F_3}}.
hypotheses: Setting of SP.11.
proofSteps: Use the restriction and ordinary Hecke base-change diagram of NT26 p.24, Thorne 2015 Proposition 4.18 and NTI Lemma 6.7, with the same pseudodeformation subrings.

The ordinary Hecke algebra from the Steinberg seed is faithful over Λ. Together with finiteness and equidimensionality this supplies a minimal characteristic-p component containing the Hecke kernel, rather than merely a single isolated automorphic point.

Propagate that component along the connected graph of SP.11/generic-components. At each edge, pull its witness in 𝒫 back to F₃; it is scalar locally by Proposition 3.12. Proposition 3.13 puts the Hecke kernel into both adjoining component primes. Every vertex, and hence every prime above a vertex, contains the pulled-back kernel.
acceptance: A single automorphic component plus connectivity gives all components.

sources.locator: the comparison diagram, p. 24; Proposition 3.14 and proof, p. 24
sources.match: Builds the comparison diagram of deformation rings and Hecke algebras over F_3 and shows every component of the Steinberg problem becomes automorphic after restriction.

nodes.title: Automorphy of the untwisted tensor r_π ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_σ (Newton–Thorne 2026 Theorem 3.2)
nodes.statement: Under SP.11/tensor-section-3-hypotheses, assume SP_{r−1} and SP_{r+1}. For any σ with the properties of SP.11/ordinary-companion, r_{π,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ,ι} ≅ r_{Π,ι} for an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(𝔸_F). (For r = 1 the statement is trivial.) This is the tensor theorem for the prescribed π and σ only, not general GL_2 × GL_r functoriality.
proofSteps: The specified s gives f:R_{𝒮_{F₁}}→O. Choose a minimal prime Q⊂ker(f). Proposition 3.11 puts Q in a characteristic-p dimension-one generic prime 𝔭 whose image 𝔭_{F₂} lies in 𝒫.

Proposition 3.14 first gives J_{𝒮_{F₃}}⊂𝔭_{F₃}. Proposition 3.12 makes the local restrictions of this generic representation scalar. Apply Proposition 3.13 again, now to Q_{F₃}⊂𝔭_{F₃}, to get J_{𝒮_{F₃}}⊂Q_{F₃}⊂ker(f)_{F₃}. This second use is necessary: membership in the larger generic prime alone does not establish automorphy of f.

The Hecke support criterion gives automorphy of s restricted to K₃. Undo X,Y and use soluble descent from K₃ to K₁ and then F, obtaining exactly the prescribed tensor. Treat r=1 directly by Sym⁰=1, without invoking SP₀.
acceptance: For r = 2 the tensor r_π ⊗ r_σ is automorphic by Ramakrishnan's GL_2 × GL_2 (parent ML.3/ramakrishnan-tensor-product), a consistency check.

nodes.title: Preliminary reductions and the CM set-up for tensor functoriality lifting
nodes.statement: In the situation of SP.12/tensor-functoriality-lifting, after Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 4.1.4 and a soluble totally real base change one may assume in addition: (10) det r_π = det r_{π′} = ε^{−1}; (11) [F : ℚ] even; (12) π_v, π′_v and σ_v Iwahori-spherical at every finite v, with an even number of places where π, π′ are ramified; (13) with Σ the places where π or σ is ramified (σ's ramified places added, repairing E24 of the extraction) and S = S_p ∪ Σ, r̄_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} trivial for v ∈ S, and for v ∈ Σ^p, q_v ≡ 1 mod p with π_v, π′_v Steinberg or unramified as the case may be (if Σ ∩ S_p ≠ ∅ then p > 2); (14) an S-split everywhere unramified quadratic CM K/F with CM type Φ and places S̃; (15) everywhere unramified type-A_0 characters X, Y of K with X∘N = χ∘N (σ ≅ σ^∨ ⊗ χ), Y∘N = |·| and prescribed infinity types; (16) (r_π ⊗ r_σ)|_{G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})}} and (r_{π′} ⊗ r_σ)|_{G_K} irreducible. Put π_K = BC(π), π′_K = BC(π′), σ_K = BC(σ) ⊗ X^{−1}, and T the RACSDC representation of GL_n(𝔸_K) of weight 0 with r_T ≅ r_{π_K} ⊗ r_{σ_K} ⊗ r_Y^{1−r}; with integral models r, r′, s (r̄ = r̄′) and the group determinants t, t′ of (r ⊗ s)|_{G_K} ⊗ r_{X^{−1}Y^{1−r}} and its π′ analogue, with common reduction t̄.
hypotheses: Hypotheses (1)–(9) of SP.12/tensor-functoriality-lifting.
Repair of E24: unramified local conditions for r̃ at σ's extra ramified places, D unramified and V_0 Iwahori there.

Write Σ_π for the ramification set of π (and π′ after the reductions), and Σ=Σ_π∪Σ_σ for the full set used in S and in the unitary Iwahori level. The quaternion algebra D is ramified only at Σ_π away from p, not at σ-only places. At a σ-only place D is split and the rank-two deformation condition remains unramified.
proofSteps: Soluble base change preserves (1)–(9) and the conclusion descends (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0).
XX^c = χ∘N and YY^c = |·|_K give r_T^c ≅ r_T^∨ ⊗ ε^{1−2r}; X^{−1}Y^{1−r} has trivial infinity type (PL.0, auxiliary characters).
acceptance: For r = 1, σ is a character, T = π_K ⊗ σ_K and the argument is rank-two modularity lifting.

nodes.title: Artinian points are torsion semistable, and the tensor map P → R
nodes.statement: (Lemma 4.2) For Artinian A ∈ 𝒞_𝒪, v ∈ S_p and a lift r̃_A of r̄|_{G_{F_v}} of determinant ε^{−1} of the given type at v, the module A^{2r} with the action r̃_A ⊗ s|_{G_{K_ṽ}} ⊗ r_{X^{−1}Y^{1−r},ι} is a subquotient of a lattice in a semistable representation with Hodge–Tate weights in a fixed interval [a, b]. (Corollary 4.3) Consequently r̃ ↦ (r̃ ⊗ s)|_{G_K} ⊗ r_{X^{−1}Y^{1−r},ι} defines a morphism P → R in 𝒞_𝒪 from the conjugate self-dual pseudodeformation ring of rank 2r (semistable in the torsion sense at p) to the rank-two deformation ring R, and t, t′ give homomorphisms P → 𝒪.
hypotheses: Setting of SP.12/tensor-lifting-setup.
proofSteps: At a potentially crystalline weight-{0,1} place, the finite-flat/Barsotti–Tate comparison makes each Artinian rank-two point a quotient of a lattice in a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights {0,1}. Tensor with the fixed semistable lattice and the fixed character, obtaining a uniform interval [a,b]. The precise BBM finite-flat generic-fibre comparison is requested from R07.4.

At a noncrystalline ordinary place use the closed, stable torsion-semistable quotient R′ of the universal local ring, for an interval determined by the fixed tensor factor. The reduced local deformation ring has dense characteristic-zero semistable points; all of them factor through R′. Thus its whole map factors through R′, and every Artinian specialization has the required torsion property. An ordinary filtration alone does not prove this assertion.
Apply the semistable pseudodeformation universal property to the tensor representation and its fixed polarization. This gives P→R and the two specified O-points (Corollary 4.3).
acceptance: At the automorphic point t the map P → 𝒪 is the composite of R → 𝒪 (from r) with P → R.

sources.match: Shows Artinian lifts tensored with s are torsion semistable and defines the tensor map from the pseudodeformation ring to the deformation ring.

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles data and rings for the tensor product
nodes.statement: A Taylor–Wiles datum of level N for the tensor is (Q, Q̃, (α_v, β_v), (γ_{v,1}, …, γ_{v,r})) with Q split in K, q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N, a factorisation v = ṽṽ^c, (r̄ ⊗ s̄)(Frob_ṽ) having 2r distinct eigenvalues, α_v, β_v the eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_ṽ) and γ_{v,i} those of (s̄ ⊗ r_{X^{−1}Y^{1−r}})(Frob_ṽ). Attached: Δ_Q, with R_Q an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra such that R_Q ⊗_{𝒪[Δ_Q]} 𝒪 ≅ R; P_Q the quotient of the pseudodeformation ring of G_{K,S∪Q} by the Taylor–Wiles conditions (at ṽ ∈ Q̃ the residual characters are α_vγ_{v,i} for i ≤ r and β_vγ_{v,i−r} for i > r), with its 𝒪[Δ′_Q]-structure; and the map P_Q → R_Q extending SP.12/tensor-map.
hypotheses: The 2r distinct eigenvalues exist by the perfect subgroup hypothesis (6) of Theorem 4.1.
N≥1, Q is disjoint from S, and Δ′_Q=Δ_Q^{2r}. At the auxiliary places the decomposition is into ordered lifts of the residual eigencharacters; the lifts may be ramified and encode the diamond action.
proofSteps: As SP.9/symmetric-taylor-wiles-data, with the tensor eigenvalue pattern in place of the symmetric-power monomials; the decomposition into characters by uniqueness for multiplicity-free pseudocharacters.

Prime selection uses the perfect residual subgroup containing a regular semisimple element in hypothesis (6), together with the rank-two residual large-image bound. This is the tensor-specific prime-selection variant requested from GlobalGaloisDeformations G7; characteristic-zero enormousness alone is not this hypothesis.
acceptance: For r = 1 the datum reduces to a rank-two Taylor–Wiles datum with γ_{v,1} a fixed scalar.

nodes.title: Unitary automorphic forms at Taylor–Wiles level for the tensor
nodes.statement: Let G be the definite unitary group over F with G(R) = {g ∈ M_n(𝒪_K ⊗ R) : g = (1 ⊗ c)(g)^{−t}}, H_G(V) the 𝒪-valued forms of level V, V_0 Iwahori at Σ and hyperspecial elsewhere (with σ's ramified places included, E24), V_0(Q) ⊃ V_1(Q; N) with quotient Δ′_Q/(p^N), and maximal ideals m_G, m_{G,Q} (the latter generated by the U_{ϖ_ṽ}^{(i)} minus products of the eigenvalues αγ, βγ, misprinted in the source, E26). (Lemma 4.5) For p = 2 each quadratic χ of F^×\(𝔸_F^∞)^×/det U_1(Q; N) has a unique quadratic θ_χ with θ_χ(z/z^c) = χ∘N_{K/F}(z). (Proposition 4.6) For a datum of level N+c_G, where p^{c_G} kills the p-primary base-level stabilizers: m_G and m_{G,Q} are in the supports; H_G(V_1(Q; N))_{m_{G,Q}} is free over 𝒪[Δ′_Q/(p^N)] with coinvariants H_G(V_0)_{m_G}; and it carries a compatible P_Q-module structure.
hypotheses: Setting of SP.12/tensor-lifting-setup.

N≥1. Order the eigenvalues η=(αγ₁,…,αγ_r,βγ₁,…,βγ_r). At each auxiliary place the maximal ideal contains U^{(i)}−q^{i(1−i)/2}∏_{j=1}^iη_j. In particular for i>r this product is α^rβ^{i−r}(∏_{j=1}^rγ_j)(∏_{j=1}^{i−r}γ_j), with both γ-products present.
proofSteps: The datum at level N+c_G puts the p-primary stabilizer images in V₁(Q;N). Thus the deck group Δ′_Q/(p^N) acts freely on the relevant finite double quotient. Exactness gives group-ring freeness and the trace identifies the coinvariants with H_G(V₀)_{m_G}; triviality of every base-level stabilizer is unnecessary.

Support comes from Labesse descent of the automorphic tensor T. The ordered cumulative products η₁⋯η_i define m_{G,Q}; the multiplicity-free decomposition of the Hecke pseudocharacter gives its P_Q action. For p=2 use Hilbert 90 to construct the unique quadratic θ_χ of Lemma 4.5.
acceptance: For N=1, augmentation from O[Δ′_Q/(p)] recovers H_G(V₀)_{m_G} with its Hecke action.

sources.locator: §4, unitary forms, pp. 31–32; Lemma 4.5, p. 32; Proposition 4.6, p. 33
sources.match: Defines the unitary forms and Taylor–Wiles levels for the tensor, the quadratic twisting characters for p = 2, and proves freeness and the P_Q-module structure.

nodes.title: The tensor image is enormous
nodes.statement: The image of (r ⊗ s)|_{G_K} ⊗ r_{X^{−1}Y^{1−r},ι} restricted to G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})} is enormous in the sense of the parent's §4.1 (Newton–Thorne, JEMS, Definition 2.23).
hypotheses: Hypothesis (8) of Theorem 4.1 (strong irreducibility of r_π ⊗ r_σ) and Hodge–Tate regularity of the tensor (its weights are {0, 1, …, 2r − 1} by (7)).
proofSteps: By Newton–Thorne (JEMS) Lemma 2.28 it suffices that the derived subgroup G^1 of the identity component G^0 of the Zariski closure G of the image of ρ = (r ⊗ s)|_{G_K} ⊗ r_{X^{−1}Y^{1−r},ι} contains regular semisimple elements and acts absolutely irreducibly; G^1 lies in the Zariski closure of ρ(G_{K(ζ_{p^∞})}) (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, characteristic-zero enormous subgroups).
G^0 acts irreducibly because ρ is strongly irreducible, so its centre is scalar and G^0 = G^1 or G^1𝔾_m; hence G^1 acts irreducibly.

At v ∈ S_p the Sen operator lies in Lie G^0 and has n distinct eigenvalues because ρ|_{G_{K_ṽ}} is Hodge–Tate regular (Patrikis Lemmas 2.2.5, 2.2.7); a maximal-torus argument (Borel II.7.1) gives regular semisimple elements in G^0, hence in G^1.
Enormousness is the input to adjoint Selmer vanishing (parent §4.1; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.8) at the automorphic point.
acceptance: A tensor that is not Hodge–Tate regular (σ with weights {0, 1, …, r − 1} instead of {0, 2, …, 2r − 2}) need not have a Sen operator with distinct eigenvalues, and the criterion fails.

sources.match: Shows the image of the tensor representation on the cyclotomic-infinite subgroup is enormous.

nodes.title: Patching for tensor functoriality lifting
nodes.statement: (p > 2, Proposition 4.8) There are W_∞ = 𝒪[[Y_1, …, Y_q, Z_1, …, Z_{4|S∪S_∞|−1}]] and W′_∞ (with n copies of the Y-variables), a W′_∞-algebra P_∞ and a W_∞-algebra R_∞ with P_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ P and R_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ R, a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R_∞ with g = q + |S ∪ S_∞| − 1, patched modules H_{G,∞}, H_{D,∞} finite free over W′_∞, W_∞ specialising to H_G, H_D, and P_∞ → R_∞ compatible with P → R. (p = 2, Proposition 4.9) With q ≥ |S ∪ S_∞| and γ = 2 − |S ∪ S_∞| + q, the same with R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R′_∞ → R_∞ (g = 2q + 1), a free action of Ĝ_m^γ on Sp R′_∞ and an equivariant δ : Sp R′_∞ → Ĝ_m^γ (for the square of the standard action) with δ^{−1}(1) = Sp R_∞, and compatible actions of Ĝ_m^γ[2] lifting to H_{D,∞} and H_{G,∞}.
hypotheses: For all N≥1 use the tensor Taylor–Wiles data selected using hypothesis (6), the perfect residual subgroup, and the rank-two large-image bound. This step does not follow from SP.12/tensor-enormous.
For odd p choose q≥0 with 2q≥|S∪S_∞|. For p=2 choose q≥|S∪S_∞| as in Proposition 4.9.
proofSteps: As SP.9/symmetric-patching-odd and SP.9/symmetric-patching-dyadic, patching the quaternionic modules for r̄ and the unitary modules of SP.12/tensor-unitary-modules simultaneously; the rank 2r of the pseudocharacter side enters only through P, the Taylor–Wiles data and the unitary module.
acceptance: dim W′_∞ − dim W_∞ = (n − 1)q, the extra Y-variables of the rank-n unitary side.

sources.match: Constructs the patched rings and modules for the tensor version, for p odd and p = 2.

nodes.title: Functoriality lifting for a tensor with one factor fixed (Newton–Thorne 2026 Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, r ≥ 1, p any prime, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, π, π′ RAESDC on GL_2(𝔸_F) and σ RAESDC on GL_r(𝔸_F) with (1) π, π′ of weight 0 and non-CM; (2) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}; (3) r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) containing a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), p^a > 5; (4) at each v | p, r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} ordinary (resp. potentially crystalline) iff r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} is, both potentially crystalline if p = 2; (5) at each v ∤ p, π_v a twist of Steinberg iff π′_v is; (6) a perfect subgroup of (r̄_{π,ι} ⊗ r̄_{σ,ι})^{ss}(G_F) containing an element with 2r distinct eigenvalues; (7) HT_τ(r_{σ,ι}) = {0, 2, …, 2r − 2} for every τ; (8) r_{π,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} automorphic and strongly irreducible; (9) r_{π′,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} irreducible. Then r_{π′,ι} ⊗ r_{σ,ι} is automorphic. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.23 (first paragraph); the proof covers σ ramified where π is not after the repair of E24 in SP.12/tensor-lifting-setup.
hypotheses: Hypotheses (1)–(9).
proofSteps: Reduce as in SP.12/tensor-lifting-setup.

Characteristic-zero enormousness and adjoint Selmer vanishing give P_{(𝔭)}=E at the automorphic characteristic-zero prime. The patched specialization then gives regularity of (P_∞)_{𝔭_∞}. Consequently 𝔭_∞ lies on a unique component of Supp H_{G,∞}; no equality of the entire pseudodeformation ring with E is claimed.

For odd p the rank-two patched support is irreducible and H_{D,∞} is faithful, so its image contains the target point on the same unitary component. For p=2 use the torus action on the rank-two local rings of rank n+4|S∪S_∞| and the formal Ĝ_m^γ[2]-torsor of Proposition 4.9: its action is transitive on components and lifts to both patched modules. This yields the same support conclusion.
Hence t′ is automorphic: r_{π′_K} ⊗ r_{σ_K} ⊗ r_Y^{1−r} comes from a RACSDC representation of GL_n(𝔸_K); descend from K to F and by soluble descent.
acceptance: r = 1: classical modularity lifting for weight-zero non-CM Hilbert forms twisted by a character.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1, p. 25; proof and component argument, pp. 34–37
sources.match: States and proves functoriality lifting for r_π ⊗ r_σ with σ fixed, by simultaneous patching of the rank-two deformation ring and the rank-2r pseudodeformation ring and a component argument.

nodes.title: Reciprocity for the two auxiliary splitting conditions
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real and H the ray class field of modulus (8) times all infinite places. (Square generator) If a finite place w of odd residue characteristic splits in H, its prime ideal has a totally positive generator λ_w ∈ 𝒪_F which is a square in F_v^× at every v | 2. (Lemma 5.3) For a finite set S of finite places and finite places v, w ∤ 2 outside S splitting in F(S)H, v splits in F(S ∪ {w}) iff w splits in F(S ∪ {v}), where F(S) is the maximal abelian extension of exponent two unramified outside S (and the infinite places).
hypotheses: F totally real; v, w odd and outside S.
proofSteps: Splitting in H gives a generator λ_w ≡ square at the dyadic places and totally positive (class field theory, ray class group of modulus (8)∞).
F(S ∪ {w}) = F(S)(√λ_w) when w splits in F(S)H (Kummer description after adjoining one ramified place; ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3, exponent-two ramification field).

So the claim is the equality of Hilbert symbols (λ_v, λ_w)_v = (λ_v, λ_w)_w; by the product formula (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 14) it suffices that (λ_v, λ_w)_u = 1 at every other place u: at u | 2∞ because λ_v, λ_w are local squares there, and at odd finite u ≠ v, w because both are units.
acceptance: F = ℚ, S = ∅: H = ℚ(ζ_8), so v, w are primes ≡ 1 mod 8; F(∅) = ℚ and F({w}) = ℚ(√w), and the statement is quadratic reciprocity (v/w) = (w/v) for such primes.

sources.locator: §5.1, the field H and Lemma 5.3 with proof, pp. 38–39
sources.match: Introduces the ray class field of modulus (8)∞, the totally positive dyadic-square generators, and proves the reciprocity of the two auxiliary splitting conditions by the product formula.

nodes.title: Large image at every prime from two tamely dihedral places
nodes.statement: Fix M > 5. Let π be RAESDC on GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight 0 with (1) primes t_1, t_2 > M and places v_1, v_2 of residue characteristics p_1, p_2 > 3, unramified in F, with π_{v_i} tamely dihedral of order t_i and p_1, p_2, t_1, t_2 distinct; (2) with S the finite places v ≠ v_1, v_2 where π is ramified or v is ramified over ℚ, together with the places above 2 and 3, v_1 splits in F(S ∪ {v_2}) and v_2 splits in F(S ∪ {v_1}). Then for every prime p and ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) contains a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) for some p^a > M.
hypotheses: Weight 0 (Fontaine–Laffaille weights {0, 1} at unramified p-adic places).
proofSteps: Away from {p₁,t₁}, the local representation at v₁ is irreducible with a projective element of order t₁>5. Finite projective classification leaves PSL₂(q) or PGL₂(q), or the dihedral case. For the former, t₁ divides q−1 or q+1. At odd residual characteristic q is odd, so q=t₁−1 is impossible and q>M.

At residual characteristic 2 both local places remain available. If q≤M, the two distinct odd primes t₁,t₂>M can divide q−1 or q+1 only by both equalling q+1, a contradiction. Thus q>M here as well. For p∈{p₁,t₁} use v₂; these p are odd.

If the residual representation is induced from K/F, Fontaine–Laffaille and the tame local conditions bound the ramification of K by S∪{v₂}; dyadic places are already in S. The required splitting of v₁ in this exponent-two extension contradicts local irreducibility at v₁. Exchange the two places in the other case.
acceptance: If the splitting hypothesis is removed, a quadratic inducing field can be nonsplit at v₁, for example unramified quadratic locally. Ramification of that quadratic field at v₁ is not forced by odd-order tame inertia.

sources.match: Shows two tamely dihedral places with the reciprocal splitting conditions force large residual image at every prime.

nodes.title: The hypotheses S5-global and S5-local of Newton–Thorne 2026 §5
nodes.statement: S5-global: F totally real, p ≥ 5, 0 < r < p, SP_r, SP_{r+1} and, when r>1, SP_{r−1}, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, and π RAESDC on GL_2(𝔸_F) with (1) det r_{π,ι} = ε^{−1}; (2) weight 0 and π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg for every v | p; (3) a place v_0 with q_{v_0} ≡ −1 mod p and π_{v_0} tamely dihedral of order p; (4) for every prime l and every ι_l, r̄_{π,ι_l}(G_F) containing a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{l^a}) with l^a > max(4r, 5), and r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) containing a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with a > a_0(p); (5) π_v potentially unramified at every finite v ∤ p. S5-local: F, p, r, ι as before, M > p^{a_0(p)}, π with (1)–(3); (4) a place v_1 with q_{v_1} ≡ 1 mod p and π_{v_1} an unramified twist of Steinberg; (5) π_v potentially unramified at every v ∤ pv_1; (6) primes t_1, t_2 > M and places w_1, w_2 of residue characteristics p_1, p_2 > 3 unramified in F, with π_{w_i} tamely dihedral of order t_i and p_1, p_2, t_1, t_2 distinct; (7) with H the ray class field of modulus (8)∞ and S the places v ≠ w_1, w_2 where π is ramified, v is ramified over ℚ or has residue characteristic 2 or 3: w_1 splits in H·F(S) and w_2 splits in H·F(S ∪ {w_1}). φ_p ∈ G_{ℚ_p} denotes an arithmetic Frobenius lift, acting on coefficients.
hypotheses: SP_m is the parent's statement (node ML.3/sp-statement).
proofSteps: By SP.13/ray-class-reciprocity, (7) implies the symmetric splitting condition of SP.13/dihedral-large-image, so S5-local implies the global large-image condition (4) of S5-global with M in place of max(4r, 5).
acceptance: For r=1 the tensor is a coefficient conjugate of π. This branch is direct and invokes no SP₀; SP₁ and SP₂ are the trivial character and the given rank-two form, respectively.

nodes.title: The companions σ, σ′ and the auxiliary prime t
nodes.statement: (Lemma 5.6) Under S5-global there is a RAESDC σ on GL_2(𝔸_F) with the properties of SP.11/ordinary-companion and r_{π,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ,ι} automorphic. (Lemma 5.7) Let K_π be the coefficient field of π, K̃_π its Galois closure, Γ_π = Gal(K̃_π/ℚ), B ≥ 1 with K_π ramified only at primes < B, and φ = ιφ_pι^{−1}. There are a prime t, ι_t and a RAESDC σ′ with: t > max(5, 4r + 2, B), t unramified in F and all three forms unramified above t; the residual tensors of π and φπ with Sym^{r−1}σ at t absolutely irreducible over F(ζ_t) (the cyclotomic restriction needed by BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1, with the commutator argument below supplying the omitted step E25); r̄_{σ,ι_t} ≅ r̄_{σ′,ι_t} and σ′_{v_0} an unramified Steinberg twist; r_π ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ′} automorphic, and r_{φπ} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_σ automorphic iff r_{φπ} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ′} is; for every l < B and ι_l, r̄_{σ′,ι_l} has image containing SL_2(𝔽_{l^a}) with l^a > max(4r, 5) and projective fixed field meeting that of γπ in degree at most 2 over F for every γ ∈ Γ_π; choose the new auxiliary place v₁ away from p,t and all prescribed bad places, so both π and σ are unramified there (repair E28).
hypotheses: S5-global, with the r=1 case direct. Choose t also outside the exceptional-image sets of π, φπ and σ, and unramified in the coefficient fields and F.
proofSteps: For r>1 obtain σ from Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2. Choose t as in Lemma 5.7. If the two residual projective fields coincided, finite projective classification would identify the adjoint representations up to coefficient Frobenius. Their Fontaine–Laffaille weights {−1,0,1} and {−2,0,2}, at an unramified t>5, exclude this. Apply the same argument to φπ.

The projective fields therefore meet in at most a quadratic extension. Goursat gives PSL₂(q_π)×PSL₂(q_σ) in the joint projective image. Taking commutators and lifting the central scalar kernels gives SL₂(q_π)×SL₂(q_σ) in the joint linear image. One can check the last step inside SL₂×SL₂: a subgroup surjecting onto the full projective product, multiplied by the center, is the whole perfect product, and hence is itself the whole product.

G_{F(ζ_t)} is normal with abelian quotient in G_F. Its joint image contains the commutator subgroup and thus the perfect SL₂×SL₂ product just obtained. On this product Std⊗Sym^{r−1} is absolutely irreducible, since r<t≤q_σ. This proves the needed cyclotomic irreducibility for both π and φπ, not just irreducibility over F. No extra disjointness assumption is added.

Choose the Chebotarev place v₁ outside the finite set over p,t and the ramification of π,σ and the coefficient conjugates. The original splitting, q_{v₁}≡−1 mod t and Frobenius-ratio conditions still have positive density. Construct σ′ with order-t dihedral type at v₁ and the original local connections elsewhere. At small l, its projective field differs from each γπ field by ramification at v₁; classification gives projective field size q≥t−1>4r, which suffices.

The potentially diagonalizable automorphy-lifting theorem now applies over F(ζ_t), giving the two automorphy comparisons in Lemma 5.7. The constructions are unchanged for r=1 except that the tensor and its irreducibility reduce to the first factor.
acceptance: For K_π = ℚ (rational coefficients) Γ_π is trivial and B = 1, so the conditions at small primes are vacuous.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.6, p. 40; Lemma 5.7 and proof, pp. 40–42
sources.match: Produces the companion σ with automorphic untwisted tensor, and an auxiliary prime t with a second companion σ′ separating the coefficient conjugates.

nodes.title: Propagation over the Galois group of the coefficient field
nodes.statement: Under S5-global with σ, σ′, B, K̃_π, Γ_π from SP.13/tensor-companions: (Lemma 5.8) for γ ∈ Γ_π, a finite place w | l of K̃_π and δ in the inertia group I_{w/l}, if r_{γπ,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ′,ι} is automorphic then so is r_{δγπ,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ′,ι} (for δ ≠ 1 only l < B occurs; the second factor is fixed); hence r_{γπ,ι} ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ′,ι} is automorphic for every γ ∈ Γ_π, since Γ_π is generated by inertia subgroups (ℚ has no nontrivial everywhere unramified extension); and taking γ = φ, with the σ′-to-σ equivalence of Lemma 5.7 and coefficient conjugation, there is an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(𝔸_F) with r_{Π,ι} ≅ φ_p(r_{π,ι}) ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_{σ,ι}.
hypotheses: The checks in the proof of Lemma 5.8 are for ι_l where the source prints ι (E2); the application of Theorem 4.1 there has σ = Sym^{r−1}σ′ Steinberg at v_0 while γπ is unramified there after base change, the case covered after the repair of E24 (SP.12/tensor-lifting-setup).
proofSteps: Lemma 5.8: change the comparison embedding to one inducing w; δ acts trivially on the residue field, so r̄_{δγπ} ≅ r̄_{γπ} at the prime above l; apply SP.12/tensor-functoriality-lifting with σ = Sym^{r−1}σ′, and return to ι (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.6, coefficient conjugation and independence of the embedding). Check all nine hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 at this l: the coefficient inertia gives the residual congruence; the different weights give regularity; the two projective fields give a perfect product. For its regular semisimple element choose x with order>2r−2 and choose y avoiding the at most 2r−1 forbidden ratios ±x^i; q>4r permits this. Ordinarity and Steinberg status at the other places are preserved by coefficient conjugation. The tensor-factor automorphy at one embedding transfers to the comparison embedding by AG2.6.
Inertia generation of Γ_π (Minkowski: ℚ has no unramified extensions).
The final step uses SP.13/tensor-companions and the regularity of the different-weight companion σ.
acceptance: If K_π = ℚ, Γ_π is trivial and the propagation is empty; φ acts trivially and the conclusion is the untwisted tensor.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.8 and proof, pp. 42–43; completion of Theorem 5.5, pp. 42–44
sources.match: Propagates automorphy of the tensor through inertia elements of the coefficient field's Galois group, and deduces automorphy of the Frobenius-twisted companion tensor.

nodes.title: A residual witness for φ_p r̄ ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄ under global image hypotheses (Newton–Thorne 2026 Theorem 5.5)
nodes.statement: Under S5-global (with SP_r, SP_{r+1} and SP_{r−1} when r>1) there is an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(𝔸_F) with r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ φ_p(r̄_{π,ι}) ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄_{π,ι}. The statement is residual: it does not identify r_{Π,ι} with a Frobenius twist of a characteristic-zero tensor of π with itself.
hypotheses: S5-global.
proofSteps: SP.13/coefficient-conjugate-propagation gives Π with r_Π ≅ φ_p(r_π) ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r_σ.
Reduce: r̄_σ^{ss} ≅ r̄_π^{ss} (SP.11/ordinary-companion), so r̄_Π ≅ φ_p(r̄_π) ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄_π; ordinarity from that of π and σ.
acceptance: For r = 1 the conclusion is a residual witness for φ_p r̄, given by the coefficient conjugate of π.

sources.match: Produces an ordinary RAESDC representation of GL_{2r} whose residual representation is the coefficient-Frobenius twisted tensor of r̄ with Sym^{r−1}r̄.

nodes.title: A residual witness retaining a Steinberg place (Newton–Thorne 2026 Theorem 5.9)
nodes.statement: Under S5-local (with SP_r, SP_{r+1} and SP_{r−1} when r>1) the residual image of r̄_{π,ι} contains SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with p^a > M, and there is an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(𝔸_F) with r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ φ_p(r̄_{π,ι}) ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄_{π,ι}; π remains Steinberg at v₁ for the later level raising, while no Steinberg condition at v₁ is asserted for this residual witness Π. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.23 (second paragraph).
hypotheses: S5-local.
proofSteps: Large image at every prime from SP.13/dihedral-large-image via SP.13/ray-class-reciprocity.

Remove the extra Steinberg place: a congruent ι-ordinary RAESDC π′ of weight 0, determinant ε^{−1}, Steinberg at all p-adic places, with r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} for v ∤ pv_1 and π′_{v_1} a principal series i(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2) with (χ_1/χ_2)|_{𝒪^×} of order p (residually the same inertial semisimplification as Steinberg since q_{v_1} ≡ 1 mod p), preserving the dihedral types at w_1, w_2 (Ihara-avoidance local conditions; LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2).
π′ satisfies S5-global; SP.13/residual-twisted-tensor-global gives the witness for π′, hence for π (same residual representation).
acceptance: The witness is residual only, as in Theorem 5.5.

sources.match: Deduces from Theorem 5.5 the residual twisted tensor witness under the local hypotheses, replacing the Steinberg place by a congruent principal series.

nodes.title: Ordinary replacement with a Frobenius-tensor residual witness (Newton–Thorne 2026 Corollary 6.2)
nodes.statement: For F totally real, π non-CM RAESDC on GL_2(𝔸_F), p ≥ 5, 0 < r < p and SP_r, SP_{r+1} and SP_{r−1} when r>1, there are a soluble totally real E/F, ι and RAESDC π′ over E with: Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π,ι} automorphic iff Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π′,ι} is; π′ of weight zero and an unramified Steinberg twist at every p-adic place of E (the source prints 'of F', E5); r̄_{π′,ι} with image containing SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), a > a_0(p); an unramified Steinberg twist at some v_1 ∤ p; and an ι-ordinary RAESDC representation of GL_{2r}(𝔸_E) whose residual representation is φ_p(r̄_{π′,ι}) ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄_{π′,ι}. The intermediate claim of the proof of Proposition 6.1 is part of this node: there are ι, a soluble totally real E/F and RAESDC π_0 over E of weight 0, Steinberg at all v | p, det r_{π_0} = ε^{−1}, residual image containing SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with a > a_0(p), Steinberg at some v_1 ∤ p with q_{v_1} ≡ 1 mod p, potentially unramified away from pv_1, and Sym^{p+r−1}r_π automorphic iff Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π_0} is.
hypotheses: Proposition 6.1 (the favourable local replacement with all eight conditions) is stated in the parent's §4.22 (node ML.3/clozel-thorne-reductions); this node uses it.
proofSteps: Intermediate claim: a prime q from Dimitrov's Proposition 3.8; an everywhere unramified finite-order character χ of G_E with χ² det r_{π,ι_q} = ε^{−1} (the obstruction to a square root of the totally even character ε det r_{π,ι_q} is a 2-torsion class in Br(F), killed by local conditions on E); π_a from Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty Theorem 6.1.9; a prime t prime to the conductor of π_a (E8) with tamely dihedral level raising.
Proposition 6.1 (parent §4.22) then gives π′ with conditions (1)–(8), hence S5-local; SP.13/residual-twisted-tensor-local gives the residual witness.
acceptance: For r = 1 the residual witness is φ_p r̄_{π′}, given by a coefficient conjugate.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 6.1, intermediate claim, pp. 46–48; Corollary 6.2, p. 49
sources.match: Proves the intermediate replacement step of Proposition 6.1 and deduces Corollary 6.2: an ordinary replacement over a soluble extension with a residual witness for the twisted tensor.

nodes.title: Symmetric-power lifting from two ordinary residual blocks (Newton–Thorne 2026 Proposition 6.3; Thorne 2024 Proposition 7.4)
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p ≥ 5, 0 < r < p and π RAESDC on GL_2(𝔸_F), ι-ordinary for some ι with residual image containing SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), a > a_0(p), of weight zero, with an unramified Steinberg twist at a place v_1 ∤ p. Suppose there are ι-ordinary RAESDC π_1 on GL_{p−r}(𝔸_F) and π_2 on GL_{2r}(𝔸_F) with residual representations Sym^{p−r−1}r̄_{π,ι} and φ_p(r̄_{π,ι}) ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄_{π,ι}. Then there is an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{p+r}(𝔸_F) with r_{Π,ι} ≅ Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π,ι}. These residual witnesses replace the hypotheses of Thorne 2024 Proposition 7.4 that Sym^{r−1}r_π and Sym^{p−r−1}r_π are automorphic and that tensor functoriality TP_r holds.
hypotheses: The residual decomposition (Sym^{p+r−1}r̄)^{ss} ≅ (φ_p r̄ ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄) ⊕ (det r̄)^r ⊗ Sym^{p−r−1}r̄ for 0 < r < p (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, mod-p Clebsch–Gordan decompositions (b)).

In the residually reducible inputs, primitive means weakly primitive in the source sense, tested over the algebraic closure of the residual field. Choose a common finite splitting field for every subgroup of the residual image before fixing integral coefficient rings. The PL.6 normalization coefficient condition then holds; no implication from arbitrary finite-field primitivity to geometric primitivity is assumed.
proofSteps: Pass to a CM quadratic extension with the conditions of Thorne's Proposition 7.4 (soluble base change).

Twist the witnesses into conjugate self-dual cuspidal σ_1, σ_2 with σ_2 Steinberg at the place above v_1 (Khare–Wintenberger method, Thorne 2012 Theorems 9.1, 10.2), so Σ = σ_1 ⊞ σ_2 is regular algebraic, ι-ordinary of weight 0 and r̄_Σ ≅ (Sym^{p+r−1}r̄)^{ss}.

SP.6/thorne-steinberg-level-raising gives a cuspidal ι-ordinary Π_0 Steinberg at the place above v_1 with the same residual representation (hypothesis (3) of Theorem 6.11 from an element diag(t, t^{−1}) with 1, t², …, t^{2(p+r−1)} distinct, which exists since a ≥ 3).
Thorne 2024 Theorem 7.5 (residually reducible ordinary lifting with a Steinberg place; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.7) shows Sym^{p+r−1}r_π automorphic; descend.
acceptance: For p = 5, r = 1: blocks Sym³r̄ (rank 4) and φ_5 r̄ (rank 2), giving Sym^5 (rank 6).

sources.match: Deduces automorphy of Sym^{p+r−1} from ordinary residual witnesses for the two blocks, via Thorne 2024 Proposition 7.4 and Theorem 7.5 without TP_r.

sources.locator: Proposition 7.4 and proof, pp. 43–44; Theorem 7.5, p. 44
sources.match: Proves residual automorphy and level raising for Sym^{p+r−1} from the two blocks via Theorem 6.11, and states the strengthened residually reducible lifting theorem.

nodes.title: Thorne's induction step and the small cases (Thorne 2024 Theorems 7.1, 7.6, Corollary 7.2)
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and 0 < r < p. (Theorem 7.6) Assume SP_{p−r}, SP_r and TP_r (tensor functoriality GL_2 × GL_r → GL_{2r} for RAECSDC representations over CM fields with irreducible Hodge–Tate regular tensor). If (π, χ) is RAESDC on GL_2(𝔸_{F⁺}), ι-ordinary with residual image containing SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) for some a > a_0(p), of weight 0, with an unramified Steinberg twist at some v_0 ∤ p, then Sym^{p+r−1}π exists as an ι-ordinary cuspidal RAESDC Π. (Theorem 7.1) Hence SP_{p−r} + SP_r + TP_r ⇒ SP_{p+r}. (Corollary 7.2) SP_n holds for n = 1, …, 10 and for even n = 12, …, 26; and TP_r for all r implies SP_n for all n.
hypotheses: TP_r is known for r = 1, 2, 3 (Ramakrishnan, Kim–Shahidi), and SP_n for n ≤ 5 (parent ML.3/low-rank-symmetric-powers).
proofSteps: Theorem 7.6 from Thorne's Proposition 7.4 (the TP_r version of SP.13/two-block-symmetric-lifting) and Theorem 7.5 after soluble base change.

Theorem 7.1 from Theorem 7.6 by the reductions of Clozel–Thorne (parent ML.3/clozel-thorne-reductions, which also records Thorne 2024 Theorem 8.1 and Proposition 8.3 for the passage from essentially square-integrable to regular algebraic π).
Corollary 7.2(1) from TP_1, TP_2, TP_3: SP_{p−1} ⇒ SP_{p+1}, SP_{p−2} ⇒ SP_{p+2}, SP_{p−3} ⇒ SP_{p+3} for p = 5, …, 23; (2) by Bertrand's postulate as in SP.13/sp-induction.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.1, Corollary 7.2 and Lemma 7.3, p. 42; Theorem 7.6, p. 45; proofs, pp. 42–47
sources.match: Proves the implication SP_{p−r} + SP_r + TP_r ⇒ SP_{p+r}, the unconditional small cases and the conditional general case.

nodes.title: The induction proving SP_n for all n (Newton–Thorne 2026 Theorem 6.4)
nodes.statement: SP_n holds for every n ≥ 1: for every totally real F and every non-CM RAESDC π on GL_2(𝔸_F), there is a RAESDC Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) with r_{Π,ι} ≅ Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} for every ι. This proves the statement the parent records in §4.30 (node ML.3/all-regular-symmetric-powers), and, through the parent's §§4.35–4.36, Newton–Thorne 2026 Theorem A.
hypotheses: Induction on n, with base cases n ≤ 5 (parent ML.3/low-rank-symmetric-powers).
proofSteps: For n>5 choose a prime p with n/2<p<n and write n=p+r with 0<r<p. The positive indices r,r+1,p−r are below n, and so is r−1 when r>1. Apply induction at these indices. When r=1 use the direct coefficient-conjugate tensor branch; SP₀ is neither defined nor needed.
By the parent's one-prime criterion (§4.15) it suffices to prove automorphy of Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π,ι} for one ι.
SP.13/ordinary-replacement gives π′ over a soluble E with the residual witness for φ_p r̄ ⊗ Sym^{r−1}r̄; SP_{p−r} gives a witness for Sym^{p−r−1}r̄ (ordinary by the Steinberg-at-p condition).
SP.13/two-block-symmetric-lifting gives Sym^{p+r−1}r_{π′} automorphic, hence Sym^{p+r−1}r_π by the equivalence of Corollary 6.2.
acceptance: n=6: choose p=5,r=1. The direct rank-one tensor branch needs SP₁,SP₂ and SP₄, with no SP₀.
n=7: choose p=5,r=2. The induction uses SP₁,SP₂,SP₃ and SP₃.
n=12: choose p=7,r=5. The induction uses SP₄,SP₅,SP₆ and SP₂.

sources.match: Proves SP_n for all n by Bertrand's postulate and induction, from Corollary 6.2 and Proposition 6.3.

gaps.title: G1. Deligne–Lusztig theory and the modular representation theory of U_3(𝔽_q) have no owner
gaps.detail: Newton–Thorne I §1.8 uses Deligne–Lusztig induction for the anisotropic tori of U_3 and GL_3, Lusztig's cuspidal unipotent representation, Dudas–Malle's modular irreducibility, Geck's decomposition numbers and Kazhdan–Varshavsky's transfer of Deligne–Lusztig functions. No atlas roadmap plans these, and TauCetiRoadmap CharacterTheory Layer 9 treats GL_2(𝔽_q) only. The SP.4 nodes state exactly the special cases used and are cited inputs until an owner exists (request at CharacterTheory Layer 9 for a Part II).

gaps.title: G2. The odd case of Newton–Thorne I Theorem 7.1 (Proposition 7.4) has a gap (E21)
gaps.detail: In NTI arXiv v3 Proposition 7.4, p.87, the proposed GL₂ block fails conjugate self-duality by δ_{K/ℚ}|_{G_{F₀}}, so its use of Theorem 4.1 is unsupported (atlas PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21/E21, scoped here to v3). The rank-one extension repairs the GL₁ range but does not repair this GL₂ failure, even for n=3. Within the CM seed construction only the powers-of-two route is independent of it. Low-rank symmetric-power endpoint theorems for n≤5 do not provide all the residual, field and Steinberg data of Theorem 7.1. Supply a conjugate-self-dual GL₂ block with the required residual representation and types, or a different construction of that seed. The separate SP.13 method proves the endpoint without repairing this intermediate seed route.

gaps.title: G3. Thorne 2024 §§3–5 (p-adic automorphic forms and the Drinfeld half-space) have no owner
gaps.detail: Thorne arXiv v2 Theorem 6.11 (pp.39–41) uses Theorem 3.4 (Steinberg detection), Theorem 4.5 (even-multiplicity weights), Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 6.3/Proposition 6.5 on p-adic automorphic forms. The concentration statement is for the Hecke-localized derived tensor RΓ_c(Ω^{n−1},k) ⊗^L_{k[GL_n(F_{w₀})⁰]} A_m under residual genericity, concentrated in degree n−1. Bare compactly supported Drinfeld cohomology is not asserted to be concentrated there. These inputs still need an owner; R4 proposes the boundary.

gaps.title: G4. Mœglin's explicit description of tempered packets of p-adic unitary groups
gaps.detail: ML.4 and ET.7a provide classification and endoscopic comparison, but not the required explicit Mœglin Jacquet/socle calculation (2007 Lemme 5.4, Théorème 5.7 and Proposition 5.5, as used by CTIII §§3.3–3.5, pp.21–27). In particular the uniqueness assertion after CTIII (3.9), p.26, cannot simply be repeated: Y is already a submodule with the same exponent. A proof must count the full socle and isolate the other constituent before assigning the Z/W sign. The packet retains that explicit calculation as a proof boundary rather than calling the repair immediate.

gaps.title: G5. GL_2 inputs of Newton–Thorne I §7 and Clozel–Thorne III §6
gaps.detail: Diamond 1989 Corollary 6.9 (level raising) is owned by SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2 (Diamond's level-raising criterion). Diamond–Taylor 1994 Theorem A (prescribed supercuspidal or Steinberg components at non-optimal level), Edixhoven 1992 Theorem 2.6 (ordinarity of forms with reducible residual representation in low weight) and Clozel–Thorne II (Annals 2015) Proposition 3.10 with the reductions of its §6 have no atlas owner; they are cited inputs.

gaps.title: G7. Inherited and requested supplier extensions for finiteness and patching
gaps.detail: The Maire antiunit rank input is a source-check boundary in ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3. PL.7/auxiliary-place-ant-finiteness records a nonscalar unobstructed local-ring and Hecke-level comparison gap; NT26 needs its geometric weak-primitive variant. The exact BBM finite-flat lattice comparison, perfect-subgroup tensor Taylor–Wiles prime selection, and formal torus invariant contract are requested above, beyond what the cited R07.4, G7 residual-enormous and R03.5 statements currently provide. PL.7 sum-of-characters finiteness also inherits its separately recorded rank-one ordinary-finiteness boundary. These are imported proof obligations, not locally established results. Geometric primitivity and the initial subgroup-splitting coefficient convention discharge the separate PL.6 finite-field normalization concern for these applications; arbitrary finite-field primitivity alone would not.

restructure.detail: The design brief carried ten continuations of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions in three independent directions: (a) the proof of symmetric power functoriality (Newton–Thorne I, II and 2026, Clozel–Thorne III, Thorne 2024; routes SymmetricPowersByAnalyticContinuation, SymmetricPowersByUnitaryLevelRaising, SymmetricPowerAutomorphyLifting, SymmetricPowersByTensorFunctorialityLifting); (b) level-one change of weight and cuspidal cohomology of GL_n(ℤ) (Boxer–Calegari–Gee 2025; route LevelOneCuspidalCohomologyGLn, 39 items), which consumes the endpoints of (a) but uses a different method (Bellovin–Gee deformation rings, Harris's tensor product trick, relative Lie algebra cohomology); (c) the explicit local theory and Galois representations of GSp_4 (BCGP 2018 and 2025; route GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations, 30 items), unrelated to (a).

restructure.detail: Gap G1: Deligne–Lusztig induction and the modular representation theory of finite unitary groups are needed here and have no owner.
restructure.proposal: A Part II of RepresentationTheory/CharacterTheory (Deligne–Lusztig induction for finite reductive groups, Lusztig's cuspidal unipotent characters, Brauer characters in non-defining characteristic) should own them; SP.4/depth-zero-cuspidals, SP.4/level-raising-types and SP.4/type-transfer then import it and keep only the U_3 and GL_3 special cases with their p-adic consequences.

upstreamNotes.note: The parent PR #1180 §4.9/§4.12 uses the NTI §7 seed method. Its odd-rank GL₂ block fails conjugate self-duality in the arXiv v3 proof (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21/E21). Even n=3 is not repaired by extending the GL₁ range: only the powers-of-two seed construction avoids that failure. Low-rank endpoint functoriality is separately known for n≤5 but does not produce all Theorem 7.1 seed data. The parent can identify §4.30/§4.35 (the NT26 method) as a separate route to the endpoint over ℚ, while keeping the seed-method boundary explicit.

TauCetiRoadmap PR #1180 §4.23 states Newton–Thorne 2026 Theorem 4.1 as printed. Its printed proof takes S = S_p ∪ Σ with Σ the ramification of π only, which does not cover the application in Lemma 5.8, where σ = Sym^{r−1}σ′ is ramified where π is not (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26/E24). The repair (add σ's ramified places to S with unramified local conditions) is planned in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensionsPartII SP.12/tensor-lifting-setup; the package statement is unaffected.
